title: Buccaneers' undrafted rookie QB Jalon Daniels impresses in preseason debut
summary: Buccaneers undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels is fourth on the depth chart, but he looked in his preseason debut like he might have an NFL future.
full_text: ' Buccaneers undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels is fourth on the depth chart, but he looked in his preseason debut like he might have an NFL future. Daniels played the second half on Friday night and completed 10 of 15 passes for 111 yards, and also ran for a touchdown. Third-string quarterback Connor Bazelak started for the Buccaneers on a night when starter Baker Mayfield and backup Jake Browning were both off, but Daniels looked better than Bazelak, and Bucs coach Todd Bowles praised Daniels after the game. "I thought he was very poised," Bowles said. "He went in relaxed. We knew he could make off-schedule plays out of the pocket, but he played very confidently in the pocket. He made the right reads. He zipped some throws in there. I thought he played very well." Daniels spent six years at Kansas and developed a reputation as a quarterback who made plays with his legs as much as his arm, but Bowles said after the preseason opener that he appreciated Daniels trying to work within the Buccaneers' offensive system rather than rely on his running. "He took what they gave him," Bowles said. "He didn't try to get out of there too fast and he was calm under pressure, and he let the system work for him as opposed to just trying to make a play. He did some very good things tonight from a poise standpoint." Daniels said he's been hard at work on learning to play in an NFL system, rather than the more improvisational style he had in college. "We've worked on a lot of different things to get me out of certain habits I had in college," Daniels said. "I have a better understanding of it than when I first got here." He put that on display in his preseason debut.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Tua Tagovailoa: It starts with me, my play in preseason opener was not up to standard
summary: The Falcons' quarterback went 3-for-5 for 22 yards in Friday night's preseason game.
full_text: Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa said after Friday night's preseason opener that he was not good enough. "Definitely not up to standard, not even up to par. Start with the first drive, second play, just being able to catch the snap. Little things like that," Tagovailoa said. "What we put out there is not a reflection of the hard work that we've put in the first two weeks of training camp, and it does no justice to the work our coaches have implemented. It starts with me. I've got to be better with that." Tagovailoa completed three of his five passes, for 22 yards. The Falcons punted on both of his possessions. "It starts with me," Tagovailoa said. "I've got to be better. That's it. . . . I've got to be better for our guys." Tagovailoa said he hopes he will play in the remaining two preseason games so that he can get more work in live action on his new team. If Friday night's game is any indication, the Falcons need that work.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Nazeeh Johnson says his PED suspension is for taking a fertility medication
summary: Titans cornerback Nazeeh Johnson, who has been suspended for the first six games of the season for violating the NFL policy on performance-enhancing substances, says his violation came from his and his wife's efforts to conceive a child.
full_text: Titans cornerback Nazeeh Johnson, who has been suspended for the first six games of the season for violating the NFL policy on performance-enhancing substances, says his violation came from his and his wife's efforts to conceive a child. Johnson released a statement saying that he took a fertility medication without knowing that it was on the league's list of banned substances. “My wife and I were trying to conceive a child," Johnson wrote. "We found out that I was infertile, and I took a fertility medication that was helping me try to conceive a baby. I was not aware that there was a substance in the medication that was on the banned list, and I tested positive for a PED. Lesson to all NFL players and new players coming into the league: do not put anything in your body without following the process and getting approval beforehand. We lost our baby a few weeks ago, and this has been an incredibly difficult time for my wife and me. Fortunately, we have nine good eggs left, so we’re holding on to hope that we’ll be able to grow our family.” Some fertility medications are considered banned performance-enhancing substances, although athletes can apply for therapeutic use exemptions if they are going to take the medication under a doctor's supervision. Johnson apparently didn't apply for the therapeutic use exemption because he didn't realize the medication was on the list of banned substances, and that will cost him six games. Because NFL suspensions are unpaid, Johnson will lose one-third of his salary this season, a little over $350,000.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Sean Payton takes shot at light turnout in Atlanta
summary: Broncos coach Sean Payton has a history with Atlanta, dating back to the intense rivalry between the Saints (whom he coached from 2006 through 2021) and the Falcons.
full_text: Broncos coach Sean Payton has a history with Atlanta, dating back to the intense rivalry between the Saints (whom he coached from 2006 through 2021) and the Falcons. Payton's current team was back in Georgia tonight for a preseason game. And Payton couldn't resist making a crack about the crowd in Atlanta, or the lack of one. "There's a lot of people dressed up as empty seats today ," Payton said at a halftime interview, via Awful Announcing . The official game book for the Broncos-Falcons contest lists attendance at 68,183. That may have been the tickets sold, not the tickets used. Whether the seats will be filled during the Falcons' regular-season home games depends on whether the team performs better than it did on Friday night. Preseason or not, the Falcons trailed 24-0 at the half. The final score was 27-7. The Falcons have reason for optimism. They finished in a three-way tie for the NFC South crown. If they can get something/anything out of the quarterback position, they could win the division in 2026. They'll need to win early in the season to get the fans on board. Three of the first four games are on the road, and three of the first four teams they play made it to the playoffs in 2025.
author: Mike Florio

title: Steelers, DT Keeanu Benton agree to four-year extension
summary: The Steelers and defensive tackle Keeanu Benton have agreed to a long-term extension.
full_text: The Steelers and defensive tackle Keeanu Benton have agreed to a long-term extension. Benton will sign a four-year, $72 million deal, Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports. The $18 million per season annual average will make Benton the highest-paid defensive lineman in Steelers history. Benton, 25, was entering the final year of his rookie deal, due to make $1.750 million this season. The Steelers selected him in the second round in 2023, and he has played all 51 possible games, while starting 40. Benton has totaled 123 tackles, nine tackles for loss, 7.5 sacks, 28 quarterback hits and an interception.
author: Charean Williams

title: Cardinals rookie OL Chase Bisontis tears MCL
summary: Cardinals second-round offensive guard Chase Bisontis will miss most, or possibly all, of his rookie season.
full_text: Cardinals second-round offensive guard Chase Bisontis will miss most, or possibly all, of his rookie season. NFL Media reports that an MRI revealed a torn MCL for Bisontis, which will require surgery. The Cardinals listed Bisontis as the second-team right guard, but he was competing with Isaiah Adams for the starting job. A Raiders defensive lineman fell into the side of Bisontis' left knee in the third quarter on Thursday night, and he was carted to the training room. The Cardinals have not had good luck with rookie offensive linemen in the preseason. Last year, sixth-round pick Hayden Conner missed most of the regular season after he was injured in the preseason. In 2024, fifth-round pick Christian Jones missed most of the regular season after he was injured in the preseason. In 2023, fourth-round pick Jon Gaines missed his entire rookie season with a preseason injury.
author: Charean Williams

title: Two drives, two punts for Tua Tagovailoa in Falcons debut
summary: Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa made his preseason debut with the Falcons on Friday night against the Broncos.
full_text: Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa made his preseason debut with the Falcons on Friday night against the Broncos. In two drives led by Tua, the Falcons punted twice. The first was a three-and-out effort, netting four yards. The second saw the Falcons gain a first down and advance from their own 15 to their own 32 before punting again. Before exiting for Cooper Rush, Tua completed three of five passes for 22 yards and a passer rating of 70.4. He also fumbled a shotgun snap before falling on it. Tagovailoa is currently listed as the first-string quarterback. Michael Penix Jr. doesn't have a formal spot on the depth chart, as he recovers from a torn ACL suffered last season. Penix has yet to be cleared for team activities. The Falcons open the regular season with a September 13 visit to the Steelers. Last year, a Dolphins loss in Week 15 at Pittsburgh triggered Tua's benching by the Dolphins — setting the stage for his offseason exit and the Dolphins paying him more than $50 million to play for the Falcons.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cade Klubnik plays two series, leads Jets to 10 points
summary: The Jets made a late change at quarterback on Friday and rookie Cade Klubnik got the start against the Buccaneers as a result.
full_text: The Jets made a late change at quarterback on Friday and rookie Cade Klubnik got the start against the Buccaneers as a result. Klubnik opened his first NFL appearance with a short pass to tight end Mason Taylor that turned into a 12-yard gain. The pair hooked up again for seven yards and Klubnik then found wideout Garrett Wilson twice for 32 yards. Wilson made an impressive leaping grab in traffic for a 21-yard gain on the first completion. The Jets settled for a field goal on that drive and Klubnik let running back Braelon Allen do the heavy lifting on the next drive. Allen ran for a 31-yard touchdown on Klubnik's final play of the night. Klubnik finished 5-of-7 for 56 yards. Geno Smith was expected to start the game, but the Jets scratched him just before kickoff with what head coach Aaron Glenn called ankle soreness on the CBS broadcast. Glenn said the team does not believe it is a serious issue.
author: Josh Alper

title: Michael Holley is fine after fainting on-air during PFT Live
summary: Friday's edition of PFT Live included a moment that was unprecedented in the 15-year history of the show.
full_text: '' Friday's edition of PFT Live included a moment that was unprecedented in the 15-year history of the show. Co-host Michael Holley fainted on live TV. Others have written about the incident; it makes sense for us to address it here. Michael, who has been part of the show for the past two years, became overheated during the two-hour program. He hadn't had anything to eat or drink before the show began at 7:00 a.m. ET on Peacock, NBCSN, and SiriusXM 85. And, as he later told me, his studio is very warm. It happened in the final 30 minutes of the program. Earlier in the show, Michael's audio in his earpiece had cut out, and I noticed him bending over to try to get it working again. As he became ill, I was looking at the camera, which sits above the monitor that returns the live feed of the show. I noticed Michael moving. I thought that he had again lost his audio. When he slumped to the right and fell out of the view of the screen, I knew something was wrong. We went straight to a commercial break and immediately commenced an effort to contact Michael's wife. Within a minute or so (which seemed a lot longer than that), Michael was moving. He later confirmed that he was fine. Except for the five stitches he needed in his knee, which he cut when he fell. Many who witnessed the incident as it happened expressed concern for Michael, and we appreciate that. Some posted the clip on social media; we exercised our prerogative to have the video removed. We also decided not to re-air the show on Peacock or NBCSN. It was not televised in its usual spot on Sky Sports. Several clips from Friday's show were posted on YouTube. The lesson learned was a simple one — the control room needs to have phone numbers for family members who can be immediately contacted if a co-host who is contributing from home has a sudden health issue. Two years ago, I thought I might be having a heart attack during a live episode; at the time, I didn't consider that it would make sense for the folks running the show to have my wife's number at their fingertips. Moving forward, we'll have emergency contact information for all co-hosts who appear from home instantly available. The best news by far is that Michael is fine, but for the five stitches. It was a scary moment, one of the realities of two hours of live TV. Again, we appreciate the concern expressed by those who saw it happen. Michael will be back for his next scheduled appearance.
author: Mike Florio

title: Malik Willis, De'Von Achane play one series, score TD
summary: Malik Willis made his Miami debut in the team's first preseason game.
full_text: Malik Willis made his Miami debut in the team's first preseason game. The Dolphins starting quarterback played one series, and that was all he needed. The Dolphins went 93 yards on 14 plays, with De'Von Achane scoring on a 1-yard run for a 7-0 lead over the Commanders. Willis went 4-of-5 for 43 yards, and Achane ran for 39 yards on seven carries. The Dolphins signed Willis to a three-year, $67.5 million deal in free agency before signing Achane to a four-year, $64 million extension. The two players are cornerstones in the Dolphins' rebuild.
author: Charean Williams

title: Marcus Mariota injured in first quarter, heads to locker room
summary: Marcus Mariota got the start at quarterback for the Commanders on Friday night, but his night came to an early end.
full_text: Marcus Mariota got the start at quarterback for the Commanders on Friday night, but his night came to an early end. Mariota left the game during Washington's first offensive possession and went to the sideline medical tent. Mariota went to the locker room a short time later. Mariota's departure came after a play that saw him hand the ball off to Kaytron Allen, but he took a hit while delivering a pass on the previous play. Reports from the game say Mariota appeared to be gesturing to his knee. Sam Hartman took over at quarterback for the Commanders. Rookie Athan Kaliakmanis is the other available quarterback with Jayden Daniels taking the night off.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Bills, 49ers and Bears have called Bucs about Vita Vea
summary: Defensive tackle Vita Vea remains at odds with the Buccaneers over his contract and thus is not practicing.
full_text: '' Defensive tackle Vita Vea remains at odds with the Buccaneers over his contract and thus is not practicing. He wants a trade. The Buccaneers insist they aren't trading him. Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that the Bills, 49ers and Bears are among the teams who have called the Bucs about Vea. Vea requested a trade ahead of training camp after spending the offseason seeking a new contract. Philadelphia's Jalen Carter, Dallas' Quinnen Williams and Tennessee's Jeffery Simmons all have signed extensions recently, with Carter now at the top of the defensive tackle market at $38 million annually. Williams ($35.3 million per season) and Simmons ($35.276 million) are close behind. Vea now ranks 16th with an annual average of $17.75 million. He is entering the final year of his deal, set to make $17 million in base salary.
author: Charean Williams

title: Heather McPhee settles all claims in lawsuit against NFLPA and others
summary: Earlier this summer, former NFL Players Association general counsel Heather McPhee settled her wrongful discharge lawsuit against the union, without resolving the pending claims against the other defendants in the lawsuit.
full_text: Earlier this summer, former NFL Players Association general counsel Heather McPhee settled her wrongful discharge lawsuit against the union, without resolving the pending claims against the other defendants in the lawsuit. McPhee has now settled the entire case. Via ESPN, court filings submitted on Friday indicated that McPhee and the various defendants "have executed a final settlement agreement in this matter." The parties to the lawsuit asked the presiding judge to stay the case for 30 days while the conditions of the settlement are fulfilled. McPhee, a long-term employee of the NFLPA, was placed on leave last summer, following the resignation of executive director Lloyd Howell. She filed her lawsuit in December, and she was fired not long thereafter. She had sued the union, former executive director Lloyd Howell, general counsel Tom DePaso and Players Inc. president Matt Curtin after raising various concerns regarding union matters, including the strange decision to conceal from NFLPA membership a partial victory in a collusion grievance. While the terms weren't disclosed, the NFLPA's next annual report will likely contain information relating to any payment made to resolve to litigation.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Emeka Egbuka has sprained toe, should be good for Week 1
summary: The Buccaneers received good news about wide receiver Emeka Egbuka's injury on Friday.
full_text: The Buccaneers received good news about wide receiver Emeka Egbuka's injury on Friday. Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports that Egbuka underwent more testing on his injured toe and a specialist diagnosed him with a sprained toe. The Bucs are confident Egbuka will play Week 1. Egbuka limped off the field during the joint practice at the Jets' facility in New Jersey on Wednesday and did not return. He had 63 catches for 938 yards and six touchdowns during his rookie season and is expected to have an even bigger role with Mike Evans now in San Francisco.
author: Charean Williams

title: Geno Smith out on Friday due to foot soreness, Cade Klubnik will start for Jets
summary: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said this week that the team's starters would play against the Buccaneers on Friday night, but there's one significant change to that plan.
full_text: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said this week that the team's starters would play against the Buccaneers on Friday night, but there's one significant change to that plan. Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that quarterback Geno Smith has been scratched due to foot soreness. Per the report, the Jets are not concerned about the injury and Smith would be playing if this were a regular season contest. With Smith out of the lineup, fourth-round pick Cade Klubnik will get an extended run in his first NFL game action. The Jets listed Klubnik as the No. 2 quarterback on their initial depth chart and he will now get the start against Tampa. Brady Cook and Bailey Zappe are the other Jets quarterbacks.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bucs QB Jake Browning will not play against the Jets
summary: The Buccaneers have scrapped their plan to have Jake Browning start at quarterback against the Jets on Friday night.
full_text: ' The Buccaneers have scrapped their plan to have Jake Browning start at quarterback against the Jets on Friday night. Browning injured his back in a joint practice at the Jets' facility on Wednesday and Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports that he will not play in the preseason opener as a result. The Bucs said earlier in the week that Baker Mayfield will not take part in the game. Connor Bazelak and undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will be the quarterback for the Bucs on Friday. Browning signed with Tampa in March and is expected to be the No. 2 quarterback behind Mayfield as long as he's healthy.
author: Josh Alper

title: Commanders announce Jayden Daniels, many others won't play on Friday night
summary: There won't be anyone wearing No. 5 for the Commanders on Friday night.
full_text: There won't be anyone wearing No. 5 for the Commanders on Friday night. The Commanders announced that quarterback Jayden Daniels will not play against the Dolphins in the team's preseason opener. Daniels has been at odds with LSU this week about the school's decision to issue No. 5 to cornerback DJ Pickett for the 2026 season. Marcus Mariota, Sam Hartman, and Athan Kaliakmanis will be the available quarterbacks for Washington. Daniels will have plenty of company on the sideline. The Commanders announced that 25 other players will also be sitting out on Friday. That list includes most of the team's projected starters, but does not include first-round linebacker Sonny Styles.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sam Darnold won't play Saturday, as Drew Lock, Jalen Milroe will rotate series
summary: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will not play the team's preseason opener against the Cowboys on Saturday.
full_text: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will not play the team's preseason opener against the Cowboys on Saturday. Instead, it will be Drew Lock and Jalen Milroe in a rotation, Mike Macdonald said. "Sam's not going to play," Macdonald said, via Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 Seattle. "Drew will start the game, and then Jalen will come in, and they'll rotate to some degree. "Normally a quarterback goes until he doesn't go, and then the next guy goes and closes the game out. This game, I think we're going to rotate them to some extent." Darnold's absence is not a surprise, given the Seahawks have two more preseason games. The Seahawks' next preseason game is Aug. 23 at Tennessee. Rookie running back Jadarian Price also won't play. He has missed practice time of late due to lower-body soreness but did participate in a walkthrough Wednesday. "He's on the mend," Macdonald said.
author: Charean Williams

title: Deebo Samuel is officially back to wearing No. 19 in San Francisco
summary: New 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel's new number will be the same as old 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel's old number.
full_text: '' New 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel's new number will be the same as old 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel's old number. Samuel will officially wear the No. 19 jersey, the NFL's transaction report confirmed today. That's no surprise, as it's the number he had been wearing in practice. A 2019 second-round pick of the 49ers, Samuel wore No. 19 for his first five seasons in San Francisco before switching to No. 1, which he wore both in high school and at South Carolina, in 2024. He stayed No. 1 last year with the Commanders, but now he's back in San Francisco and back to his original jersey number. Before Samuel arrived, 49ers wide receiver Jacob Cowing had been wearing No. 19. Cowing is now wearing No. 6.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bills sign DB Wande Owens
summary: Defensive back Wande Owens is back with the Bills.
full_text: Defensive back Wande Owens is back with the Bills. The Bills announced Owens's signing on Friday. Linebacker Otis Reese was waived in a corresponding move. Owens signed with the Bills after going undrafted out of New Hampshire last year and spent the season on injured reserve. He returned to the Bills for the 2026 offseason, but was cut on July 31. Reese signed with the Bills a little more than a week ago, so it was a brief stay on the roster in Buffalo. The Bills also announced that wide receiver Quentin Skinner has switched to No. 18. He had been wearing No. 82 prior to the change.
author: Josh Alper

title: Josh Jacobs could return to Packers practice next week
summary: Packers running back Josh Jacobs has missed more than a week of practice with a groin injury, but his return could be around the corner.
full_text: ' Packers running back Josh Jacobs has missed more than a week of practice with a groin injury, but his return could be around the corner. Head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters on Friday that Jacobs could return to practice next week. LaFleur said that if Jacobs does return, he would likely come back late in the week. The Packers played their preseason opener on Thursday and they play again next Friday, so it is unlikely that Jacobs would be under consideration to play so soon after making it back to the field. Jacobs ran 535 times for 2,258 yards and 28 touchdowns over his first two seasons in Green Bay. He also caught 72 passes for 624 yards and two scores.
author: Josh Alper

title: DeMarcus Lawrence says this will be his final season
summary: Seahawks defensive end DeMarcus Lawrence thought about retiring after the 2025 season, but he won't go through the same process after the 2026 campaign.
full_text: Seahawks defensive end DeMarcus Lawrence thought about retiring after the 2025 season, but he won't go through the same process after the 2026 campaign. Lawrence told Jori Epstein of Yahoo Sports that " this will be my last year " as an NFL player. Lawrence is entering his 13th season. Given Lawrence's previous flirtation with retirement, it's not a great surprise that he has decided to make this his swan song. Lawrence joined the Seahawks last year after 11 seasons with the Cowboys and posted 53 tackles, six sacks, two fumble returns for touchdowns and three forced fumbles in the regular season. He had two more sacks in the playoffs to help the Seahawks secure the franchise's second Super Bowl title. Lawrence had 503 tackles, 61.5 sacks, two interceptions, 21 forced fumbles and eight fumble recoveries while with Dallas. He's been selected for five Pro Bowls and was a second-team All-Pro once.
author: Josh Alper

title: Texans cut K Chris Freeman
summary: The Texans signed kicker Chris Freeman on Wednesday to have him kick in Friday's preseason game.
full_text: The Texans signed kicker Chris Freeman on Wednesday to have him kick in Friday's preseason game. He kicked an extra point in the team's 27-7 loss to the Chargers. The team waived Freeman on Friday. Freeman is an undrafted free agent who played four college seasons at Indiana and two at Connecticut. In the past two seasons in Storrs, he made all 101 extra points and 43-of-52 field goals, with his 82.7 percent accuracy and 230 points leading the nation. Ka'imi Fairbairn is the Texans' kicker.
author: Charean Williams

title: Ravens activate LB Teddye Buchanan, place OL Kendall Lamm on reserve/retired
summary: The Ravens activated linebacker Teddye Buchanan from active/physically unable to perform, the team announced.
full_text: The Ravens activated linebacker Teddye Buchanan from active/physically unable to perform, the team announced. Buchanan, who is returning from a torn ACL, passed his physical Friday. Buchanan injured his knee on Dec. 14. "This dude has been incredible in how he's attacked coming off the injury that he's come off of," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said of Buchanan last week, via Ryan Mink of the team website. "It's our job to make sure that when we put him into the football environment that he's ready and he doesn't have any setbacks off of that." Buchanan took over the starting job next to Roquan Smith early last season and finished third on the team with 93 tackles despite missing the final three games. The Ravens also announced that they have placed veteran offensive tackle Kendall Lamm on the reserve/retired list. Lamm signed Aug. 3. Lamm, 34, played 11 NFL seasons with the Texans, Browns, Titans and Dolphins after entering the league as an undrafted free agent.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bills DT Phidarian Mathis suspended three games
summary: The NFL has suspended defensive tackle Phidarian Mathis for the first three games of the season for violating its substances of abuse policy.
full_text: The NFL has suspended defensive tackle Phidarian Mathis for the first three games of the season for violating its substances of abuse policy. Mathis can practice and play in the preseason, with his suspension starting on Aug. 30. He becomes eligible for reinstatement on Sept. 28. The suspension stems from an alcohol-related incident in spring of 2025 when Mathis played for the Jets, Alaina Getzenberg of ESPN reports. Mathis had 13 tackles in six games for the Bills last season and also appeared in one playoff game. Mathis appeared in 23 games over three seasons with Washington before signing with Buffalo. He had 25 tackles and a fumble recovery during his time with the NFC East squad.
author: Charean Williams

title: Steelers chief of staff Steve Scarnecchia suffered "medical situation" on Thursday
summary: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy shared on Friday that the club had a situation that resulted in some on-the-fly changes for last night’s preseason opener.
full_text: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy shared on Friday that the club had a situation that resulted in some on-the-fly changes for last night’s preseason opener. In an interview on the Pat McAfee Show, McCarthy said chief of staff Steve Scarnecchia suffered a “medical situation” and was attended to. “ We were really challenged last night ,” McCarthy said, via Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com. “[Scarnecchia is] my chief of staff, and he’s the guy that’s in charge of everything, especially the little things. A challenging opportunity for us as a coaching staff, football operations, especially the first game out the door. There was a lot of running around, frankly, behind the scenes and making sure we had everything buttoned up.” Scarnecchia is the son of famed former Patriots offensive line coach Dante Scarnecchia. The younger Scarnecchia joined the Steelers this offseason after McCarthy was hired.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Commanders DE Dorance Armstrong suspended one game
summary: The NFL suspended Commanders defensive end Dorance Armstrong for one game for violating its personal conduct policy.
full_text: The NFL suspended Commanders defensive end Dorance Armstrong for one game for violating its personal conduct policy. Armstrong can practice and play in the preseason, with the suspension scheduled to start Aug. 30. He becomes eligible to return Sept. 14. Nicki Jhabvala of TheAthletic.com found public records that show Armstrong was arrested May 10, 2025, in Frisco, Texas, on misdemeanor charges of assault causing bodily injury and resisting arrest. He received deferred adjudication for both. Armstrong continues to work his way back from the ACL he tore in Week 7 last season. He has 10.5 sacks over the past two seasons in Washington.
author: Charean Williams

title: Nazeeh Johnson suspended six games for violating PED policy
summary: The Titans will not have one of their cornerbacks at the beginning of the regular season.
full_text: The Titans will not have one of their cornerbacks at the beginning of the regular season. The NFL announced on Friday that Nazeeh Johnson has been suspended for the first six games of the year for violating the league’s policy on performance-enhancing substances. Johnson’s suspension will begin on Aug. 30 and he will be eligible for reinstatement on Monday, Oct. 19. Johnson, 28, was a Chiefs seventh-round pick in 2022, winning a pair of Super Bowls with the club. He’s appeared in 29 career games with six starts, recording three passes defensed and 66 total tackles. He signed with the Titans in late July.
author: Myles Simmons

title: NFL suspends James Pearce Jr. eight games for February domestic-violence incident
summary: Pearce entered a diversion program in May, triggering the disciplinary process.
full_text: As expected, the NFL has suspended Falcons defensive end James Pearce Jr., following a February domestic-violence incident that resulted in three felony charges. The league has announced that it has imposed an eight-game suspension on Pearce, under the Personal Conduct Policy. Per the league, Pearce is eligible to participate in all preseason activities, including games. The suspension will begin on August 30, and he will be eligible for reinstatement on Monday, November 2. The policy provides a baseline suspension of six games for domestic violence. The number can increase due to aggravating circumstances. In this case, Pearce resisted arrest and ultimately drove away from police. Pearce entered into a diversion program in May, which is one of the automatic triggers for discipline under the Personal Conduct Policy. The Falcons seemed to know it was coming; their initial depth chart had Pearce listed on the third string . It's unclear at this point whether Pearce has accepted the punishment and will not appeal, or whether he'll try to reduce the punishment. In various cases, the announced suspension is the result of a negotiation between the team, the player, and the NFL Players Association. Basically, the player accepts something less than what the league would try to secure through the full-blown process created by the Personal Conduct Policy and the Collective Bargaining Agreement. Pearce will be subject to even stronger punishments in the event of another violation, up to and including banishment from the league with the opportunity to apply for reinstatement after one year. UPDATE 3:32 p.m. ET : Per the league, the suspension is final. There will be no appeal.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jordyn Tyson will miss time with hamstring injury, could linger into regular season
summary: The Saints will not have one of their key rookies on the field for a while.
full_text: The Saints will not have one of their key rookies on the field for a while. Head coach Kellen Moore told reporters on Friday that first-round pick Jordyn Tyson will miss time with the hamstring injury he suffered during Thursday’s joint practice with the Jaguars. While Moore did not provide a timetable for Tyson’s recovery, he noted the receiver’s injury could potentially linger into Week 1. “We've just got to let these experts evaluate this, and then we'll put together a plan ," Moore said, via Katherine Terrell of ESPN. "Not going to jump to conclusions. I don't have a doctor in front of my name, so I'm not going to jump to put together a timeline on it.” Moore noted that this injury is unrelated to the previous hamstring injuries Tyson has suffered throughout his playing career. "I think my understanding of this one, any player that was put in his situation where your foot slips and you get shoved from behind, this has nothing to do with Jordyn's history," Moore said. "Any player in that situation probably has the same diagnosis coming out of this.” Tyson was the No. 8 overall pick of this year’s draft, with the Saints set to pair him with Chris Olave to provide a pair of strong receiving targets for young quarterback Tyler Shough.
author: Myles Simmons

title: NFL preseason Week 1 winners and losers: Steelers rookie QB shines, Cam Ward struggles for Titans
summary: From rookie quarterbacks making their mark to standout wide receivers, we break down the biggest winners -- and some losers -- from the opening week of NFL preseason action
full_text:
The first week of the NFL preseason is officially here. We got a small taste of the action last week with the Hall of Fame Game, but this week, things will be kicking into warp drive with 16 games going down between Thursday and Saturday.
When it comes to the preseason, you never know what you're going to see on the field. Some coaches will keep their starters on the bench, but that strategy isn't for everyone. There are also plenty of coaches who like to see their starters get some action in the preseason.
With that in mind, we're going to start off this winners and losers list by naming every coach who plays their starters a winner. Thanks for adding some excitement to the preseason.
And now, let's get to our full winners and losers list for Week 1 of the preseason.
Courtland Sutton set the tone Friday evening, and apparently, the word got around: Let's make some highlights. Sutton "Mossed" Falcons defensive back Mike Hughes on the opening possession and made a ridiculous one-handed snag on the next drive. Overall, he finished with three catches for 60 yards in very limited action.
Courtland Sutton doing Courtland Sutton things in the 1st quarter 🔥 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/iIDAcg6WOv
Sutton's size, strength and contested-catch ability are going to be great complements to trade acquisition Jaylen Waddle , whose game is more based on speed, verticality and yards after the catch. Bo Nix (who, like Waddle, didn't play Friday night) is going to love having both on the field together.
Sutton's catch was awesome, but let's also shout out Dolphins rookie Caleb Douglas , who is making waves in training camp ...
Caleb Douglas oh my 😮 MIAvsWAS Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/21vkGuMeTb
What a catch by Garrett Wilson! TBvsNYJ on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/nULmGf71tf
With Aaron Rodgers set to retire at the end of the 2026 season , the Steelers need to find their quarterback of the future and they might have already done that. The team drafted former Penn State QB Drew Allar in the third round back in April and he was a one-man highlight show during the Steelers' 28-9 win over the Packers on Thursday night. Allar didn't get in the game until the second half, but once he was on the field, he absolutely took over: He finished 10 of 13 for 153 yards and three total touchdowns.
Drew Allar SHINES in His Steelers Preseason Debut vs. Green Bay 🔥 10/13, 153 PYDS, 2 PTD, 1 Rushing TD pic.twitter.com/j3Zmx8dsUV
Will Howard and Mason Rudolph also saw some action on Thursday and they were both good, but Allar was great. Khan's decision to draft Allar -- despite having Rudolph and Howard already on the roster -- is looking like a smart one so far. Of course, Allar put up his numbers in the second half against the backend of the Packers' defensive roster, so we still need to see what he can do against better competition, but this is a promising start. We broke down Allar's full performance from Thursday and you can read more about that here .
Oh, and Friday, the Steelers and Keeanu Benton agreed to a four-year, $72 million extension, per E SPN. It's another nice find for Khan: Benton was the 49th overall pick in 2023.
The rookie kicker has struggled at times during training camp, but he seems to have put those struggles behind him. Smack had a huge game against the Steelers, scoring all nine of Green Bay's points in the loss. Smack went 3-for-3 on field goal attempts and that includes hitting a 58-yarder just before halftime.
Trey Smack went from a problem to a solution tonight! #gopackgo pic.twitter.com/B8ibXAPFzv
Long field goals are notoriously difficult to hit at Heinz Field, so that's an impressive kick.
Smack actually Smacked TWO 58-yard field goals in the game, but one of them got taken off the board due to a Steelers penalty. The former Florida star was the ONLY placekicker selected in this year's draft and the Packers' decision to take him is starting to look like it might actually pay off.
Earlier this year, we ranked the 10 worst QB rooms in the NFL and the Cardinals were near the top of the list. And I'm only telling you that because we might need to redo our rankings if the Cardinals quarterbacks keep playing like they did during the team's 27-14 win over the Raiders on Thursday. Jacoby Brissett , Gardner Minshew and Kedon Slovis combined to go 26 of 30 for 212 yards and three touchdowns. Brissett and Minshew combined to go a perfect 15 of 15 in the first half and Brissett threw what might end up going down as the most impressive touchdown pass of the preseason.
Marvin Harrison Jr TD! Also, what a throw from Jacoby Brissett pic.twitter.com/zwB57KgMVB
Brissett was on the field for just one possession, but he made the most of it, going 5 of 5 for 44 yards, including that TD pass to Marvin Harrison Jr . You never want to overreact to anything from the preseason, but if Brissett is going to be making throws like that all year, the Cards' offense could surprise us this year.
The Mendoza hype train has been going strong since April 23 when the Raiders selected him with the first overall pick in the NFL Draft . We finally got to see Mendoza in action on Thursday and he looked impressive. He wasn't perfect -- he completed 10 of 16 passes for 97 yards and a TD -- but he showed flashes of what he could eventually become, and that's exactly what you want to see if you're the Raiders.
Fernando Mendoza threading the needle! Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/PC9UPZvRxA
Although Mendoza was good, Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said the starting QB job was still Kirk Cousins ' to lose, so don't look for the rookie to be starting in Week 1. If you want a deeper dive into Mendoza's first start, we've got that here .
Kyle Shanahan made the decision to bench most of his starters against the Titans on Thursday, which makes sense, because training camp has been a battle of attrition for the 49ers . Everyone is injured. However, Stribling is healthy and he might have been the best offensive player on the field for the 49ers. He caught seven passes for 63 yards against the Titans and he did all of that in just one half of play.
An impressive preseason debut for @49ers ' second-round pick De'Zhaun Stribling: 7 catches 63 yards All in the first half 🙌 TENvsSF on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/VxhMoyrhFb
If you have a fantasy draft coming up, you might want to think about taking Stribling. With Ricky Pearsall out for the season, Stribling could definitely make a name for himself in San Francisco as a rookie.
If you need someone to root for this year, make it Dohnte Meyers . Going into training camp, the Bengals receiver looked like a long shot to make the roster, but he's slowly been proving that he belongs. In Thursday's game against the Lions , not only did he catch three passes for 29 yards, but the human Swiss Army knife also had one rush for 13 yards and a punt return for 11 yards.
After the Bengals' 16-14 win, Joe Burrow revealed that Meyers drove seven hours overnight from Atlanta to Cincinnati just to attend an offseason throwing session with the QB. And that's just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to his unlikely story.
Driving through the night from Atlanta to Cincinnati to impress your QB? Just the latest step for Dohnte Meyers: 🏈 Presbyterian College (2018-19) 🏈 Delta State College (2020-22) 🏈 Undrafted (2023) 🏈 Saskatchewan Roughriders (2024-25) 🏈 Grey Cup Champion (2025) 🏈 Cincinnati… pic.twitter.com/5DIa0LjLz2
The 26-year-old Meyers, who spent some time in the CFL , has never played a down in an NFL regular-season game, but that could soon change because it's looking more and more likely that he's going to make the roster.
Last week, the Falcons lost 2025 first-round EDGE Jalon Walker to a torn ACL in practice. It was a crushing, sudden blow.

title: NFL hands down four suspensions before preseason action, with Falcons' James Pearce Jr. hit hardest
summary: The NFL announced four suspensions before Friday's preseason slate, with Falcons edge rusher James Pearce Jr. ordered to sit out eight games
full_text:
We had a bit of a news dump in the NFL ahead of the three preseason games that kicked off Friday night. The league suspended four players at the start of the season for various violations, headlined by Atlanta Falcons pass rusher James Pearce Jr. , who was issued an eight-game suspension following his offseason arrest.
All four suspensions begin on Aug. 30, meaning the players can participate in preseason activities, including preseason games. Two notable players who did not receive suspensions on Friday are Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs and Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua . However, the NFL is looking into these situations. Jacobs was arrested this offseason on charges related to domestic violence, but the case remains open. As for Nacua, a woman filed a civil lawsuit against him in March on allegations of gender violence, along with assault and battery.
The NFL suspended James Pearce Jr. eight games without pay for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy. He is eligible for reinstatement on Monday, Nov. 2.
The Defensive Rookie of the Year finalist was arrested on Feb. 7 after he chased his then-girlfriend in an SUV and rammed her vehicle. Pearce fled from police before eventually being apprehended. He was initially charged with three felonies: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person.
Pearce struck an agreement where if he completed a pre-trial intervention program and stayed out of trouble for six months, all charges would be dismissed. The victim and the police officers involved in the case agreed to this resolution.
The loss of Pearce is a massive one for Atlanta, especially when you consider that fellow second-year pass rusher Jalon Walker suffered a torn ACL in training camp. In his first NFL season, Pearce set a Falcons rookie record by racking up 10.5 sacks in addition to 26 tackles. On the Falcons' initial depth chart, Cameron Thomas and Brandon Dorlus are listed as their starting pass rushers.
Buffalo Bills defensive tackle Phidarian Mathis was suspended for the first three games of the season after he violated the NFL's substance abuse policy. He is eligible for reinstatement on Monday, Sept. 28.
The former second-round pick of the Washington Commanders played six games for the Bills last year and made 13 tackles. He re-signed with Buffalo on a one-year deal this offseason.
On the Bills' initial depth chart, Mathis was listed as a second-string defensive lineman behind Ed Oliver , Deone Walker and T.J. Sanders .
Tennessee Titans cornerback Nazeeh Johnson was suspended six games for violating the NFL's performance-enhancing substances policy. He is eligible for reinstatement on Monday, Oct. 19.
Johnson spent his first four NFL seasons with the Kansas City Chiefs before signing with the Titans last month. In 29 career games played with six starts, he's recorded 66 tackles, three passes defensed and one sack.
Johnson was listed as a third-string cornerback on Tennessee's initial depth chart. In the Titans' 19-13 preseason victory over the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday night, he tied for the team lead in tackles with five.
Commanders pass rusher Dorance Armstrong was suspended one game for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy. Armstrong was arrested in Texas last year on misdemeanor charges of assault causing bodily injury and resisting arrest/search or transport, a ccording to ESPN .
Armstrong got off to a productive start for Washington last season, recording 5.5 sacks in the first seven games. However, he then tore his ACL.
Armstrong is still recovering from his knee injury, and was listed as a second-string pass rusher on Washington's first depth chart behind free-agent additions Odafe Oweh and K'Lavon Chaisson .

title: James Pearce Jr. suspended eight games following offseason arrest
summary: Pearce's suspension stems from a February arrest following a domestic dispute involving his then-girlfriend Rickea Jackson
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons pass rusher James Pearce Jr . received an eight-game suspension from the NFL for his Feb. 7 arrest following a domestic dispute with then-girlfriend Rickea Jackson, according to ESPN .
Pearce was initially charged with three felonies: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person. A felony aggravated stalking charge was changed to a misdemeanor, while a charge of aggravated battery of a law enforcement officer was dropped.
Jackson told police she noticed Pearce following her vehicle in a white Lamborghini SUV, according to the criminal complaint, obtained by ESPN . When stopped at a red light, Pearce exited his car and attempted to open the driver's side door of her vehicle. Jackson sped away, while Pearce went back to his vehicle and pursued her.
Jackson began to head towards the Doral Police Department, and she told police during the drive that Pearce "intentionally collided into the rear of her vehicle." He eventually cut her off with his SUV and hit her car head-on.
When police arrived on the scene, they observed Pearce standing outside of his SUV with the door open. An officer drew his firearm and ordered Pearce to the ground. The 22-year-old instead got back in his vehicle, locked it, and after a short time, drove away. Police pursued Pearce, who eventually crashed his vehicle. After a brief foot pursuit, Pearce was apprehended. Authorities say he "began to resist arrest by tensing his arms and not allowing officers to apprehend him."
Pearce's legal team said in a March statement released to ESPN that he "maintains his innocence and urges the public to understand that while allegations have the power to shape a narrative, it is hardly the full, complete story."
Despite the dramatic situation, Pearce's legal team struck an agreement where if he completed a pre-trial intervention program and stayed out of trouble for six months, all charges would be dismissed. Jackson and the police officers involved in the case agreed to this resolution.
While Pearce is on track to avoid prison time, his infraction still violated the NFL's personal conduct policy and resulted in his suspension.
The Falcons front office was aggressive during the 2025 NFL Draft , selecting former Georgia pass rusher Jalon Walker at No. 15 overall, then trading back into the first round for Pearce at No. 26 overall. Atlanta won't have either player to begin the season.
Walker, who recorded 36 tackles and 5.5 sacks as a rookie, tore his ACL in training camp and will miss the entire 2026 season. Now, the Falcons will be without their other young pass rusher for the first eight games, as well.
The loss of Pearce is a big one. He set a Falcons rookie record by racking up 10.5 sacks in his first NFL season, to go along with 26 tackles, 16 QB hits, 10 tackles for loss, five passes defensed and a forced fumble. Pearce and teammate Xavier Watts were named finalists for Defensive Rookie of the Year, an award ultimately won by Cleveland Browns linebacker Carson Schwesinger .
With Pearce and Walker now out, the Falcons will look at Azeez Ojulari , Samson Ebukam , Brandon Dorlus , Cameron Thomas and Bralen Trice to pick up the slack. Keep an eye on sixth-round pick linebacker Harold Perkins Jr . as well, who could work as a hybrid.
James Pearce Jr. (suspended)
Ojulari, Ebukam and Thomas are additions made in free agency this offseason. Ojulari, who is 26, notched eight sacks as a rookie for the New York Giants back in 2021 and six sacks for Big Blue in 2024, but played just three games for the Philadelphia Eagles last season due to a hamstring injury. Ebukam, who is an older player at 31, comes over from the Indianapolis Colts . He's recorded 35 sacks over eight seasons, and missed the 2024 campaign with a torn Achilles. Thomas, on the other hand, has bumped around the league, playing for the Arizona Cardinals , Kansas City Chiefs, and Browns. Despite his initial placement on Atlanta's depth chart, he has very limited starting experience with just three games.
How this new-look pass-rush group pans out in the preseason is certainly something to watch.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Cowboys' Dak Prescott on George Pickens' future contract: 'He should get every dollar that he deserves'
summary: Prescott wants his team to keep the star wide receiver long term
full_text:
Count Dak Prescott among the many people in Dallas who think the Cowboys should back up the Brinks truck and pay George Pickens his money. CeeDee Lamb already spoke earlier this week about his desire to see the Cowboys keep his running mate around over the long term, and on Thursday, it was Prescott's turn to advocate for the team to spend up and keep one of the league's best receiver duos intact.
"George, you know he loves football. And at the end of the day, it's not for the money," Prescott said during an appearance on Up & Adams . "However, he should get every dollar that he deserves because he's a hell of a player. And we should probably give it to him sooner than later because [the price] is only gonna go up."
Alas, the Cowboys actually cannot pay Pickens anytime soon. The deadline for franchise-tagged players to sign a long-term deal with their team passed back in July, and Pickens signed his franchise tag. He will play this season on a fully guaranteed, one-year, $27.3 million contract, and the Cowboys won't be able to give him a long-term deal until after the Super Bowl .
Prescott is correct, though, about the price only going up. The wide receiver market has exploded over the last few years, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba set a new high-water mark at the position with the four-year, $168.6 million contract extension he signed this offseason.
If Pickens comes anywhere close to replicating what he did in Dallas last year, when he caught 93 passes for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns and was named both a Pro-Bowler and Second Team All-Pro, he is going to get paid at or near the top of the market by somebody, whether it's the Cowboys or another team. That is going to happen. (Unless the Cowboys use the franchise tag on Pickens for a second time.)
As we wrote earlier this week, investing in both Lamb and Pickens on long-term deals wouldn't exactly be unheard of. The Bengals paid both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins , the Lions paid both Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams , the Dolphins paid both Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle before later moving on from both of them and the Eagles paid both A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith before trading Brown this offseason.
The difference, of course, is that the secondary receivers among those duos got paid quite a bit less than the No. 1s, whereas if Pickens has a season that's even close to representative of his talent, he might earn a contract that pays him even more than Lamb. Paying two wideouts at that level would be somewhat unprecedented -- and somewhat complicated for a team that is also paying Prescott, Tyler Smith and the recently-extended Quinnen Williams near the top of the market at their respective positions.
Still, the Cowboys can absolutely afford to do it if they want to. We've seen plenty of teams pay numerous players at or near the top of the market for their positions by massaging cap hits with bonuses and void years, kicking the can down the road on the cap.(The Eagles are experts at this, and the Lions will soon have to be as well, given how many players they have paid in recent years.) The salary cap can be manipulated in pretty much any way you want to do it in the short term, as long as you're willing to eat dead cap hits somewhere down the line.
Jerry Jones himself admitted that it's realistic for the Cowboys to pay Pickens. The only open questions here are whether Pickens will keep his head on straight and perform like he did last year, and whether the Cowboys will be willing to open the checkbook if and when he does.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Rams' Puka Nacua reveals injury he suffered at Michael Rubin party
summary: Nacua ran into a glass window while looking for teammate Davante Adams
full_text:
It won't find him on the non-football injury list, but Puka Nacua did injure his face (and maybe his pride) earlier this offseason at Michael Rubin's infamous "White Party." During a recent appearance on the "Impaulsive" podcast, the Los Angeles Rams receiver recalled running into a glass window at Rubin's party after seeing Snoop Dogg while looking for his teammate and fellow wideout, Davante Adams .
"The glass window pane won," Nacua told host Logan Paul. "It was Snoop Dogg, I was so excited. ... I had to go see where Davante [Adams] was at, and I turned around and I'm like ... They clean the windows really good at Rubin's house. They are perfectly crisp and didn't see it coming."
Paul recalled seeing Nacua at the party after he slammed into the window, and there was blood dripping down his face.
"They made me feel better when they said three other people ran into it, but nobody else ended up bleeding from it, so I'm like, I don't know if that made me feel much better or worse."
Puka Nacua INJURED his face at Michael Rubin’s white party 😱🩸 pic.twitter.com/gPEIzcckmR
Fortunately for Nacua and the Rams, the injury was not serious and hasn't impacted his availability throughout training camp. That said, the veteran pass catcher is dealing with psoas (deep core muscle connecting the lower spine to the thigh bone) soreness that forced him to leave Tuesday's joint practice with the Cowboys . He did not practice on Thursday, but head coach Sean McVay said that Nacua will be "ready to go" for practice next week.
"We're just being smart with him," McVay said, via the official team website . "Expecting to be back next week, ready to go."
Nacua is coming off a 2025 season where he led the NFL with 129 receptions and 107.2 receiving yards per game. His 1,715 receiving yards made him just the third Rams player in franchise history with at least 1,700 receiving yards in a single season. His 10 receiving touchdowns were also a career high.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: One takeaway from each NFL team's first depth chart: Browns show rookies love; starting over for Deebo Samuel
summary: The first unofficial depth charts of the preseason are here, revealing surprising rookie placements and intense position battles across the league
full_text:
The NFL preseason is here, and it's about time. Training camps are fun, but these exhibition matchups are more important when it comes to position battles and surprise standouts. The preseason is where quarterback battles are won and lost, and where roster spots are earned and fumbled. It's where undrafted players will stake their claim to the eventual "final 53," and where starting veterans can begin to give way to younger talents.
Now that we've reached the second week of August, each NFL team has released its first unofficial depth chart. These are not to be taken as gospel, and there are a lot of "ORs" featured. Depth charts will experience quite a bit of change over the next three weeks, but that won't stop us from overanalyzing them.
With that said, here's one takeaway from each NFL team's first depth chart.
The Arizona Cardinals took a major swing in selecting former Notre Dame running back Jeremiyah Love with the No. 3 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft . Since he was drafted this high, Love automatically becomes the highest-paid running back in the NFL with $50.5 million guaranteed in his rookie contract. Correct, Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs don't have those kinds of guarantees in their new contracts. Still, new coach Mike LaFleur is going to make Love earn his starting spot, as free agent addition Tyler Allgeier is listed as the starter over him and James Conner . It's expected that Love will overtake Allgeier on the depth chart at some point, but the former Falcon will still have a role in this offense.
With Jalon Walker set to miss the 2026 season after tearing his ACL and the looming James Pearce Jr . suspension, the rest of the Atlanta Falcons pass-rush group is going to need to step up. The two players slated to start right now according to the depth chart are Brandon Dorlus and Cameron Thomas , with Azeez Ojulari and Samson Ebukam backing them up.
Dorlus was a fourth-round pick of the Falcons in 2024. In 15 games played with nine starts from the interior of the defensive line last season, he recorded 27 tackles and 8.5 sacks -- which ranked second on the team behind Pearce's 10.5. Thomas on the other hand comes over from the Cleveland Browns , and has limited starting experience with just three starts in 58 career games played.
Rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane has been one of the biggest stories of training camp. The third-round pick out of USC has dazzled on the practice field, registering multiple highlight-reel catches, and will force Jesse Minter and Declan Doyle to put him on the field. On the Baltimore Ravens ' first depth chart, Lane was listed as second team behind Rashod Bateman and Zay Flowers . Lane is one of two second-team wideouts, joining Devontez Walker . He is listed ahead of Elijah Sarratt and Chris Moore .
The Buffalo Bills are listing Alec Anderson as the starter at left guard over Austin Corbett . Anderson, who went undrafted in 2022 out of UCLA, has started six games over two seasons, and played snaps at left guard, center and right tackle last year for Buffalo. Corbett comes over from the Carolina Panthers , where he started 37 games over four years. He's got the edge when it comes to experience, and played plenty of center too.
There weren't many surprises with the Panthers' first depth chart. It's easy to identify their top two running backs in Chuba Hubbard and Jonathon Brooks , but I was interested in their RB4. AJ Dillon , also known as the Quadfather or Quadzilla, is listed last on Carolina's depth chart behind second-year back Trevor Etienne . Etienne provides special teams value as a returner, but Dillon is an ideal short-yardage back -- as he proved during the Hall of Fame Game. Could the Panthers keep all four running backs at the 53-man deadline?
Os Panthers respondem com A.J. DILLON! 📺: Assista ao vivo no @sportv e NFL Game Pass pic.twitter.com/u0BLSeHZav
The Chicago Bears didn't want to list a starting left tackle on their depth chart. They didn't even want to cut the competition down to two players. Braxton Jones , Jedrick Wills Jr. and Kiran Amegadjie are all listed as "first string." The battle to replace Ozzy Trapilo rages on. Jones is probably considered the favorite.
Now that Trey Hendrickson is out of the picture, the Cincinnati Bengals are looking for new difference-makers at pass rusher. Free agent addition Boye Mafe and former first-round pick Myles Murphy are listed as the starters right now, with former No. 17 overall pick Shemar Stewart and rookie Cashius Howell listed as the backups.
Maybe this isn't a surprise, but Murphy has recorded just 8.5 sacks in 47 career games played. This could be his last season with the Bengals. Stewart is on the mend after suffering a hyperextended knee in camp, and you have to wonder if he could overtake Murphy on the depth chart at some point.
Shoutout to the Browns, who aren't trying to hide the fact that rookies are going to play major roles for them this season. A whopping THREE first-year players were listed as starters on their first depth chart: Wide receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion , and then left tackle Spencer Fano .
There's nothing dramatic about the Dallas Cowboys ' initial depth chart, and they didn't want to name a front-runner in the Shavon Revel Jr . vs. Cobie Durant battle at corner. What was sweet is that Dallas has a "DB" position -- which surely means slot corner. Rookie Caleb Downs is listed as the starter there, with him also a second-string safety.
Downs should be a front-runner to win Defensive Rookie of the Year. He was the only FBS defensive back to rack up 250 tackles, 15 tackles for loss and grab five interceptions over the past three seasons.
Marvin Mims , the All-Pro returner who has started in just 13 of his 48 career games played, is listed as a starting wide receiver with Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton . He's listed above Troy Franklin , the college teammate of quarterback Bo Nix , who finished second on the team last year with 709 yards receiving, and Pat Bryant , who has been making some serious waves in training camp. Mims caught 37 passes for 322 yards and one touchdown last season. Interesting.
One position battle I'm interested in with the Detroit Lions is cornerback. Terrion Arnold is no longer with the team after his arrest on eight felony charges which include kidnapping and armed robbery. That opened up a starting job.
Right now, the Lions have the veteran Rock Ya-Sin listed opposite of D.J. Reed with Roger McCreary in the slot. This isn't a major surprise, but we'll see if the young Ennis Rakestraw Jr ., Nick Whiteside or rookie Keith Abney II can push him.
Anthony Belton is listed as the starting right guard for the Green Bay Packers right now, with Donovan Jennings and Karsen Barnhart behind him. Jager Burton has been working in as well. Belton, who mostly played left tackle in college, has a ways to go when it comes to locking down this job. He could end up being demoted to swing tackle. To make matters worse, the expected starter at left guard, Aaron Banks , has been held to just individual work due to a knee issue.
The Houston Texans ' first depth chart didn't provide us with any surprises. What's notable is that rookie Keylan Rutledge has apparently already earned the starting center spot, while the right tackle battle continues with Trent Brown and Braden Smith separated by an "OR" on the depth chart.
Backup quarterbacks Riley Leonard and Anthony Richardson have an "OR" between their names on the Indianapolis Colts ' depth chart. It's been quite a fall from grace for the former No. 4 overall pick, who hasn't had the best training camp, according to reporters on the beat. It's a bit surprising that the Colts have been unable to move him. Perhaps a strong showing in the preseason sparks a market. The Tennessee Titans are likely hoping the same happens with Will Levis .
There are some notable position battles to monitor in Jacksonville and everyone is going to care about where Travis…

This is the second consecutive year in which Jeremiah Smith opens the campaign as the No. 1 player in college football. Brockermeyer says he is the greatest receiving prospect he has ever evaluated, and anyone who watched Ohio State over the past two years would find it hard to disagree.

title: Beaks & Geeks: Cardinals take down Raiders
summary: The Arizona Cardinals finally got a win in this year’s preseason. Last week, they had a late lead only to lose in the final seconds. New head coach Mike LaFleur had to wait a week to get his first NFL victory as they slayed the Las Vegas Raiders 27-14 on the road. Playing under a […]
full_text: QB Gardner Minshew II #15 hands the ball off to RB Jeremiyah Love #4 in the second quarter (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals finally got a win in this year’s preseason. Last week, they had a late lead only to lose in the final seconds. New head coach Mike LaFleur had to wait a week to get his first NFL victory as they slayed the Las Vegas Raiders 27-14 on the road. Playing under a dome certainly helped with the stagnant heat in Nevada, where it is hot under a shade tree at night. A good crowd of 61,683 showed up to see their new quarterback, first overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza. RELATED: BISONTIS LEAVES GAME WITH KNEE INJURY The first string offense only played one series, but that ended in seven points. Keep in mind, this is only preseason, and this game was against the Raiders, who only won three games last year. Both teams finished with identical 3-14-0 records last year, and both teams sport new head coaches. So, who played well for the Cardinals? Who didn’t? ——————————————————————————- BEAKS Play calling – It is just the preseason, and vanilla is pretty popular. But what we have seen from the new ball coach and his ability to run an offense has been impressive in both games so far. QB Jacoby Brissett – Okay, so maybe a quarterback that goes to work and hasn’t shown up for the last several months can indeed learn a new system quickly. He was in command and led his one drive for early points. The touchdown to WR Marv Harrison in the back right of the end zone almost appeared like it came off his hand as a Hail Mary, but was on the money with a step to spare in the back corner in double coverage. Amazing throw. Early in the first quarter, facing a third-and-11 just inside Raiders’ territory, Brissett found WR Michael Wilson for 18 yards down to the 28-yard line. Several plays later, he hit WR Kendrick Bourne for 12 yards to the seven, with the TD pass to Harrison the very next play. Brissett went 5-for-5 for 101 yards, one TD, zero picks, and was not sacked a single time. His QB rating was 142.9. QB Gardner Minshew – Let’s just continue with the quarterback room. Another excellent performance. Minshew took over the second series like an old pro. At one time was 10-for-10 and finished 14-for-16 for 102 yards with two touchdowns and zero picks, with a 132.8 QB rating. If Brissett is named the Week 1 starter, Minshew doing well in live games is such a great sign for this offense. The Minshew vs. Carson Beck debate can sizzle all year, but we know if something happens to Brissett, this offense will still compete. Two good efficiency performances from two quarterbacks is a LaFleur trait. Gardner Minshew threw a dime. Jalen Brooks caught it and celebrated. Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2vlsdSFK6A — NFL (@NFL) August 14, 2026 WR Jalen Brooks – Second impressive game out of two. Get this: targeted six times, had six receptions. Great hands and is a fearless receiver. Just go ahead and name him on the final roster. Led all receivers with 52 yards, and his touchdown was with just 17 seconds left in the first half. LB Karson Sharar – Had a great game and seemed to be everywhere, even when he wasn’t making a tackle. Big hit on special teams. Led all Arizona defenders with five total tackles and one tackle for loss. First down and third down – This offense netted 23 first downs, which is a great sight to see. Then on third-down efficiency, they went 8-15. Take both every game. Zero turnovers – When is the last time you saw a team in preseason not turn the ball over? Chad Ryland is good from 56! 📲 NFL+ pic.twitter.com/6antqjqVLV — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) August 14, 2026 Kicking team – P Blake Gillikin had only two punts all game, but he had a 51.5 average per kick. Both times he flipped the field position. Last year he led the league in punting average with 51.7, so he is keeping his consistency going. K Chad Ryland went 2-for-3 in field goal attempts but nailed on for 56-yards. ————————————————————————————————————- GEEKS Preseason injuries that affect the regular season – We all know that the preseason has its place in the lives of every player in training camp. 90 players have to be pared down to 53. But lordy, when a promising rookie, such as OG Chase Bisontis, goes down and is holding his knee, it makes you want to scream. We will see just how bad, or perhaps the bullet he dodged, very soon. Afterwards, LaFleur told the media, “Not good.” Already lost another rookie, DT Kaleb Proctor, for the year. WR Ihmir Smith-Marsette – With a thick receiving room full of talented young guys, Smith-Marsette only has a few games to show he is the Wild Card in this group to make the final roster. Despite looking really good in practices against his own teammates, he needs to show out in live action. One reception for seven yards isn’t going to get it done. He also had one kickoff return for 24 yards. Yawn. FERNANDO MENDOZA FIRST RAIDERS TD Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/G8F3FQt60C — NFL (@NFL) August 14, 2026 CB Sean Murphy-Bunting – Playing in the nickel position, he does not contest his receivers close enough. On the touchdown toss to Raiders WR Jack Bech, Murphy-Bunting just watched the receiver float on by and then acted confused as to how his man got so open. For all his game snaps, he had just two tackles. ——————————————————————————– Bird Seed: You can learn more character on the two-yard line than anywhere else in life LOVE IS IN THE AIR 🆙 📲 NFL+ pic.twitter.com/PN6FL971tX — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) August 14, 2026 RB Jeremiyah Love – For the record, the rookie’s first carry was the first offensive play of the game for three yards with the tackle by the Raiders’ Taron Johnson. Impressive run for 14 yards right before the first half two-minute warning, and then the very first play after the break for 16 yards; he ran like he had been there before. The rookie looked good for the most part. He left the game with an apparent ankle issue, so we will see where that goes. 11 carries for 58 yards, with a long run of 16 yards. Also caught three balls for 14 yards. He displayed the juice; now let’s not get him hurt before Week 1. WR Marv Harrison – One target, one reception, one touchdown, and then drew a pass interference call. Call this one sold. Reggie. Virgil. 📺: NFL+ pic.twitter.com/8nnAAnCNAW — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) August 14, 2026 WR Reggie Virgil – The rookie continues to impress. Had only two catches on four targets, but that 24-yard one-handed grab to deep left was a thing of beauty. Two receptions for 43 yards and a 21.5-yard-per-catch average. DT Walter Nolen – Played well and didn’t look like he had any issues for a change. Got a great shot on the Raiders QB for the sack and played the run well. C Jon Gaines – Had several good blocks on NT Benito Jones that sprang Love on those two good runs, plus another nine-yarder earlier in the second quarter.

title: Arizona Cardinals news: Jeremiyah Love impresses in preseason debut
summary: The Cardinals bounced back from last week’s last-second loss to the Panthers to put together a fairly complete game in a 27-14 win over the Raiders on Thursday night. Starters got snaps, including Jacoby Brissett and Jeremiyah Love, as they built a 21-14 lead at the half that they’d never relinquish over the final 30 […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 13: Jeremiyah Love #4 of the Arizona Cardinals picks up a first down against the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter of a preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Cardinals defeated the Raiders 27-14. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cardinals bounced back from last week’s last-second loss to the Panthers to put together a fairly complete game in a 27-14 win over the Raiders on Thursday night. Starters got snaps, including Jacoby Brissett and Jeremiyah Love, as they built a 21-14 lead at the half that they’d never relinquish over the final 30 minutes. Surprisingly, Love got 14 touches on the night, all of which came in the first half. That’s a bit aggressive for your third-overall pick in his first preseason game, but he nonetheless came out unscathed after a strong outing. Love took 11 carries for 58 yards and caught three more passes for 13 more. He showed off that burst and speed that made him such a high draft pick, and he even threw in a smooth hurdle for good measure. It’s wildly early in the process still, but the first look at Love was everything fans hoped it would be.
