title: Browns RB Quinshon Judkins ready to fill Todd Monken’s needs on offense
summary: Defense and a great running game. These are Cleveland Browns hallmarks. All of those Marty Schottenheimer teams that played in three AFC Championship Games featured a really good defense with a run game that was difficult to stop. Paul Brown had both with guys like Jim Brown, Ernie Green, Marion Motley, and Bobby Mitchell. RELATED: […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 11: Quinshon Judkins #10 of the Cleveland Browns runs a drill during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 11, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Defense and a great running game. These are Cleveland Browns hallmarks. All of those Marty Schottenheimer teams that played in three AFC Championship Games featured a really good defense with a run game that was difficult to stop. Paul Brown had both with guys like Jim Brown, Ernie Green, Marion Motley, and Bobby Mitchell. RELATED: BREAKING DOWN THE PIN-PULL BLOCKING CONCEPT And now, new Browns head coach Todd Monken is bringing all of this back to the franchise. Monken’s superpower has been taking a stagnant offense and transforming it into one of the best . Oklahoma State went from #88 to #11 in two years. At LSU, his offense began at #42 and finished at #9. With Southern Miss, he inherited an offense ranked #112, and in his third season they were #13. Georgia’s offense struggled nationally at #49 when he was hired, and went to #38, then to #9, and finally #5 with two National Championships. In 2024, the Baltimore Ravens, with Monken as the OC, were ranked #1 offensively. They averaged 424.9 yards per game. Scored 65 touchdowns. The #1 rushing team in the league, averaging 187.6 rushing yards per game and tied for second with 41 rushing TDs. RB Derrick Henry was ranked #2 in the NFL all three years that Monken ran Baltimore’s offense. He had 1,595 yards and 16 touchdowns last year. The year before, Henry busted out for 1,921 yards with another 16 scores, which tied for the league lead. None of this is a coincidence. Monken equals offensive production. And what Monken has already in his stable is Quinshon Judkins. Could Judkins become the league’s new Derrick Henry? Well, okay. Strike that. That’s not a great comparison, after all, Henry is 6’-2”, plus a beefy 252 pounds and runs like a dump truck whose brakes have failed. He is a linebacker holding the ball. Q is 6’-0” and 221 pounds, but he can also bring the wood on running plays. Todd Monken on Quinshon Judkins: “Looked pretty good to me. Obviously, there’s been a couple of days he gets a little sore, which is normal, but no one works harder. And you talk about a competitive spirit, and we don’t even get to see him run. I think his rare trait is he’s a… https://t.co/n6aQyH7iy8 — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) May 20, 2026 But Judkins is going to become the key to this new Browns offense. Monken requires a bellcow to run the ball, and Judkins arrives front and center. He is a beast on his own, but is more like a UPS truck whose brakes have failed. In college, he won the Conerly Trophy for the best college football player in the State of Mississippi while attending Ole Miss. In his one season while at Ohio State, he balled out with 1.567 yards and 16 touchdowns. Judkins addressed the media regarding his return from injury: “I had an offseason to prepare. I feel the same, if not better. Making it through rehab was its own journey.” He brings the mustard with the running game. Monken’s offense is predicated on multiple tight ends, a quarterback who can read a defense and play the short passing game, and a runner who isn’t afraid to lower his head and play catch in the passing game. In training camp so far, he has looked quick and explosive. No signs of his leg and ankle injury from last year. This isn’t knee-related, so both have healed as God intended. Injuries that involve the knee or Achilles are often viewed as ones that can take away aspects of a running back’s true abilities, such as being able to cut, accelerate, and decelerate. Judkins addressed his rehab from his injuries: “I spent a lot of the offseason just trying to be consistent day in and day out, just putting myself and preparing myself for this type of situation where I had to physically be available. At the same time, to just putting a lot of stress on my body so that when I came back, I was ready. Just fortunate with our staff here and every day attacking rehab. I feel good.” Judkins is one of those guys who can be a solid back in the league, and then again, he can bust out and be a Top-5 back. This will be determined by plenty of things. For one, the offensive line. If OT Dawand Jones does not start in Week 1, this would mean all of Cleveland’s starting five along the offensive line from last season have been replaced. Has any NFL team replaced their entire offensive line from one year to the next? Ever? Judkins has seen firsthand the offensive line’s transformation for better or worse: “I think we have a great group of guys up front. So, all of my belief is in them and our coaches. Physically, we will be able to do what we’ve always done. The mindset and mentality as a team is going to carry us over the top. These guys are really physical. They’re smart football players and have a lot of experience. Playing with them is just a natural connection. They communicate well.” An offensive line is not five individuals, but one group. They have to gel and get acclimated to each other and work as one common unit. Especially along the interior, where the center and both guards need to work off of each other and know where their counterpart will be in certain situations, such as stunts. Another situation is the fact that this is a new offense. Not every player will be on the same learning curve as others. Monken requires a lot of pin-pull and trap plays to be successful. This offense has been described as a sophisticated attacking system with heavy formation manipulation. None of this happens overnight. Still, again, an aid to the running game is a successful passing attack. The QB situation with the Browns is widely known as a huge question mark. There are plenty of new faces in the receiver and tight end rooms. That is a ton of new equations that must be deciphered every week. Love you too pic.twitter.com/Gplb391hl1 — CEO (@CEOtkhn) October 21, 2025 Judkins didn’t have much of an opinion on which quarterback should be the starter: “For me, I just embrace it. Because each and every one of those guys is different and talented in their own different ways. I can tailor my game by just how they play and how they communicate.” It is not a huge ask for Judkins to have a 1,200-yard season in 17 games. However, Monken’s offense has goals of at least 1,500 yards for his main back and another 500-600 yards for his secondary runner. In his rookie year, he was used sparingly in the short passing game with just 36 targets, 26 receptions, and 171 yards. Those numbers are about to explode. Monken is a good play caller and has shown he can adapt. Now, his blocking needs work. Judkins’ goals for the year? “I don’t try to put pressure on myself by saying I want to do certain things. It’s just really going out there and competing, taking it one day at a time, and going out there and accomplishing my team goals. As a competitor, you definitely want to be the best you can. And that’s what our goal is – to be the best.” Then there is the part where Monken coached Derrick Henry while he ran the offensive side of the Ravens. In three consecutive seasons under Monken, Henry ranked #2 in the league, and in 2024 he almost eclipsed that sacred 2,000-yard-in-a-season mark. Has Judkins even entertained the notion that he might become the next running back stud in the league? “I remember Coach Monken when I was in college (at Ole Miss), and he was with Georgia. I just remember how they ran the ball, and it was just like, man. That’s a super smart guy. And the way that everybody does everything up front, and the way that he uses the scheme. For me, I’m just excited to be in this offense and just do what I do. Training is the key.” So, let the games begin. And perhaps during the Monken era, the Browns fanbase just might include Q in that registry of famous Browns running backs such as Leroy…

full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 09: Parker Brailsford #52 of the Cleveland Browns runs a drill during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 09, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images With many decisions to be made over the coming weeks, the preseason matchups will help the Cleveland Browns gain clarity on what they want to do this upcoming season. Head Coach Todd Monken will be able to use these games to evaluate and gather information across the roster to inform decisions for the start of the year. When it comes to the roster, which players in particular stand to benefit most from these preseason snaps? Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders both have a lot to prove this preseason. It has been confirmed that Watson will start against the Chicago Bears, while Sanders will get the nod against the Buffalo Bills. If either quarterback can clearly separate themselves from the competition and consistently perform well, they could earn the starting job for the regular season. They will need to make every opportunity count. The Browns’ offensive line looks very different this year , and there will be some big decisions to make, including at Center. Cleveland’s 5th-round pick, Parker Brailsford , is likely to start as the backup behind Elgton Jenkins ; however, nothing is set in stone. Brailsford has been dealing with a wrist injury, but if he can get healthy and put together some impressive performances in the preseason, he could compete for the starting role or, at the very least, secure the number 2 spot over Luke Wypler . The line in general needs some time to gel, while the defense could benefit from a chance to go against offenses with some high-level QB play and consistent time together. While winning preseason games doesn’t carry much weight, this will be a crucial period for a team undergoing significant transition to begin making important decisions about its future. title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 30
summary: It is Day 30 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: UNDATED: Roger Staubach #12 of the Dallas Cowboys talks to a Minnesota Vikings' player during a game circa 1970. (Photo by Focus on Sport via Getty Images) | Focus on Sport via Getty Images It is Day 30 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Welcome in for Day 30 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit the playoff victory that sent the Cowboys one step closer to the first Super Bowl championship in franchise history. Dallas travelled to face a Minnesota team that had won eight straight games to close the regular season, but Tom Landry’s veteran squad looked to deliver one of its most complete defensive performances. Saturday, December 25, 1971 Metropolitan Stadium, Bloomington, Minnesota Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 20, Minnesota Vikings 12 The Vikings entered the postseason with plenty of momentum, led by quarterback Gary Cuozzo, a physical rushing attack and the famous Purple People Eaters defense. Minnesota looked like a legitimate championship contender and Dallas had spent years falling just short in the playoffs, but arrived determined to prove it could finally finish the job. Dallas’s first opportunity came when Larry Cole forced Dave Osborn to fumble, which Jethro Pugh recovered at the Minnesota 36-yard line. Roger Staubach then completed an 18-yard pass to Bob Hayes, but Page’s third-down sack halted the drive. Mike Clark kicked a 26-yard field goal, but Fred Cox responded with a 27-yard field goal to tie the score at 3-3. Chuck Howley intercepted Bob Lee, returning the ball 26 yards into Minnesota territory and giving the Cowboys the lead. Despite failing to score, Clark converted a 44-yard field goal for a 6-3 halftime advantage. However, Minnesota squandered excellent field position after Clint Jones’ 61-yard kickoff return, with three incompletions followed by Cox missing a 41-yard field goal. The decisive separation arrived immediately after halftime. Cliff Harris intercepted Lee and returned the ball 30 yards to the Minnesota 13-yard line. Duane Thomas scored on the next play, giving Dallas a 13-3 lead without requiring the offense to manufacture a long drive against Minnesota’s defensive front. Dallas’s best sustained possession of the second half came later. Charlie Waters returned a punt 24 yards, setting up Staubach’s third-and-15 conversion. Staubach completed a 30-yard pass to Lance Alworth, and Hayes grabbed a nine-yard touchdown to extend the Cowboys’ lead to 20-3. Minnesota’s danger continued into the fourth quarter. Page sacked Staubach in the end zone for a safety, and Gary Cuozzo replaced Lee after the free kick. Cuozzo moved the Vikings deep into Dallas territory, but Lee Roy Jordan intercepted him at the 10-yard line, preventing a comeback before it could gain momentum. Cuozzo eventually connected with Stu Voigt for a six-yard touchdown with a little more than two minutes remaining, reducing the margin to 20-12. The late score made the finish appear closer, but Dallas recovered the onside kick and protected the lead. This game belongs on the countdown because it showed the adaptability of the team that would finally win the championship. Dallas could not overwhelm the Purple People Eaters with yardage, so it relied on field position, ball security and its own opportunistic defense. The Cowboys played patiently, punished Minnesota’s errors and created enough separation before the Vikings’ late rally. #Cowboys vs #Vikings 1971 Divisional Round Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 20, Minnesota Vikings 12 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/5shIuKGSBu — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 14, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game The Cowboys held Minnesota to only one field goal through the first three quarters and never allowed the Vikings offense to settle into the game. title: Shavon Revel is stacking days on days at Cowboys camp
summary: There is one name in the Dallas Cowboys secondary that is starting to become impossible to ignore for his consistent play, and that name is second-year cornerback Shavon Revel Jr. Revel is healthy and living up to the first-round potential he had as a prospect out of Eastern Carolina in the 2025 draft, where his […]
full_text: There is one name in the Dallas Cowboys secondary that is starting to become impossible to ignore for his consistent play, and that name is second-year cornerback Shavon Revel Jr. Revel is healthy and living up to the first-round potential he had as a prospect out of Eastern Carolina in the 2025 draft, where his injury history allowed the Cowboys to draft him in the third round. Revel is not only enjoying being a full participant in Cowboys training camp in Oxnard for the first time, but like the rest of the defense and secondary in particular, getting this fresh start under the tutelage of new defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Parker arrived at his first DC job with the Cowboys as a known commodity when it came to quickly developing cornerback talent and getting them to play well within the greater Vic Fangio-styled defensive scheme. The names often associated with this have much higher draft pedigree than Revel, though. In Parker’s first job as a position coach in the NFL, with the Denver Broncos in 2021, they drafted Patrick Surtain in the first round. When Parker left for the Philadelphia Eagles in 2024, they double-dipped at cornerback in the first round with CBs Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean. Parker’s first pick with the Cowboys was obviously Caleb Downs this April, which remains highly exciting as Downs has made an impact right away too. Parker didn’t draft Revel, but the excitement is that his 2025 season was enough of a wash to almost make this a rookie redo – under significantly better circumstances all around – for the talented corner. It’s like a bonus pick for Parker that’s paying off beautifully. Watching that dreadful ‘25 Cowboys defense, it didn’t feel like there was any solution to move forward with if this defense was going to improve quickly. On the eve of the Cowboys first preseason test of 2026, we’re now living in a world where undrafted free agent carryovers like Justin Barron are making plays at linebacker, Julius Wood and Alijah Clark are doing the same at safety, and Revel has the overall situation at cornerback looking up. It looks even better when it comes to the situation Revel is in on the CB depth chart. The Cowboys are also seeing trade chip Cobie Durant play well in his first offseason work with the team, as well as a healthy DaRon Bland. Throw in Downs’ ability to stick to receivers in man coverage like a natural cornerback too, and no individual player here is being asked to do too much. The Cowboys team drills have seen Revel matched up against CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, and Ryan Flournoy, the entire big three expected to do huge things for the pass offense at wide receiver. Not only have all three been proven playmakers in the past, but they are all different body types with different skill sets, yet the consistent results have been the same when matched up against Revel – fluid coverage and great contest at the catch point. George Pickens wanted a flag on this Shavon Revel PBU. Didn’t get one. pic.twitter.com/BRY99xFXRQ — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) August 13, 2026 This buzz for Revel grew even more after the Cowboys scrimmaged the Rams in a joint practice on Wednesday. The L.A. offense threw all of their shiftiness, speed, and burst at Revel, and yet again he won enough matchups to turn heads. Shavon Revel having a great day. Playing physical. Forced a fumble and has had two big PBUs on plays where the Rams were clearly testing him. One on a downfield ball to Nacua, another on a fade from the 10-yard line to Nacua. Hasn’t been perfect but it’s been his best day in… — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 11, 2026 Dallas was right back to work on Thursday with a practice in shells, and Revel kept on stacking great reps. Playing with an even keel, trusting his athleticism and instincts, and competing for the ball on every play seem to be positive traits of Revel’s, and all things Parker can help him maximize as his scheme takes full focus going into the regular season. Regardless of scheme, cornerbacks that can match up in man coverage from both the outside or slot are valuable anywhere in today’s NFL, and the Cowboys may have their latest star in this regard with Revel. Cowboys CB Shavon Revel continues to have a strong camp pic.twitter.com/PWaGpTaorR — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) August 13, 2026 The Cowboys turning Revel into a plus player would also be yet another tangible thing to point to when explaining just how different this offseason really has been around Dallas. Second- or third-round draft risks (mainly on defense) with injury red flags used to be common place for this front office, without a high batting average of actually seeing these risks pay off. The team is expected to play both of this year’s first-round picks, Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence, in the preseason opener at the Seahawks, and last year’s top-1oo picks on defense Donovan Ezeiruaku and Shavon Revel should get some run as well. With Revel being the biggest question mark of this group, and maybe the whole roster at points this offseason, the Cowboys seeing him establish himself as a potential face to this defensive rebuild among so much other young talent to be excited about is amazing news. Cowboys CB Shavon Revel on guarding Rams wide receivers during their joint practice: “That felt easy because I’ve been doing it every day against — in my opinion, personally — the best receivers in the league [Lamb and Pickens] and I felt that throughout this camp.” ( @JoeJHoyt ) pic.twitter.com/LGUG6ZQL0K — SleeperCowboys (@SleeperCowboys) August 13, 2026 Revel will go into Saturday’s game listed as a starter with an “or” designation alongside Durant, based on the team’s first unofficial depth chart released on Tuesday this week. With Durant being the veteran that may not need as many live reps, and Revel still needing all the full-speed game action he can get, Revel is in position to do quite a lot to inch his name further up the chart to clear starter, based on everything he’s done in camp on a daily basis to this very point. Cornerback Competition Seeing Shavon Revel edge out Cobie Durant is exciting, and that’s because the veteran Durant has genuinely impressed in camp, so this speaks volumes about the incredible progress the second-year corner has made over the last couple of weeks. But to be clear, this is another one of their “or” labels, meaning that second boundary corner gig is firmly up for grabs. Caleb Downs should've been a Top 8 pick. Shavon Revel Jr. would've been a Top 15 pick. Donovan Ezeiruaku could've been a Day 1 pick. Three defensive studs. Three steals. And now they reap the rewards. pic.twitter.com/H44ojge661 — Dan Rogers (@DannyPhantom24) August 13, 2026

title: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer and the proverbial hot seat
summary: If a team starts off the season on the wrong foot and wants to reverse its fortunes, there aren’t too many options available for that front office. Can’t cut all the players on the roster, can’t draft new players, can’t even fire the GM if he happens to be the owner of the team, and […]
full_text: Jan 27, 2025; Frisco, TX, USA; (L to R) Dallas Cowboys CEO Stephen Jones, head coach Brian Schottenheimer and owner Jerry Jones speak to the media at a press conference at the Star. Mandatory Credit: Tim Heitman-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con If a team starts off the season on the wrong foot and wants to reverse its fortunes, there aren’t too many options available for that front office. Can’t cut all the players on the roster, can’t draft new players, can’t even fire the GM if he happens to be the owner of the team, and certainly can’t swap out the existing fan base for a kinder, gentler one. But you can fire the head coach. If recent history is anything to go by, there will be a couple of mid-season coaching changes this season, just as there will be coaching changes after the season. And the sportsbooks are already getting jumpy. Betonline, for example, has running odds on which head coach will be fired first during the 2026 regular season, and Schottenheimer makes the top seven: Dan Quinn (3/1) Todd Bowles (7/2) Aaron Glenn (8/1) Zac Taylor (9/1) Shane Steichen (9/1) Nick Sirianni (12/1) Brian Schottenheimer (16/1) Expectations are always high in Dallas, and the basic reality is that being on the hot seat is pretty much par for the course for a Cowboys head coach because: A. he’s not winning the Super Bowl every year, and B. he works for Jerry Jones. Last year, the defense provided a convenient excuse for a disappointing 7-9-1 performance, and Matt Eberflus turned out to be a super-convenient scapegoat for a defensive mess that the Cowboys created, in part, by their own personnel choices across the defense. I’m always wary of using tired old clichés like “ Jerry Jones has an itchy trigger finger” , but Jones is not getting any younger, and he may not have the patience to sit through another disappointing year, especially if the Cowboys get off to yet another slow start. Yes, we know that Jones has never fired a head coach after less than two seasons, but trying to predict what Jones will do based on past behavior is almost always a fool’s errand. Remember how Jones had never fired a coach mid-season – until he fired Wade Phillips after Week 10 in 2010. Or remember how “not even Jimmy Johnson lasted for more than four years” in Dallas – until Jason “8-8” Garrett more than doubled that in his nine-and-a-half-year tenure as head coach in Dallas. What Schottenheimer needs to do to keep his job in 2026 A lot of the things that Schottenheimer has done so far “feel right”. Of course, they also felt right at this time last year, but that 7-9-1 record did not “feel right” at all, regardless of any extenuating circumstances. The fact is that success in the NFL is judged solely by the W/L column. Everything else is just icing on the cake. On the plus side, the Cowboys have invested heavily in the team, as the graph below shows, so at least they are putting their money where their mouth is, even if that further increases the pressure on Schottenheimer to deliver. NFL Team Cash and Salary Cap spending for 2026 heading into training camp, including dead money. Top left quadrant are the higher Cash over Cap spending teams. pic.twitter.com/c8MymwM0zt — Troy_OTC (@TexansCap) July 17, 2026 The Cowboys aren’t behaving like a team that’s rebuilding. They’re spending like a team that expects to compete now. That doesn’t mean Schottenheimer needs to win the Super Bowl, but it does make another season of “we’re almost there” increasingly difficult to sell. And there seems to be a palpable sense of urgency in Dallas. “ This is as urgent as I’ve ever felt Jerry ,” Prescott told Jori Epstein of Yahoo Sports during a sit-down interview earlier this week. “Sure, there’s times he’s said it, and then we’ve looked up and he hadn’t done much in free agency. Or this, this and that. But starting from free agency, they started doing things they hadn’t done. And it’s kudos to Schotty and Will and the whole team, but it’s also Jerry making that decision of being aggressive and trying to go out and get what he wants.” Some believe Schottenheimer must make the playoffs to keep Jones happy. Others believe the Cowboys must win at least one playoff game. Others believe that simply winning a lowly wild-card game won’t be enough, that it must be at least a divisional-round win, perhaps even a conference championship. The Cowboys themselves are openly talking about the Super Bowl, and frankly, I have no idea what to make of that coming from a 7-9-1 team. My guess? Schottenheimer doesn’t need to reach the Super Bowl to keep his job. But after going 7-9-1 in his first season, another year without meaningful January football would make it very difficult for Jerry Jones to argue that the team is heading in the right direction. A playoff appearance probably keeps him around – if only because of the organizational inertia the Cowboys tend to display. A playoff win should make his position considerably safer. Anything less, particularly if the Cowboys stumble out of the gate again, could put Jones in a very different frame of mind. So where’s your line in the sand? What does Schottenheimer need to deliver in 2026 to keep his job?

title: Determining how many new starters Dallas Cowboys will have in 2026
summary: The Dallas Cowboys recently released their first unofficial depth chart of the year after the scrimmage with the Los Angeles Rams. This is the first breadcrumb the team has given as to how they plan on potentially shaping this year’s 53-man roster. It also provides clarity as to how many new starters they may have […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys recently released their first unofficial depth chart of the year after the scrimmage with the Los Angeles Rams. This is the first breadcrumb the team has given as to how they plan on potentially shaping this year’s 53-man roster. It also provides clarity as to how many new starters they may have in 2026. Cowboys’ first unofficial depth chart pic.twitter.com/4q9ZfMSjH4 — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) August 11, 2026 Offensively, things will look much the same as they did a season ago. The Cowboys were able to retain all of their starters from last year after re-signing RB Javonte Williams and using the franchise tag to retain WR George Pickens’ services. There are some depth issues that need to be sorted out, but overall this is a talented and dangerous offense, one of the best in the league. The defensive side of the ball is an entirely different story. After having one of the worst defensive units in 2025, and one of the worst in the organization’s history, the Cowboys decided to pretty much wipe the slate clean. From Christian Parker and his coaching staff to the personnel, this group will look much different from a season ago and hopefully be much more productive. According to the first unofficial depth chart, it’s conceivable to see the Cowboys new-look 3-4 defense feature more than a half-dozen new starters this year. From the defensive front to the back end of the secondary each position has at least one new starter, others potentially more than one. New projected defensive starters DT Otito Ogbonnia OLB Rashan Gary LB DeMarvion Overshown LB Dee Winters CB Cobie Durant* CB Shavon Revel* DB Caleb Downs S Jalen Thompson *currently battling for the starting job Ogbonnia and Gary immediately upgrade Dallas’ run defense, with the latter hopefully improving their pass rush as well. Overshown and Winters should both be upgrade linebacker from a season ago and Durant/Revel, whichever ends up starting, along with Thompson and Downs should all be significant upgrades on the backend of the Cowboys secondary. There is one name to watch who could still be competing for a starting job. Rookie LB Jaishawn Barham is someone to keep an eye on. He is currently dealing with a groin injury that isn’t considered serious, but prior to that his name was on everybody’s lips as someone who is standing out in practice as a run defender and in pass coverage. All in all, from Christian Parker and his new coaching staff to the new additions to the roster, especially the starting ones, early returns about the Cowboys new-look defense are mostly of the positive nature. They performed much better than expected in the scrimmage with the Rams and hope to do the same against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 1 of preseason. Barring some unforeseen trade, although there’s quite a bit of talk that Jerry Jones and Company are exploring that avenue, we foresee the Cowboys having a total of seven new starters once a decision is made about Cobie Durant and Shavon Revel. And yes, we’re also including rookie Caleb Downs in that projection. Offensively we know what to expect from Dallas’ starters. They will once again be one of the more dangerous and feared units in the league. Defensively though, the jury is still out. They’ve had a lot of turnover on that side of the ball with numerous new starters, however, all signs point to them being much improved throughout the defense.

The two teams converged for a joint practice, and Cowboys fans have a lot to be excited about, even if it was barely a scrimmage. Hasn’t been perfect but it’s been his best day in… — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 11, 2026 Quinnen was this disruptive throughout the practice. Of all the things we expect CP to supercharge, I can’t overstate how much I expect Q to shine…I’m talking career year. https://t.co/MYUT9mCrDk — Derek Eagleton (@derekeagleton) August 12, 2026 . @justinbarron22 with the INT❗️ #CowboysCamp | @AmericanAir pic.twitter.com/dKkLyEayHt — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 11, 2026 Cowboys linebacker Justin Barron had three INTs, one from Rams QB Matthew Stafford and two from backup Stetson Bennett. As for the rest of the Cowboys, Dallas not only was able to hang with the Rams, who are once again Super Bowl favorites, but, as you just saw, was able to get the better of them in some cases. Offense needs to work on one area By all indications, Dallas was able to move the ball some on offense. WR George Pickens made some plays, and QB Dak Prescott had some impressive plays of his own. One was a nice completion to TE Brevyn Spann-Ford, the other was an escape out of the pocket for a touchdown. Brian Schottenheimer even said the team was better in the redzone on offense. But there were reports that the Cowboys struggled to open up their run game in the practice. It was also noted that Terence Steele had a lot of problems with the Rams pass rush. So there are things to be worked on. It’s way too early to say the Cowboys are on par with the Rams. Dallas has a ton to prove in the upcoming weeks. The Rams just have to play at the level they’re capable of, and they could very well be in the Super Bowl again. Either way, this practice looked a lot different last year, and the change in intensity, focus and success on the field is obviously a welcome one. title: Predicting which WRs make Cowboys 53-man roster
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are fortunate in that they should once again be one of the best offensive units in the entire league with all of their starters still intact from a season ago. This is one of the more talented units in the NFL, headlined by their impressive group of wide receivers. The Cowboys have […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys are fortunate in that they should once again be one of the best offensive units in the entire league with all of their starters still intact from a season ago. This is one of the more talented units in the NFL, headlined by their impressive group of wide receivers. The Cowboys have a dream WR duo in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens and some promising depth behind them. The only question about this position group is how many receivers Dallas will carry on the active roster and which ones will make the cut? Below is how we see things shaking out and why. What we know… There’s no need to guesstimate which wide receivers are currently roster locks with the Dallas Cowboys. They are currently four deep with CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Ryan Flournoy, and Kavontae Turpin, with Flournoy as the only one of the group without a Pro Bowl appearance. This group is highlighted by Lamb and Pickens, arguably the best WR duo in the entire league, leaving Flournoy as their primary backup and Turpin as Dallas’ return specialist/gadget player. This is a WR core that will make nearly every team around the league envious and give opposing defensive coordinators nightmares. Lamb and Pickens should both easily hit the 1000-yard receiving mark once again in 2026 and Flournoy should have a career year facing favorable matchups due to the attention No. 88 and No. 3 will command. Turpin will be sprinkled in time to time on offense, but his value remains on special teams. How will Dallas round out the rest of the position? What we suspect… The biggest question we need answered about the Cowboys WR position is how many they will carry on the 53-man roster. We’re guessing there will only be one spot up for grabs, but they could possibly carry as many as six. Due to the uncertain depth at other positions and the current top-heavy nature of the position, we believe they will choose to go little short here carrying only five on the active roster. So, which receiver currently on the Cowboys roster claims that final spot on the depth chart? There are a number of veterans currently in contention for the WR5 job as well as some first- and second-year WRs. There’s still a lot of training camp and preseason to go before things need to be finalized, but the WR with the most special teams ability may give them the slight edge to round out the Cowboys WR position. Final prediction As things stand right now, based on what we’ve seen/heard in training camp, we believe the final WR roster spot will go to either Anthony Smith or Camden Brown, both rookies. Smith was a seventh-round pick out of East Carolina this year and Brown signed with the Cowboys as an undrafted free agent out of Georgia Southern. Both WRs have stood out in practice, creating an intriguing head-to-head battle. Under the assumption the Cowboys only keep five receivers on the active roster, we believe Anthony Smith earns the WR5 job. His deep threat ability and the way he’s been used in a variety of ways in practice at training camp gives him the slight edge over his competitors. He will of course have to prove his value on special teams, a must for fringe players on the Cowboys roster. Cowboys 2026 WR depth chart prediction CeeDee Lamb George Pickens Ryan Flournoy KaVontae Turpin Anthony Smith (R) Agree or disagree? Will the Cowboys carry five or more WRs and who earns the final roster spot?

title: Cowboys news: Jerry Jones talks Parsons trade, current defense
summary: Ahead of the Cowboys first preseason game, reports are starting to surface about some of the defensive starters getting some playing time over the course of the Cowboys three preseason games. With Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence headlining those conversations, Cowboys fans should expect to see both play in some capacity over the next three […]
full_text: OXNARD, CA - JULY 28: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones listens as head coach Brian Schottenheimer answers a question during an opening press conference at training camp on Tuesday, July 28, 2026, in Oxnard, Calif. (Smiley N. Pool/The Dallas Morning News via Getty Images) Ahead of the Cowboys first preseason game, reports are starting to surface about some of the defensive starters getting some playing time over the course of the Cowboys three preseason games. With Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence headlining those conversations, Cowboys fans should expect to see both play in some capacity over the next three weeks. And Jerry Jones discusses the big trade from last offseason and how it has resulted in the Cowboys we see today, especially on defense. Jerry Jones: Very happy with Cowboys post-Micah Parsons trade – Todd Archer, ESPN Roughly a year later, Jerry Jones discusses the big trade of Micah Parsons, the reconstructed defense and more in his latest interview. Jones called Parsons a “great player,” noting his ability enabled the Cowboys to make such a dramatic deal with Green Bay. “Otherwise, we wouldn’t have had the opportunity to make that kind of trade. That’s why it worked,” Jones said. “But the fact that we revamped our defense, that was an instigator toward that attitude: ‘Let’s come in here and change this up, let’s get rush from the interior, let’s be stronger on the run in the interior with an emphasis on those guys in the middle.’ That’s not an accident. That that’s what you see out there from the inside.” Dallas Cowboys Reveal Preseason Plan For Caleb Downs, Malachi Lawrence – Josh Sanchez, SI.com A big question heading into the Cowboys first preseason game was if Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence would get any snaps in the preseason game action. Tommy Yarrish reports both could get “a little bit” of run over the next three weeks. Both Downs and Lawrence have been impressive during the first few weeks of training camp, so it would be nice to see how the rookies perform in their first taste of NFL action. But because the players are expected to be contributors this season, we may only get a glimpse. According to Cowboys insider Tommy Yarrish, Schottenheimer expects the first-round picks to “play a little bit.” As for who else will get a look during the preseason as the team works its way down to a 53-man roster, that plan is still being developed. Practice Points: Notes from final practice before 1st preseason game – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys are used to having a young wide receiver breakout during training camp. This year is seems like Georgia Southern UDFA Camden Brown is just that guy. Can he carry it into the preseason to win the WR5 job? Camden’s Climb: Undrafted free agent wide receiver Camden Brown is continuing to put together a strong camp, and was rewarded for it on Thursday by getting a few snaps with the first-team offense and his first reception from Dak Prescott. In his work with the second and third team offenses, Brown has been a consistent contributor, especially in the red zone where he’s caught several touchdowns since camp began. — (Tommy Yarrish) With his confidence back, Shavon Revel Jr. now growing into CB the Cowboys hoped he could be – Joseph Hoyt, The Dallas Morning News After a disappointing rookie season, second-year CB Shavon Revel Jr. is ready to breakout in year two. Can he squeak his way into the starting limeup? Cowboys cornerback Shavon Revel Jr. had a realization during Tuesday’s joint practice with the Rams that you probably wouldn’t expect, given his competition. The tandem of Davante Adams and Puka Nacua have earned their label as one of the league’s best. That should be enough to concern any opposing corner. But not Revel. “That felt easy,” Revel said of going up against the Rams receivers, “because I’ve been doing it every day against — in my opinion, personally — the best receivers in the league and I felt that throughout this camp.” The Dallas Cowboys preseason should finally give us some answers on the most mysterious roster battle going on – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports The Cowboys defense is getting a lot of the focus in this year’s training camp. But don’t forget about this position battle going on, on the offensive side of the ball. We’re closing in on three weeks of training camp and the truth is we haven’t found much about the bottom-half of the Dallas Cowboys wide receiver room. Sure, we know about the top-end. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are cooking. Ryan Flournoy is solidified himself as WR3 and KaVontae Turpin is once again a part of the offense, albeit in a limited role. But the Cowboys are surely carrying a fifth wide receiver and maybe even a sixth. But we have yet to see anyone truly separate from the rest of the pack. Three preseason games, starting Saturday night against the Seattle Seahawks, should provide more clarity. Below is a breakdown of the position right now. See which Cowboys player Jerry Jones says has surprised him at training camp – Calvin Watkins, The Dallas Morning News Jerry Jones gives praise to Tyler Guyton ahead of preseason game one. Guyton taking the next step (and staying healthy) would be huge for the Cowboys 2026 success. Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones mentioned one name when asked if any players had surprised him at training camp : Tyler Guyton. The Cowboys left tackle started training camp in a battle with Nate Thomas for the starting job. But Guyton has emerged as the starter 10 practices into training camp. “I really like Guyton,” Jones said after Thursday’s practice. “Guyton is really, I think being where at the level of competition that we had hoped for with him. That’s a plus. That’s a plus.” Cowboys LB Jaishawn Barham is close to returning from groin injury – Matthew Lenix, Blogging the Boys Rookie LB Jaishawn Barham has been a star of training camp so far, but a recent groin injury has had him sidelined for the last week. How close is he to getting back on the field? Rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham is currently dealing with an groin issue that began last week. Luckily, it’s not something serious that will keep the third-round pick from missing any significant action. Some great news came about in regards to his status on Thursday. Barham is close to being cleared from his groin injury. Could he play versus the Seattle Seahawks in the Cowboys’ preseason opener on Saturday? Maybe. Daily discussion question: How are you watching the preseason game? With others? Yourself? What’s going down?

title: Sean Payton was pleased with the Broncos’ run game vs. Falcons
summary: The Denver Broncos looked impressive throughout most of the 27-7 preseason win over the Atlanta Falcons outside a couple of special teams miscues. The best aspect to that win could be the underrated run game. Denver outgained the Falcons by over 100 yards on the ground and that was something that head coach Sean Payton […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - AUGUST 14: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos rushes against DeMarcco Hellams #23, Ja'quan McMillian #29 and Nate Adkins #45 of the Denver Broncos during the first quarter of a NFL preseason game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos looked impressive throughout most of the 27-7 preseason win over the Atlanta Falcons outside a couple of special teams miscues. The best aspect to that win could be the underrated run game. Denver outgained the Falcons by over 100 yards on the ground and that was something that head coach Sean Payton was happy about afterwards. “I was pleased with that,” Payton said. “I thought the runners played well and I thought we blocked them pretty well. It’s kind of a heavy front; they’ll play some base. I know we had one fumble, but those guys ran hard.” The player that impressed me the most on the night was rookie Jonah Coleman. His first two carries were a bit disappointing, but after that he was the best runner of the night for the Broncos. His first two carries went for four yards, but his last two went for 20. Coleman has had a good camp and Payton backed that up when asked about his impressions of Coleman during the game. “Just what we’ve been seeing, right? And then you see enough of it, and you’re like, all right. Look, he’s had a good camp, and I liked his balance coming out of some of the tackles. I thought overall, the group had a good night.” His ability to avoid going down with first contact is something he was known for in college and we saw more of that in his runs on Friday night. JK Dobbins is your clear starter this year, but Coleman had himself a good first showing for us fans. It would be good for the team to have hit pay dirt on a midround pick like Jonah. What were your impressions of the Broncos’ run game last night? Horse Tracks

title: Winners and Losers from the Denver Broncos’ 27-7 victory over the Atlanta Falcons
summary: No Bo Nix or Jaylen Waddle, no problem. The Denver Broncos opened their preseason on fire and dominated the Atlanta Falcons throughout tonight’s game. They had a 24-0 lead at halftime and had contributions from both their offense and defense during the first half. Things slowed down a bit in the second half, but the […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - AUGUST 14: Jarrett Stidham #8 of the Denver Broncos reacts after a rushing touchdown by Adam Prentice #46 against the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter of a NFL preseason game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images No Bo Nix or Jaylen Waddle, no problem. The Denver Broncos opened their preseason on fire and dominated the Atlanta Falcons throughout tonight’s game. They had a 24-0 lead at halftime and had contributions from both their offense and defense during the first half. Things slowed down a bit in the second half, but the Broncos held the lead and improved to 1-0 in the preseason. We have plenty of winners from this game, including 2025 1st-round pick Jahdae Barron and backup quarterback Jarrett Stidham, with a handful of players leaving this game as losers. So, with all that said, here are my winners and losers from the Denver Broncos 27-7 victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 1 of the preseason. WINNER – QB Jarrett Stidham Entering tonight’s game, there was talk about a potential competition for the backup quarterback between veteran Jarrett Stidham and third-stringer Sam Ehlinger. Well, that talk will quiet down a bit after tonight due to Stidham outplaying Ehlinger and leading the offense to multiple touchdowns. Stiddy finished the night going 9 for 15 for 131 yards and 1 touchdown. He had a 40-yard throw to Courtland Sutton that led to an Adam Prentice 1-yard touchdown and later had a touchdown throw to Jaleel McLaughlin Stiddy throws a 40 yard BOMB to Courtland Sutton pic.twitter.com/9jXL3719rt — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 14, 2026 He looked like the better quarterback tonight. Plain and simple. Now, Ehlinger was playing with the third-team unit while Stidham had the starters and backups, but still. Ehlinger needed to outplay Stidham by a wide margin for this to be a conversation, and that simply did not happen. I would anticipate Stidham being the backup come Week 1, but I believe Ehlinger may get his time with the 2’s next week vs. the Packers, but we shall see what happens there. LOSER – QB Sam Ehlinger I already talked about him, but Sam Ehlinger’s quest to become the Broncos’ backup quarterback probably ended tonight. Stidham played well while Ehlinger struggled to get much going with the Broncos ‘ third-team offense. Now, Ehlinger did not play bad by any means. He finished the night going 10 for 14 for 67 yards with an additional 23 yards rushing. However, he did have a near interception and struggled to get the offense moving consistently in the second half. As I said, he may get run with the second team offense next week, but I think this battle, if there ever was one, is likely over with after tonight’s performance. WINNER – CB Jahdae Barron Jahdae Barron NEEDED a night like tonight. The Broncos 2025 1st-round pick had been a topic of conversation amongst fans and media. He has yet to crack the starting lineup and wasn’t making a ton of noise during training camp. However, that all changed tonight. Barron had a pick-6 touchdown, and unlike his one vs. Pat Mahomes and the Chiefs, this one wasn’t called back by a bogus penalty. JAHDAE BARRON PICK-6 TOUCHDOWN pic.twitter.com/yJ1w9EStjI — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 15, 2026 Even before the pick-6, Barron was playing well. He had a few PBUs, a near second INT, and was active and aggressive in the run game. Again, the type of showing we needed to see from Barron. Hopefully, he can build on this performance, continue to develop and build his confidence, and be a weapon for the Broncos in the secondary LOSER – RB Jaleel McLaughlin This is tough, but Jaleel McLaughlin is a loser for me. Yes, he had a nice touchdown catch and run in the game, but he also fumbled the ball. Nothing will put you in the doghouse quicker as a running back than fumbling the ball. Especially when you’re on the roster bubble and likely on the outside looking in. McLaughlin looked like his usual self tonight, but came in behind RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman, and the fumble likely has not helped his odds of making the team. He briefly left the game due to an injury on special teams, but returned to the game before eventually fumbling the ball. Jaleel is a great story, and I like his work ethic, but he’s going to need to have a strong few weeks if he wants to make the team. WINNER – RB Jonah Coleman Rookie Jonah Coleman proved tonight that he deserves touches early and often this season. He only had 4 carries for 24 yards, but in those limited touches, Coleman showcased a good burst, vision, balance, and power and simply looked like a damn good running back. After the game, head coach Sean Payton told reporters that Coleman has had a good camp and that he liked Coleman’s balance coming out of some of the tackles tonight. Sean Payton told reporters after the Broncos' first preseason game that he was pleased with Jonah Coleman. Said he saw what he's been seeing from Coleman. "He's had a good camp. I liked his balance coming out of some of the tackles" — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 15, 2026 Strictly as a runner, Coleman should be the Broncos’ RB2 and split carries with veteran RJ Harvey. This isn’t a knock on Harvey, who excels in space and in the passing game, but when it comes to running between the tackles, Coleman is far superior, which honestly is not a huge surprise. Coleman didn’t last long in this game either. He entered behind RJ Harvey, who got the start but sat down after a few offensive series for Jaleel McLaughlin and Tyler Badie. That right there shows you that the Broncos have belief in Coleman and his future production with the team this season. LOSER – Broncos reserve special teams Darren Rizzi will not be happy. In the second half, the Broncos had some sloppy special teams play. #Broncos FG unit has been a mess tonight. First the bad snap from Luke Basso. Then Matt Peart ran on late. Wil Lutz re-set his spot but hit a bad ball from 55. In the regular season, there's perhaps a timeout called if it's a big spot. But still. — Parker Gabriel (@ParkerJGabriel) August 15, 2026 Backup long snapper Luke Basso had a botched snap, which led to holder Jeremy Crawshaw having a hard time handling the ball and ended up with Crawshaw running and sliding with the ball. Not what you want from a field goal attempt. Then, on another field goal attempt, kicker Wil Lutz had to rush a 55-yard field goal due to reserve offensive lineman Matt Peart running on the field late When special teams play decides who gets those final few spots on a roster, you cannot have mistakes like this. Basso, who is competing for the long snapper job, cannot afford to have bad snaps. You have one job, and if you cannot do that, your time with the team is likely over. WINNER – FB Adam Prentice The fullback position may be a dying position in the NFL, but with the Denver Broncos, it’s an important piece to their team and offense. Veteran Adam Prentice was productive as the Broncos ‘ short-yardage back in a few instances, including a one-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Not only that, but he led the way for the Broncos’ ball carriers who had success running the ball this evening. What a day for Adam Prentice. He scored a TD on the first drive them got more job security from Sean Payton at halftime. Payton told @cfrelund on @9NEWS : "We believe in the fullback." — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 15, 2026 At halftime, Broncos head coach Sean Payton told reporters that “We believe in the fullback”. Prentice, who originally started his career with the Broncos, spent time with the Saints and would eventually sign with the Broncos last summer, has become a key member of the team. He has been used as a short-yardage runner, pass catcher, pass blocker, and he contributes on special teams. You need players like this on your roster, and Prentice is a good one who the coaches love. WINNER – WR Courtland…

title: Instant reaction: Broncos earn decisive victory over Falcons in preseason opener
summary: The Denver Broncos started off the preseason the right way. When the clock struck zero, the Broncos had notched a decisive 27-7 victory over the Atlanta Falcons. It was abundantly clear who was the better coached team in this one. Here are several instant reactions from their first preseason game. Broncos’ offense looked sharp in […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - AUGUST 14: Denver wide receiver Courtland Sutton (14) reacts during the NFL pre-season game between the Denver Broncos and the Atlanta Falcons on August 14th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Denver Broncos started off the preseason the right way. When the clock struck zero, the Broncos had notched a decisive 27-7 victory over the Atlanta Falcons. It was abundantly clear who was the better coached team in this one. Here are several instant reactions from their first preseason game. First one done ✅ pic.twitter.com/sIhPnswI6C — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) August 15, 2026 Broncos’ offense looked sharp in the first half. One of the key storylines to watch in tonight’s game was how Denver’s offense would perform with Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb calling plays and Jarrett Stidham getting the start. All things considered, I’d say they looked quite good in their first preseason game. The Broncos started out hot with a six-play drive that went 69-yards for a score. That’s exactly the type of execution you want to see. Wide receiver Courtland Sutton impressed early on, hauling in a big 40-yard catch that put the team in scoring position. The first drive would result in a 1-yard touchdown run by fullback Adram Prentice. Overall, I felt Stidham performed well in the first half. He did a good job working different levels of the field. Four different receivers had receptions of at least fifteen yards. He looked sharp with a clean pocket, but had a few errant throws when pressure got to him. Overall, the veteran backup went 9-of-15 for 131 yards and 1 touchdown. The Broncos had a whopping 31 plays on offense in the first half. They averaged nearly seven yards per play and accrued 14 first downs. Their rushing attack was also successful with 17 carries for 94 yards. By the end of the first half, Denver amassed 225 yards of total offense and put 17 points on the board. A beautiful first drive that results in a touchdown! This huge play by Courtland Sutton set up the FB Dive from Adam Prentice for the TD 🔥 #BroncosCountry pic.twitter.com/knkR8303qr — SleeperBroncos (@SleeperBroncos) August 14, 2026 Jonah Coleman’s NFL debut showed some promise, but also one big concern. Rookie running back Jonah Coleman was one of the players I was keyed in on for tonight’s game. The former Washington Huskies standout had six carries in his NFL debut for 24 yards—a six yard per carry average. Personally, I thought he would get more opportunities than that. Even so, his decisiveness and burst at the line of scrimmage was evident. Additionally, his low center of gravity and penchant for breaking tackles stood out. The aforementioned are all reasons why Coleman should be a quality contributor in the Broncos’ rushing attack this season. However, he had several whiffs in pass protection. That’s typically an area that takes young running backs time to get the hang of. Nevertheless, he will need to improve upon that aspect of the game to see more playing time during his rookie season. Denver’s defense reels in a few big turnovers. Finding a way to create more takeaways has been a focal point for the Broncos’ defense this offseason. After being in the bottom five last season with just 14, finding a way to get better in that aspect will be mission critical for sustained success in the regular season. They didn’t disappoint tonight. Cornerbacks Riley Moss and Jahdae Barron both hauled in first half interceptions. Barron, a player I highlighted in my players to watch article, came up big tonight. I was impressed with how he played in the first half. In the right spot at the right time, Barron took a deflected pass by linebacker Karene Reid and returned it the distance for a 97-yard pick six. That play kept the Falcons off the board and put the Broncos up 24-0 near the end of the first half. It’s still unknown what kind of snap share Barron will have this season, but if he continues to make plays like that—Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph may have a hard time keeping him off the field. Jahdae Barron takes it 98 yards to the house! 🏠 He reached a max speed of 21.15 mph on this pick-6, per @NextGenStats Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ixw9rzbhCj — NFL+ (@NFLPlus) August 15, 2026 Miscellaneous thoughts and observations. Is there actually a real competition at backup quarterback? Several reports mentioned how Sam Ehlinger has been on par, if not better than Stidham during training camp. While they had different units and tiers of talent playing with them, Stidham certainly looked much better in tonight’s game. Sure, there is still time to go, but I’d wager the thought of the battle being close may have been slightly exaggerated. It’s definitely not time to hit the panic button, but the two snafus on the Broncos’ field goal units tonight were concerning. On numerous occasions last year, the special teams had execution problems. Special Teams Coach Darren Rizzi will need to work out those kinks before the regular season begins. Denver can’t afford to have those mistakes when the stakes actually matter. One of the big camp battles for the Broncos is at inside linebacker. Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad are the starting duo, but who will wind up backing them up remains to be seen. Based off tonight’s performance, seventh-round draft selection Red Murdock may have an inside track for one of the spots. He played a lot of snaps and had 7 tackles tonight. I thought he played well moving downhill and did a great job diagnosing plays against the run.

title: 2026 preseason: Denver Broncos vs. Atlanta Falcons final score
summary: The Denver Broncos kicked off their preseason on the road against the Atlanta Falcons. Starters were projected to play just 10-15 plays with Jarrett Stidham at the helm and that is about how it went. Though the defense was so good with their first team that they ended up playing four series and still came […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - AUGUST 14: Courtland Sutton #14 of the Denver Broncos reacts after a reception during the first quarter against the Atlanta Falcons in an NFL preseason game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos kicked off their preseason on the road against the Atlanta Falcons. Starters were projected to play just 10-15 plays with Jarrett Stidham at the helm and that is about how it went. Though the defense was so good with their first team that they ended up playing four series and still came in under 15 total plays, while the offense ended up getting just three drives and played a bit more than 15. The result was a blowout first half by Denver with the offense putting up three scoring drives and the defense stuffing the Falcons offense. Jahdae Barron would also add a 97-yard interception return for a touchdown. Things got a bit quiet in the second half, but we should be pleased with the performance of the first and second team units in this first preseason game. Bring on Bo Nix next week! Broncos vs. Falcons final score Team 1st 2nd 3rd 4th Final Denver Broncos 7 17 0 3 27 Atlanta Falcons 0 0 7 0 7 First Quarter Stidham and the Broncos took the field to start the game and he immediately found Pat Bryant for a quick 15 yards to kickstart their drive. RJ Harvey picked up four on the next play, then a quick slant to Courtland Sutton brought up a third and short that was picked up by fullback Adam Prentice to move Denver across midfield on their opening drive. Stiddy throws a 40 yard BOMB to Courtland Sutton pic.twitter.com/9jXL3719rt — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 14, 2026 Then the big play struck on a 40-yard bomb from Stidham to Sutton down to the goal line where an inside handoff to Prentice would put Denver on the board first. Tua Tagovailoa and the Falcons starters didn’t get anything going with their first possession. Jonathon Cooper with a tackle for a loss on first down, then a botched snap resulted in a Malcolm Roach sack and a completed pass well short of the sticks for a quick three-and-out for Atlanta. With Denver’s 7-play scoring drive well below the expected 10-15 snaps, we ended up getting their starters out for a second possession in the first quarter. They would open up with back-to-back handoffs to RJ Harvey. He would pick up nine yards and with a third consecutive handoff he fought his way across the line for a first down. Two plays later Courtland Sutton was being manhandled, but all he needed was one hand to bring down the 16-yard completion. Quite the effort from the veteran in a meaningless preseason game. We have a preseason Courtland Sutton one handed catch 🤯 pic.twitter.com/JHRlaHdn3O — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 14, 2026 Rookie Jonah Coleman got into the mix after that with back-to-back runs for just four yards. On third and six, Stidham was hit when he was throwing for an incomplete pass to end the drive and the starters night. Kyle Pitts picked up a nice gain to get Atlanta their first first down of the game, but the Broncos defense completely clamped down from there. Tua was a bit hurried and rattled to end that drive due to the constant pressure. Surprisingly, the starters stayed in the game on the third series. They began their possession backed up inside the 20, but Stidham would hit Evan Engram on a nice deep crosser for 20 yards to get things moving on the drive. The drive looked like it would stall after a few penalties, but rookie Jonah Coleman would bounce outside for a first down run for 13 yards. He looked good on that drive. This is why #Broncos drafted Jonah Coleman. He is a thumper. #BroncosCountry pic.twitter.com/Czz5d1e3z0 — Troy Renck (@TroyRenck) August 14, 2026 The first quarter would end with Stiddy finding Troy Franklin wide open for a big gain into Falcons’ territory. Broncos 7, Falcons 0. Second Quarter Denver’s drive would stall out from there to bring Wil Lutz out for a 43-yard field goal that he would boot right through. The Falcons starters were done for their third series and that change proved disastrous as Denver kept many of their starters in. Cooper Rush would look to throw over the middle and Riley Moss would come down with the interception to set Denver up in scoring position. Riley Moss INT! 💰💰 pic.twitter.com/H59m0PLOBo — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 14, 2026 Cam Ross would bounce an end-around for a 28-yard gain to set the Broncos up with a first and goal opportunity. Stidham would be pressured, but found Jaleel McLaughlin open inside for an easy five-yard touchdown to put the Broncos up big in the first half. Denver would keep their starting defense on the field for a fourth drive and would force another punt from Atlanta. That was surprising until I saw that the defense was only on the field for 13 plays, which would be right between that 10-15 play count. That would change everything for the Falcons offense under Cooper Rush. They would finally get a drive going late in the first half driving down to the six yard line. Rush, pressured and threw into good coverage, where the ball was tipped into the waiting hands of Jahdae Barron who would return it 97 yards for the pick six touchdown to make this first preseason game into a blowout. JAHDAE BARRON PICK-6 TOUCHDOWN pic.twitter.com/yJ1w9EStjI — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 15, 2026 Broncos 24, Falcons 0. Third Quarter Sam Ehlinger took over the offense in the second half. He would get Denver into fringe field goal range for a 55-yard field attempt, but a muffed snap would result in a turnover on downs to give Atlanta decent field position. The defense would force another predictable punt, but disaster awaited Denver anyway. Jaleel McLaughlin returned to the game and on his second carry he would cough up the football to give the Falcons the ball at Denver’s 17 yard line where they would quickly get into a first and goal situation at the five. The Broncos defense would stuff the first run with a tackle for loss by Taurean York. On second down, they would get that yard back and more down to the one yard line before punching it in from there. Broncos 24, Falcons 7. Fourth Quarter Ehlinger and the Broncos got a drive going early in the fourth quarter. They avoided disaster on a deep shot that was initially ruled an interception, but overturned on review. The drive would ultimately stall out to bring Wil Lutz out for another 55-yard field goal attempt. This time the snap was high, but manageably. Lutz would pull it just wide left for the miss. #Broncos FG unit has been a mess tonight. First the bad snap from Luke Basso. Then Matt Peart ran on late. Wil Lutz re-set his spot but hit a bad ball from 55. In the regular season, there's perhaps a timeout called if it's a big spot. But still. — Parker Gabriel (@ParkerJGabriel) August 15, 2026 The Falcons did nothing with that good field position and were kicking it right back after a three-and-out. Denver then benefited from several penalties on their next drive to get them back into field goal range again. The 46-yard field attempt was finally good by Wil Lutz and he was happy enough to give a thumbs up over to the coaching staff on that one. Broncos 27, Falcons 7.

title: Injuries not a concern to Broncos fans
summary: While a few fans thought this week’s poll was aimed at “baiting” them, my intent behind the question was to gauge level of concern over some of the injuries in training camp. So joke’s on you; it was a serious question. And it was serious because I always hold my breath during training camp, hoping […]
full_text: While a few fans thought this week’s poll was aimed at “baiting” them, my intent behind the question was to gauge level of concern over some of the injuries in training camp. So joke’s on you; it was a serious question. And it was serious because I always hold my breath during training camp, hoping there’s no news of an injury. So when Jaylen Waddle isn’t practicing or Nik Bonitto is taking an extra day or Bo Nix “gets hit in the end zone,” I’m usually apoplectic until Sean Payton says, “he’ll be fine.” Thankfully, most of you freak out a lot less than I do. Preseason officially begins tonight for the Broncos, and while I’ll be excited to get to some real football (ok, semi-real), I’ll mostly be hoping everyone stays injury-free — for the next three 22+ weeks. The recent dings to the offensive line are exactly what makes me nervous this time of year. On Tuesday, depth center Michael Dieter was injured during a running play that turned out to be a season-ending quad injury. Third on the depth chart at center, Deiter was “next man up” after backup center Alex Forsyth missed a few days. And Forsyth was playing because starter Luke Wattenberg hurt his soldier earlier in the week. Tonight’s option for center is likely rookie undrafted free agent Gavin Ortega. Veteran backup lineman Calvin Throckmorton could also see some minutes. And if either of those are out, all-Pro guard Quinn Meinerz is also an option. Given that the fourth center is playing tonight, I’m more than relieved Nix is going to sit this one out. “He wants to play, and he’ll play the next two weeks,” head coach Sean Payton said Thursday, adding that had been decided a month ago. “If we were playing a [regular season] game, I would say he would play and probably, you’d have to ask him, but I would say 100 percent.” "The Denver Broncos are the best team that for some reason hasn't been talked about since the Bo Nix injury." @danorlovsky7 has his eyes on the Broncos heading into a new NFL season 🏈 pic.twitter.com/1VCNvkFIS8 — Get Up (@GetUpESPN) August 14, 2026

title: 7 storylines to watch during the Broncos vs. Falcons preseason opener
summary: The Broncos play football today! Later tonight, the Denver Broncos will kick off their 2026 preseason in Atlanta when they take on the Falcons in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL preseason. Broncos Country will need to wait one more week before we see quarterback Bo Nix on the field. Head Coach Sean Payton told […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JUNE 4: Jonah Coleman (20) of the Denver Broncos works out with teammates during OTAs at the Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Thursday, June 4, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Broncos play football today! Later tonight, the Denver Broncos will kick off their 2026 preseason in Atlanta when they take on the Falcons in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL preseason. Broncos Country will need to wait one more week before we see quarterback Bo Nix on the field. Head Coach Sean Payton told reporters that Nix will NOT play in this game, but instead will play the following two weeks. He is coming off offseason ankle surgery and has been practicing fully throughout camp, but the team would rather not have him on the turf when they don’t need him out there. With Nix sidelined, quarterback Jarrett Stidham and Sam Ehlinger will get a half each, according to Payton, as they continue their competition for the QB2 job (even though Payton says there isn’t a battle happening). Besides all that quarterback talk, we have several storylines to keep an eye on during the preseason opener, including the tight end and linebacker competition, who will replace John Franklin-Myers, and more. Here are the 7 storylines I will be watching during the Broncos preseason opener vs. the Falcons. Stidham vs. Ehlinger While Payton has downplayed this competition, veteran backup Jarrett Stidham and third-stringer Sam Ehlinger have been splitting reps throughout training camp. This has led many to speculate that they are indeed competing for the right to be the backup quarterback behind starter Bo Nix. Both quarterbacks have had their moments this offseason/training camp, but Ehlinger has shown noticeable growth in year two with the team and in Sean Payton’s offense and could be putting the pressure on Stidham. After Wednesday’s practice, Payton was asked about both quarterbacks and told reporters that they’re both doing well and that they are going to play a half each. He added they are competing against the 31 other quarterbacks, but it’ll be good to get them some real game experience and to see how they are doing. “They’re doing well. They’re going to play a half each. Again I’ve said this, they’re focused on their best stuff, and they’re competing against the 31 other quarterbacks, no different than the other positions. So it’s a great room. Those guys get along well. It’ll be good to get them some real game experience and see how they’re doing.” Stidham will likely start the game, get the reps with the starters early on, and then work with the twos throughout the remainder of the first half. Ehlinger will get the second half, and we may see this rotation flipped in Week 2. I still would be surprised if Ehlinger replaces Stidham as the Broncos QB2. Stidham is making decent backup money and was Sean Payton’s hand-picked backup when he first joined the team. It would take Ehlinger significantly outplaying him for this change to happen, at least in my opinion. It is also possible the Broncos like both as backup options and want to put as much film as they can out there for other interested teams. Teams get desperate for quarterbacks, and if you have three capable ones, teams could come calling. Regardless, I am excited to see how both perform and if Ehlinger really has closed the gap between him and Jarrett Stidham. Who will step up at TE? The Broncos’ tight end play was mostly forgettable last season, and many hoped that would change this season, especially with OC Davis Webb now calling plays. Well, through nearly two weeks of training camp, it does not seem much has changed there. Outside of Evan Engram making some noise early in camp, the updates regarding the tight ends have been few and far between. So, today’s preseason matchup could be our first real significant movement in that room. The name I am most excited to watch is 5th-round rookie tight end, Justin Joly. I thought Joly was destined to be a Day 2 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, but he slipped into Day 3 and the 5th round, where the Broncos selected him. He’s a pass-catching tight end who should thrive in the red zone, and I am hoping he gets an opportunity to showcase his talents today. Then you have 7th-round rookie Dallen Bentley, who is a bit of a forgotten man. I haven’t seen or heard a single training camp update about him, but again, he has a chance to shine tonight. He’s more of an in-line guy like Adam Trautman, so pay attention to him in the run game. Then you have Nate Adkins(if he plays) and veteran Lucas Krull. Both are fighting for roster spots, or even a spot on the practice squad, so a big game would be beneficial for them. Regardless, I am hoping we end the night feeling a little bit better about the tight end room than we do right now. Replacing JFM The Broncos’ front 7 and interior pass rush have been the story of camp thus far. They have dominated the Broncos’ offensive line throughout training camp and now will have a chance to do it against an opposing team for the first time this summer. Names like Eyioma Uwazurike, Sai’vion Jones, rookie Tyler Onyedim, Jordan Jackson, Jordan Miller, and Kristian Williams will have an opportunity to earn a larger role in the rotation, more snaps, and/or a roster spot on the 53-man roster or the practice squad. We will also have a better idea about who could replace John Franklin-Myers’ role on defense. My focus will be on Uwazurike, who reportedly has been unblockable throughout camp, second-year lineman Sai’vion Jones, and rookie Tyler Onyedim. Hopefully, we see all three of them produce tonight, get in the backfield, rush the passer, or get a big TFL or sack. Then you have guys like Jordan Jackson, Kristian Williams, and Tyler Miller all fighting for maybe one final spot on the roster and a role on the practice squad. These could be your third-team guys, so hopefully they can make some noise against the Falcons third string offensive line. Que Robinson show One player who I believe could be the star of the night is second-year edge rusher Que Robinson. He looked like a future starter last season and now has an opportunity to push for more playing time this season. He’s big, long, rangy, athletic, explosive, and has natural bend off the edge. He should have no issues against the Falcons’ reserve lineman, and I believe we’ll see him make multiple big plays tonight. With the uncertainty surrounding Jonathon Cooper’s future and potential looming suspension, a player like Robinson could have a significant role on this defense early on in the season. Jonah Elliss is likely the next man up to start if Cooper does indeed miss time, but Robinson likely is the next man off the bench alongside Dondrea Tillman. So, a strong preseason performance from Que Robinson would be great to see and, frankly, is something I feel is very likely to happen. I am also interested to see how Drew Sanders is doing. He moved to full-time edge and has been healthy for most of camp. He’s fighting for a roster spot, and more realistically, a spot on the practice squad, so he needs a solid and injury-free showing tonight. Linebacker battle One of the more intriguing roster battles happening is at the linebacker position. Starters Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad are locked in, but the battle for the reserve spots behind them is pretty wide open. We’ll have to see if Jordan Turner, who was recently activated off the NFI list, plays tonight, but if he does, he’s a strong contender for one of those spots. Same goes for Karene Reid, who made the 53-man roster last season and played a bunch of special teams snaps for the Broncos last season. I think Reid is another strong contender for a roster spot simply due to the special teams aspect. As for Levelle Bailey, the clock is ticking. He has been on the team for a few years now and hasn’t done enough to really push for a role on defense. He has been passed by other undrafted rookies and draft…

Right now, they’re one of the elite contenders. They’ll hope the same is true by the time winter arrives.” The key to the Broncos’ season is the first six weeks.
