title: 100 notes from the Houston Texans preseason matchup against LA Chargers
summary: The first Houston Texans preseason game is in the books, and it’s one the team will likely move past quickly after a 27 to 7 loss. Throughout the game I tracked the action snap by snap, taking detailed notes as each sequence unfolded. Below, in chronological order, are one hundred observations from the Texans preseason […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 13: Jared Wayne #89 of the Houston Texans scores a touchdown against Avery Smith #36 of the Los Angeles Chargers during the first quarter of a preseason game at Reliant Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) | Getty Images The first Houston Texans preseason game is in the books, and it’s one the team will likely move past quickly after a 27 to 7 loss. Throughout the game I tracked the action snap by snap, taking detailed notes as each sequence unfolded. Below, in chronological order, are one hundred observations from the Texans preseason opener. DT Naquan Jones pushed back five yards on the second play of the game. He’ll be battling for a roster spot and not a great start. DT Kayden McDonald showing good horizontal movement against a zone run play. CB Tremon Smith with good fluidity moving backwards in coverage and marking his receiver. Chargers’ KeAndre Lambert-Smith picking on linebackers a post route. The linebackers – particularly Woodaz – bit on the play action. Jones – good penetration but bad gap integrity (note: this is going to be a theme). DE Solomon Byrd moved off his spot; he keeps wanting to shoot the inside gap but gets his shoulders turned. CB Jaylin Smith’s open-field fantastic tackle started from great composure, play recognition, and body placement. Good pursuit by #14 Marte Mapu who looks light but strong. CB Tremon Smith plays too far off and doesn’t recover well enough. Will be interesting to see if he’s covering for a lack of speed or if it’s by design. Jaylen Reed was a bit late to a slant route for a first down. Multiple early instances of good play recognition, but slow to simply commit to what he sees. Alijah Huzzie is starting playing in slot. I forget how small he is. Poor footwork at point of attack by Dominic Bailey that allowed a first down. Needs to rework arms and establish positioning. Good coverage from Jake Hummel. Guarded the RB from getting the ball. For a player who missed the first part of camp he’s adjusted well to the field. Stephen Hall late to understand where he should be in coverage for press man. Had to reorganize and allowed the WR to get positioning. Defense rotated heavily on the first drive. Almost everyone rotated out from the start to the field goal. Will be interesting to see how much more run that first group will get the rest of the game. First offensive drive: Xavier Hutchinson already showing his versatility. His experience in the offense and with the team will offer him “cheap” opportunities such as that to win` Davis Mills experience and poise shown in his layered throw to Klein. Queue Texans PR to hype this throw. Noah Whittington gets the start. The pitch play demonstrates a good knowledge of his streets: downhill running in space is where he shines. Rutledge blocking against a nose tackle: they ran zone pitch and the linebacker came down to blitz. He did a fantastic job of adjusting to the defense rather than simply blocking the person in front of him. Tier two receivers Watson-Wayne-Hutchinson. Note they’re above Lewis Bond. Pretty clear group here too. Xavier Hutchinson was WIDE OPEN on the fourth down play action. Play was sniffed out quickly by the chargers defense. Braden Smith looks smooth but buckles under immediate pressure. Aireontay Ersery with great form on the third down block. Got depth and led the terms of the pass rusher. Something he wasn’t doing last year. Noah Whittington is running a bit frantic and high. Needs to settle in – he’s trying too much. Needs to block better to protect Mills. Jared Wayne is going to make a roster. Fantastic catch. Just don’t know if it will be the Texans roster. This is Collin Wright’s Super Bowl. He’s playing like it. To be fair, he’s being targeted by Trey Lance against KLM. Thus far, we’ve seen sightings from Collin Wright, McDonald, Rutledge, Klein, and Woodaz. Feeling good about this class. Jake Hummel is calling the plays with Mapu and Woodaz in. That will be KEY to him staying in the team as the backup MIKE. DE depth: WAJ/Hunter, Clowney/Horton/Byrd, Robinson/Gaye. Offensive line two: LT: Blake Fisher, LG: Patterson OC: Evan Brown RG: Nwaiwu RT: Hagen – that means Jake Andrews was the third string, not Jarrett Patterson. Speaking of rookies, poor angle from Kamari Ramsey to allow a first down and is getting stuck in bad positions. Three bad plays from him where the Chargers went after Ramsey. Mostly running 4-3 base defense with Mapu at the SAM More two tight end sets in the third offensive drive. Watching as this offense gets to its more core simple plays. Blake Fisher looks lighter, faster, and more balanced in space. They’ve run him on several screens and allowed him to get to the LB level. Fourth and one; zero push from the interior of the offensive line. Nothing from Patterson and Evan Brown which is par for the course with two lighter LBs. Not a great look. Febechi Nwaiwu looks comfortable with the second string. It’s a good baseline for the fourth rounder from OU. Can he outwork Patterson and Evan Brown to be the first swing backup on the line? That’s the step from here. Graham Mertz has been a clear step down from Davis Mills in terms of offensive control Mapu is the best backup linebacker we have and it isn’t close. He’s able to sift through blocks. Kamari Ramsey drops a pick-six. He was in a great place as the underneath coverage in zone with placement between the QB and WR. Will use this as a baseline for encouragement after a poor series. NICE three-and-out after two long drives against this defense. It’s the second-tier LBs and Safeties with the third-string CBs and DL Not getting nearly enough pressure from the defensive ends. Zero from the defensive tackles. Vibe check: both teams have a ton of depth. This is a high-quality preseason game and the coaches will be happy with the film so far. A lot to work off of both good and bad. Blake Fisher absolutely flattened on a run play that shuttered a good hole on the front side. That can’t happen against backups. Bad play all around: Mertz threw a duck. UDFA Joshua Pitsenberger missed a block that forced Mertz out of the pocket. Bad blocking by Hagen. Quick three and out. First play for Jamal Hill misses a tackle but pushes the play further and causes a short run. Pure special teamer and is competing desperately for a roster spot. Have to enjoy the good play. Mate Mapu blitz off the SAM was very, very not impactful. Allowed Trey Lance plenty of time to pick apart our team. Ali Gaye with two offsides in short order. If he’s gong to be offsides he’s got to make a play at least. Aiden Fisher struggles to get off blocks. Habit of running backwards to go forwards will not suffice. 91 Naquan Jones not getting much pressure up the middle but doing good job in the run game. Two minute defense: not great. Dropping too much into zones rather than finding players. Kayvon Merrywhether with the defensive play of the first half. That’s how you make it on the team practice squad! Jaylin Smith is being asked to play both press and off coverage. His versatility is high and he’s closing down on receivers better than the other backups. Dylan Horton has put together a ton of pass rush moves, but still struggles with contain. He has to still put it all togeteher. KAMARI RAMSEY INTEREEPTION. Love that from the rookie. Playing as a high safety. Read the Keyes. Broke early. Graham Mertz with a great opportunity with two time outs and :51 to show something. What does he do his first play? Horizontal pass. Sam Hagen was overwhelmed. Make that two in a row. Can’t bash on Mertz anymore… looks like he’s hurt that left knee again that he tore in college. Love to see Ali Gaye on special teams, but that’s a third penalty against the veteran. Jake Andrews is now at center. Oy. Whittington needs to stretch plays out. Patience is gong to be an important complement to his game. Strong block by Jake Andrews on a linebacker. Zero push from everyone…

(Photo by Michael Allio/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images According to multiple local media sources, Indianapolis Colts special teams coordinator Brian Mason has a serious knee injury, having torn multiple knee ligaments following a nasty collision along the sidelines after last night’s preseason opener against the New England Patriots had ended in a 13-13 tie : As expected, not good news on Colts ST coordinator Brian Mason. Tore multiple knee ligaments on sideline collision on final play at Pats, per source. I believe @JoelAErickson first. — Mike Chappell (@mchappell51) August 14, 2026 The 4th-year Colts special teams coordinator’s knee seemingly buckled upon impact with players—after being rolled up, and he could be seen writhing in pain on the field along the sidelines. Much to the misfortune of Mason, it’s a classic case of being in the wrong place, at the wrong time. Despite the Colts holding their own against the reigning AFC Champions in an exhibition game, unfortunately, it did have the game end on somewhat of a surprising somber note. It’ll be interesting to see how this impacts Mason’s special teams coaching availability this upcoming season, and whether it could be a situation, where he’s limited more to the press box on game days, with a rehabbing knee, presumably from upcoming ligament repair surgery. At any rate, we’re thinking about Coach Mason and hoping he makes a quick and full recovery.

title: Which Colts Training Camp Storylines Actually Matter?
summary: We’re deep into training camp, which means the countdown to Week 1 can officially begin. Last night’s preseason game was a very nice opportunity to see players in live action, though it’s important not to overreact to a singular preseason game. This is always one of the more fascinating times on the NFL calendar. Every […]
full_text: We’re deep into training camp, which means the countdown to Week 1 can officially begin. Last night’s preseason game was a very nice opportunity to see players in live action, though it’s important not to overreact to a singular preseason game. This is always one of the more fascinating times on the NFL calendar. Every team around the league is working to build chemistry, establish an identity, and evaluate their roster. At the same time, there also is very little “real football” being played, up until last night of course. After years of going through the same song and dance, buying into the hype surrounding certain players while expecting the downfall of others before they’ve even taken a real snap, I’ve became more interested in figuring out what we can actually glean from training camp and, more importantly, how predictive these storylines really are. In my opinion, joint practices are the most predictive reps that a team can get prior to Week 1. It sounded like the New England practice was a good back-and-forth. That’s exactly what you like to hear. It’s the ultimate measuring stick, because it’s true competition, where real evaluation can take place. There are outliers of course, but most of the time reports from standard practices in the summer don’t give you a good idea of how good your roster stacks up vs. the rest of the league. It really is the age-old question: is the offense good or the defense just really bad? And vise-versa. However, as I mentioned, there are some outliers. It’s not like every training camp storyline has zero merit to it, I just think a lot of them are over reactionary when sometimes it’s just too early to tell either way. I’m going to attempt to look at the big picture here and do my best to figure out what Colts storylines actually matter so far. It should be an interesting exercise to revisit later THE WIDE RECEIVER DEPTH: It Matters But Only A Little Every year Chris Ballard seems to stubbornly neglect one position in training camp (in an attempt to trust his gut by betting on unproven players) when it’s obvious to everyone that there’s a gaping hole on the roster. Some years it’s been a DB, other years it’s been a tight end. Last year, it was a linebacker. This year, it seems to be a few different positions, but in the eyes of the football world it’s WR. The Colts absolutely need to add depth at the position. With Alec Pierce out of practice, it’s one of the worst WR rooms in football. But here’s why I am not as worried about the group as others. Football gives you 5 eligible receivers on any play, but they don’t tell you who they have to be. I expect the Colts to live in a lot more heavier groupings with less WRs on the field, now that they have Tyler Warren. I also think that a lot of unsexy options can replace the role that Pittman had in the offense and give the Colts the same setup they had last year. Pittman didn’t have a diverse route tree, wasn’t asked to win vs man coverage, and wasn’t the guy you needed to scheme open on “got-to-have-it” downs. He was asked to make consted catches in the short to intermediate part of the field and block his butt off in the run game. He was the ultimate competitor and I have a lot of respect for that, but I think the film has proven that over time. So overall, I think it’s imperative that the Colts add more depth at the position, but it’s not an unmitigated disaster by any means. THE BACKUP QB COMPETITION: Absolutely Matters Even If You Hope None Of Them Actually Play A Game In my opinion, this is the most important storyline in camp so far (which I guess is a decent problem to have, all things considered). To state the obvious, if Daniel Jones goes down at any point in the season, it’s fair to say the season is almost certainly a lost cause. But I also think it be silly for the Colts to view it this way. Statistically the odds are not in Jones’ favor to be on the field for a full season. I think the Colts are missing out by having a backup QB competition with two guys they aren’t particularly thrilled about. The opportunity to add a veteran QB that could help your 2nd team players get valuable reps was inexpensive and obvious. The Anthony Richardson experiment was over last offseason and his trade value is still next to nothing. He did have a very solid showcase last night, but is that really enough to move the needle? It still feels like you’re staring down the barrel of trading your former 4th overall pick for a conditional late day 3 pick, or even releasing him on cutdown day, when you could have made the move a long time ago. Riley Leonard seems like a developmental practice squad player, but his camp has been equally as uninspiring. I think the Colts would be very wise to add a veteran to that room that you can trust in a pinch. LAIATU LATU WRECKING PRACTICE: We’ll see Is Laiatu Latu wrecking practice because he’s ready to take the leap? Or is he wrecking practice because he’s facing a quasi rookie RT in practice? We’ll see I suppose. Latu is a guy who has feasted on unproven tackles or TEs, but when matched up against quality starters, seems to fade. If anything those reports slightly worry me regarding Jalen Travis. For a front office that preached competition last offseason, they sure feel comfortable handing out jobs on the offensive line in the offseason. Tony Sparano Jr. has definitely earned the right to run the room how he sees fit, but I wonder there could be an opportunity to invest more in competition? Last year Matt Goncalves transitioned to guard and there was nobody competing with him last year. A year later, the Colts felt like they need to push him more and drafted Farmer. I hope something similar doesn’t happen with Jalen Travis at RT. SETH MCGOWAN EMERGING AS THE BACKUP RB: Nope For the Colts sake, I hope the flashes Seth McGowan has reportedly shown in camp actually translate to the field. However, I’m skeptical that we’ve seen enough to feel confident that’s the case. Live tackling is really where you can see a RB’s value. You want to see the movement patterns and speed on display, but 90% of runs in the NFL are not going untouched at the line of scrimmage. You’re going to have to push the pile or break a tackle.

title: Reacts Survey Results: The NFL Preseason is Upon Us
summary: This week, we asked Jacksonville Jaguars fans what they’re looking forward to watching during the 2026 NFL preseason. 60% of fans are especially excited to see Anthony Campanile’s defense. “I just want to see a clean operation,” head coach Liam Coen said after Thursday’s joint practice with the New Orleans Saints. “That, and then just […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 11: Jalen Huskey #22 of the Jacksonville Jaguars practices during training camp at Miller Electric Center on August 11, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images This week, we asked Jacksonville Jaguars fans what they’re looking forward to watching during the 2026 NFL preseason. 60% of fans are especially excited to see Anthony Campanile’s defense. “I just want to see a clean operation,” head coach Liam Coen said after Thursday’s joint practice with the New Orleans Saints. “That, and then just go play. Like, let’s see who is going to be the guy that’s going to go make plays when it’s not perfect … And then who’s going to win some one-on-one matchups? Whether it’s one-on-one pass pro, whether it’s I’m covering the guy one-on-one, or whether I got to defeat a one-on-one matchup at receiver. Who’s going to go do that?” Coen will be handing the playsheet to offensive coordinator Grant Udisnki, in an effort to give him some playcalling experience while providing himself some time to oversee the rest of the team. “It’ll be a really good time for me to be on the defensive headset a little bit,” said Coen. “Typically when the defense is on, I’m doing adjustments with the offensive staff, and then I’ll click over and be able to get a little bit here and there. So, being able to hear the full process and be able to hear a little bit more of the new communication that will have to exist.” According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Jaguars are 2.5-point underdogs against the Saints for Saturday’s 4 p.m. ET preseason matchup.

title: Breaking down every Chiefs position group ahead of preseason Week 1
summary: It has been over two weeks since the Kansas City Chiefs began training camp on the grass fields at Missouri Western State University in St. Joe. I learned a lot from the 11 trips I made up I-29 to cover Chiefs practice in person for Arrowhead Pride. So with a push from user “saintschiefsfan,” I’m […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: Travis Kelce #87 prepares to lead the tight end group in a drill during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on Aug 11, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It has been over two weeks since the Kansas City Chiefs began training camp on the grass fields at Missouri Western State University in St. Joe. I learned a lot from the 11 trips I made up I-29 to cover Chiefs practice in person for Arrowhead Pride. So with a push from user “saintschiefsfan,” I’m here to spread all the knowledge I gathered watching full-team practices before the preseason kicks off. This was their comment on a post Friday morning . First of all , thank you for giving us breakdowns and tweets every day from ST. Joe. If there is anyone who knows how brutal it gets in the summer up there, it is me. So I appreciate all you have done for us fans. I am going to do something I have never done as a member of this site. I want to make a request. Given that you have been up there for all this camp, can you break down or give levels of concern for every position group on the team going into this game? I think it would be very helpful since you saw more live reps than probably anyone else on AP. Thank you. Ask, and you might receive! With 24 hours to go until the preseason begins, let’s break down each position group on the Chiefs’ roster by how I’ve seen it shaking out at practice, pointing out which groups give the most concern. Quarterbacks (4) Starter: Patrick Mahomes Backup competition: Justin Fields and Garrett Nussmeier Potential practice squad: Chris Oladokun There’s little doubt in my mind that the Chiefs’ quarterback play in the preseason will be some of the best Kansas City has seen since Patrick Mahomes’ rookie year. Fields has the talent to create big plays with his arm and legs in a preseason setting, while Nussmeier, the rookie from LSU, has looked the part of a legitimate NFL prospect in camp. The concern is whether the Chiefs are willing to keep him on the roster as a third quarterback, or if they’ll risk losing him to the waiver wire on cutdown day. Running backs (6) Lead back: Kenneth Walker Backup competition: Brashard Smith, Emari Demercado and Emmett Johnson Potential practice squad: Jaydn Ott and E.J. Smith The first four seem pretty set in stone; it will just be about how the order plays out in a given game or matchup. Wide receivers (14) Starting receivers: Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy and Tyquan Thornton Backup competition: Cyrus Allen, Jalen Royals, Nikko Remigio, Andrew Armstrong and Jimmy Holiday Potential practice squad: Jacob De Jesus, Omari Evans, Jeff Weimer, Xavier Loyd, Jason Brownlee and Jeff Caldwell With my earlier compliment of the quarterbacks, there’s reason to believe we’ll get to see rookies and newcomers at this position showcase their skills, even without Mahomes in the game. And we’ll need to see it. I have a high level of concern about the fragility of the Chiefs’ starting receiving corps, but that fear can subside if Allen, Royals, Armstrong, and others prove to be quality role players in the regular season. Tight ends (6) First-team tight ends: Travis Kelce, Noah Gray and Jared Wiley Competing to earn a roster spot as the fourth tight end: Jake Briningstool, Tre Watson and Mason Pline This is one of the most intriguing positions to follow in the preseason games, considering how much work players behind Kelce and Gray should get. Wiley, who suffered a hamstring injury this week, has been a staple in the Chiefs’ starting offense all camp, but he (and Gray) needs to show it in the preseason to stave off the momentum building for Briningstool. I initially projected the team to keep just three tight ends, but Briningstool looks like he will perform well in the preseason and push the team to make room for him one way or another. His receiving skills will be on display the most. I’m still concerned about this group’s blocking ability after Kelce if the offense leans into that identity. Offensive line (15) First-team offensive line Left tackle Josh Simmons Left guard Kingsley Suamataia Center Creed Humphrey Right guard Kahlil Benson Right tackle Jaylon Moore Second-team offensive line Left tackle Esa Pole Left guard Mike Caliendo Center Hunter Nourzad Right guard Pete Nygra Right tackle Ethan Driskell Potential practice squad Right tackle Chu Godrick Guard C.J. Hanson Tackle/Guard Matt Waletzko Guard Josh Thompson If the injury to right guard Trey Smith (hip) is short-term, like head coach Andy Reid says it is, there’s little concern for me about the offensive line. It will be important to see how the Chiefs handle rookie Kahlil Benson in the preseason, however. If he sticks inside at guard with Smith presumably not playing on Saturday, it may indicate the team is ready to move forward with him as the first player off the bench at guard rather than the starting right tackle, but an extended look at him at right tackle could say the opposite. Defensive ends (9) Starting rotation: George Karlaftis, Ashton Gillotte, Felix Anudike-Uzomah and R Mason Thomas Competing to earn a roster spot as the fifth defensive end: Emmanuel Ogbah, Tyreke Smith and Ethan Hurkett Potential practice squad: V.J. Anthony and Anthony Dunn This position is very concerning, specifically the second edge rusher opposite Karlaftis. All eyes will be on No. 51 to see if Thomas’ first step is real, but all eyes should shift towards a fourth-year player from Kansas State. Anudike-Uzomah could be a difference-making X-factor if he finally puts it all together, but he has actually rushed from an interior alignment a lot of times this camp. Gillotte suffered a hamstring injury during the first week of camp and has been out since. The team signed Ogbah for a reason, but the unproven players in this group can still make a statement in the preseason and strengthen confidence. Defensive tackles (7)* Starting rotation: Chris Jones, Khyiris Tonga, Peter Woods and Omarr Norman-Lott* (PUP) Competing to be placeholder if Norman-Lott isn’t ready for Week 1: Marcus Harris and Cole Brevard Potential practice squad: Damon Payne and Amari McNeill The only note here is to watch for Harris, a penetrating, second-year lineman from Auburn who could be the substitute for Norman-Lott if he isn’t ready to go in Week 1. If the massive Brevard could prove to be a quality gap plugger, he may be a valuable piece to round out the hampered group at the start of the year. Linebackers (8) Starting linebackers in Base defense: Nick Bolton — MIKE Drue Tranquill — WILL Cole McDonald — SAM Competing to be backup linebackers on the active roster Jack Cochrane — Backup MIKE Jeffrey Bassa — WILL/SAM Cole Christiansen — Backup at every position Potential practice squad: Kam Arnold and Wesley Bissainthe At the start of camp, I got excited about this group’s potential. It all depends on whether Bassa can be a jack-of-all-trades weapon that is used situationally around the main starters. Look for No. 31’s playmaking ability this preseason, blitzing, tackling in space, or in coverage. Outside cornerbacks (8) Starting rotation: Mansoor Delane, Nohl Williams and L’Jarius Sneed Backup competition: Kristian Fulton, Melvin Smith and Kaiir Elam Potential practice squad: D’Arco Perkins-McAllister and Zelmar Vedder With the top of this group dealing with plenty of injuries, Smith has played a lot of reps with the starting defense to this point in camp. It’s worth considering whether Fulton is someone the team would be willing to trade for if he flashes in the preseason; he has rarely played with the starters in camp. Either way, the biggest preseason concern is the lack of time this group has spent on the field at full speed and full contact. We’ll learn little about that part of it this weekend. No. 19 Perkins-McAllister is a long-armed, physical body on the outside to keep an eye on in…

title: Chris Jones: ‘I don’t want to play in the preseason’
summary: We are a day away from the Kansas City Chiefs’ preseason opener against the Los Angeles Rams, a team that has historically rested its impact players in the preseason. That will be the case on Saturday at Arrowhead Stadium. The Rams have announced that career backup Stetson Bennett will take the reins at quarterback, matching […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - AUGUST 09: Defensive tackle Chris Jones #95 of the Kansas City Chiefs on the bench during the NFL Preseason 2025 game at State Farm Stadium on August 09, 2025 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images We are a day away from the Kansas City Chiefs ’ preseason opener against the Los Angeles Rams , a team that has historically rested its impact players in the preseason. That will be the case on Saturday at Arrowhead Stadium. The Rams have announced that career backup Stetson Bennett will take the reins at quarterback, matching the Chiefs’ decision to sideline starting quarterback Patrick Mahomes by resting veteran and reigning league MVP Matthew Stafford. When Chiefs star defensive tackle Chris Jones was asked about what he can get out of the preseason, he made his stance clear, in case head coach Andy Reid was listening. “Why play the starters?” Jones asked local media during his post-practice press conference on Thursday. “There’s so much risk to playing the starters in the preseason. I hope Coach Reid is like, ‘You know what, starters don’t play.‘” By Jones’ tone, it sounds like Mahomes could be the only starter excused from taking the field to begin Saturday’s game, excluding the players dealing with injuries from training camp. “It’s good to get repetition, but I don’t want to play in the preseason,” Jones continued. “I’d rather not play, but if I do have to play, I’m going to buckle up.” The Rams’ offense was as good as there was in the NFL last season, but Jones and the Chiefs’ starting defense — if the group takes the field together — will be facing a B- or C-version of the unit. On top of starting Bennett, head coach Sean McVay is also handing off the play-calling duties to offensive coordinator (and Rockhurst High School alum) Nate Scheelhaase. “The mentality is like, ‘I want to play against your starters,” Jones explained. “I want to play against the guys that are going to be starting on Sundays, because you like to weigh yourself out, where I’m at and where I can improve. Give me your best talent.” How do you feel about the preseason? Would you want the Chiefs to play their starters a normal amount, or completely rest them ahead of the regular season? Let us know in the comments.

title: 5 things to watch in Chiefs’ preseason opener against the Rams
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs will open the preseason slate on Saturday, August 15th at Arrowhead Stadium. The game will kick off at 3:00 PM Arrowhead time and be broadcast locally on KSHB 41 as well as on the FM radio waves of 96.5 The Fan. The Chiefs will welcome the Los Angeles Rams, who will […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - NOVEMBER 27: George Karlaftis #56 of the Kansas City Chiefs battles with Rob Havenstein #79 of the Los Angeles Rams at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on November 27, 2022 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs will open the preseason slate on Saturday, August 15th at Arrowhead Stadium. The game will kick off at 3:00 PM Arrowhead time and be broadcast locally on KSHB 41 as well as on the FM radio waves of 96.5 The Fan . The Chiefs will welcome the Los Angeles Rams, who will also be entering the 2026 season with high expectations. Temperatures are expected to be scorching at kickoff in the August heat, and neither team’s starting lineups are expected to be on the field for long, if at all. Here are five things to watch in the preseason opener: 1. Justin Fields With quarterback Patrick Mahomes confirmed to not be playing on Saturday, Chiefs fans will get their first look at the full experience of Justin Fields. Kansas City is his fourth team since being drafted in the first round of the 2021 NFL Draft. Last season, as a member of the New York Jets , Fields started nine games, throwing for 1,259 yards and seven touchdowns, while rushing for 383 yards and four touchdowns. His record as a starter was only 2-7, but with only one interception, that could be attributed to how putrid the New York Jets were. Fields has a chance to be the best backup quarterback Mahomes has had, and he brings another dynamic to the table that past understudies have not. Fields can be a prolific runner and is dangerous in the red zone with his legs. It will be worth watching whether the offensive brain trust puts him in position to use his legs on Saturday, or if he instinctually takes off himself on a pass play. 2. Running back rotation There is no doubt that Kenneth Walker will be the team’s lead back for the foreseeable future, but there is real competition for who will be the immediate backups when he needs a breather. Through training camp, Brashard Smith has taken the most snaps with the second team, but Emari Demercado’s name showed up on the unofficial depth chart that was released on Tuesday of this week. As a matter of fact, Smith was listed as the fourth back on the depth chart behind Demercado and rookie Emmet Johnson. The team likely has a vision for all three to be on the roster, especially since they have positive, contrasting skill sets that complement one another and provide contrast to Walker’s capabilities as the lead back. Smith has a gadget aspect to his game as well as special teams potential; Demercado has been praised for his pass blocking, and Johnson has the vision and shifty speed to eventually develop into a direct backup for Walker and a possible replacement one day. How the snaps and touches are distributed over the next three weeks should paint a picture of how the room will look in 2026. 3. Depth at corner back The Chiefs’ secondary has been a topic of debate in camp, largely due to an injury-plagued cornerback unit. First-round pick Mansoor Delane has only had one practice out of a yellow non-contact jersey, while veterans L’Jarius Sneed and Kristian Fulton have both missed significant time with injury. It is uncertain what the Chiefs lineup will look like on Saturday, but it will open up opportunities for players like Nohl Williams to further cement his status as a valuable commodity on the roster, while giving the back end of the roster more opportunities to shine. Players to keep an eye on will be Kader Kohou, Jadon Canady, Kevin Knowles, D’Aco Perkins-McAllister, Kair Elam, Melvin Smith Jr., and Zelmar Vedder. Kohou and Canady will both likely see a high number of snaps as slot corners, or Nickel players, while the others will compete for playing time along the outside. 4. The rookie defensive linemen Two Chiefs rookies have dominated the headlines in camp so far. First-round draft pick Peter Woods has been the talk of camp, and day in and day out he has dominated as a top performer in St. Joseph. Also drawing praise has been second-round pick R Mason Thomas out of Oklahoma. Although he has not stood out as much as Woods has, Thomas has shown to be more than just the speed threat off the edge many labeled him as coming out of Oklahoma. The Chiefs have long needed pass-rush help alongside Chris Jones — entering his age-32 season — and Woods and Gillotte will give them a chance to develop the next generation of pass rushers alongside him. Both players win with explosion and athleticism, and both could be impact makers early on. Saturday will be their first test and their first time experiencing NFL game speed from the front lines. Kahlil Benson Undrafted rookies making the roster is rare in the NFL, let alone finding a starting role by Week 1. However, Benson will likely be out with the starting five on the offensive line come Saturday afternoon. Starting camp as primarily the team’s right tackle with the first team, Benson could be on the path to doing something remarkable. Even though Jaylon Moore is listed as the starting right tackle on the unofficial depth chart, the snaps in camp so far have gone to Benson, and while Trey Smith has missed time with a hip injury, it has been Benson who filled in at right guard. This week, and in live-game situations, watch how he reacts in-game, how quickly he adjusts to game speed, and the strength needed to make it in the NFL. The difference in speed from practices to games in the NFL can be a lot for most rookies to handle. This will be a good test for Benson early in his career and will help the team figure out whether he is ready to go.

title: Chiefs News: Chiefs to see Stetson Bennett at quarterback for Rams
summary: The latest While the Kansas City Chiefs typically value preseason snaps for starters, the Los Angeles Rams rarely use preseason for their first-team players. It would make for an exciting preseason opener, with defensive end Myles Garrett and quarterback Matthew Stafford on the other side of the field. However, quarterback Patrick Mahomes won’t be starting, […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 1: Stetson Bennett IV #13 of the Los Angeles Rams throws during training camp at Loyola Marymount University on August 1, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The latest While the Kansas City Chiefs typically value preseason snaps for starters, the Los Angeles Rams rarely use preseason for their first-team players. It would make for an exciting preseason opener, with defensive end Myles Garrett and quarterback Matthew Stafford on the other side of the field. However, quarterback Patrick Mahomes won’t be starting, and neither will Stafford. The Chiefs will be starting backup quarterback Justin Fields against a former National Championship-winning quarterback. Stetson Bennett to start for Rams on Saturday vs. Chiefs | Pro Football Talk Rams rookie quarterback Ty Simpson will make his preseason debut on Saturday against the Chiefs. But he will not be Los Angeles’ first signal-caller up. Via multiple reporters, head coach Sean McVay said in his Thursday press conference that Stetson Bennett will start the preseason opener. Bennett, a fourth-round pick in 2023, is currently in line to serve as Matthew Stafford’s backup, as Jimmy Garoppolo was not re-signed in free agency — though Garoppolo is still available. Here are 4 Chiefs players you should keep an eye on in preseason opener vs. Rams | The Kansas City Star Jalen Royals, wide receiver There’s a common expression in the early stages of training camp, particularly when an under-the-radar player makes a few plays. Wait until the pads come on. Jalen Royals is the inverse. He struggled to get going here in St. Joseph over the first several practices, but he has actually been better since the pads came on. His best week is the one leading into this game. Five Observations from Thursday’s Practice | Chiefs Training Camp 8/13 | The Mothership 2. Wide receiver Rashee Rice had a busy day with several catches during the “offensive” portions of practice. Rice was targeted early and often during Thursday’s practice, particularly on intermediate throws over the middle of the field. The timing of his routes was in lockstep with quarterback Patrick Mahomes throughout the session. In addition to Rice, Mahomes found tight end Travis Kelce, wide receiver Tyquan Thornton, tight end Noah Gray and wide receiver Xavier Worthy for completions across the various “offensive” periods of practice. Kenneth Walker, Cyrus Allen, and the biggest storylines from Kansas City Chiefs training camp ahead of preseason Week 1 | A to Z Sports Cyrus Allen’s preseason reps will reveal his role Rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen has flashed during camp, though he’s also dealt with some bumps and bruises. The preseason will be telling. How the Chiefs handle Allen’s workload will probably say a lot about what they envision for him during the 2026 NFL season. If he’s only out there for a couple of reps, that signals Kansas City wants to protect him and keep him healthy. Dave Toub mentioned that he wants to see Allen as a kick returner, but that it’d be up to Coach Reid. Chiefs Star Chris Jones on Rookie DT Peter Woods: ‘He’s Strong as an Ox‘ | Sports Illustrated While Woods has been labeled as having “a ways to go” by DC Steve Spagnuolo and HC Andy Reid, his raw talent has stood out during training camp. He has done a solid job of inserting himself into the defensive tackle rotation alongside Jones and Khyiris Tonga. On Thursday, Jones was one of the Kansas City players who spoke to the media after padded practice. The future Hall of Famer sang Woods’ praises, particularly when discussing his freakish strength. “Strong. A young bull,” Jones said to describe Woods. “I think for him, just pulling it all together. He has the skill set. He has the power for it, also. He’s strong as an ox, and he’s willing to learn.” Around the NFL Sources: Facing charges, Terrion Arnold set to join Seahawks | ESPN The deal will be for one year, sources told Rapoport. Arnold, 23, is facing eight felony charges stemming from a kidnapping and robbery in Tampa, Florida, in February. He was arrested in Hillsborough County in June after turning himself in and was released the following week by the Lions, who drafted him in the first round in 2024. A day before the Lions cut him, Arnold was released from custody after posting a $1 million bond. No trial date has been set. Arnold’s next scheduled court date is a disposition hearing Oct. 5. Fernando Mendoza’s preseason debut: Rookie throws one TD, absorbs one big hit | The Athletic Making his NFL preseason debut for the Las Vegas Raiders, Mendoza finished 10-for-16 passing for 97 yards against the Arizona Cardinals. He took over for Kirk Cousins after the veteran led the Raiders to a touchdown on the team’s first offensive series. The last pass Mendoza threw in the first half was his lone touchdown of the night, a slant to second-year receiver Jack Bech on third-and-goal. The touchdown was impressive, especially considering Mendoza took a sack on first down two plays earlier. But the TD wasn’t Mendoza’s lone highlight. A 19-yard connection to rookie receiver Malik Benson over the middle showed Mendoza is growing comfortable operating from under center and in the play-action game, questions about the quarterback after he operated in a shotgun-heavy scheme at Indiana University that frequently used run-pass option concepts. Bears could merge two sites for potential stadium in northwest Indiana | NFL.com The Bears announced in June that they were moving forward with a stadium development project in Hammond, Indiana. They have completed their review of what they are calling the Lost Marsh site, and they are doing their due diligence on the Wolf Lake Terminal site. They could merge the two options together in some way. “Even though we’ve had occasional meetings with the state of Illinois, our sole focus at this point in time is working on a world-class stadium and mixed-use development in Hammond, Indiana,” team President Kevin Warren said Thursday. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Travis Kelce’s 2026 goal: ‘Play at a better level than last year’ “All aspects of football,” Kelce explained. “Being more accountable when the ball is in the air. There were a few games last year that I felt like I put on myself. In the blocking world, being able to get my guys so we can spring guys for bigger gains. And then on top of that, just being a better leader. When we get stuck with adversity hidden, who’s going to want you in that foxhole with them? That’s one of those things that I want — to be one of those guys that everybody counts on to be there and get us out of that foxhole.” From The Feed Follow Arrowhead Pride on Social Media Facebook: Like our page Instagram: @ArrowheadPride X: Follow @ArrowheadPride AP Staff on X: See complete list 90.9 The Bridge on X: Follow @909thebridge

title: Best and worst Chargers PFF grades vs. the Texans
summary: The Chargers came out and “out-physical’d” the Texans for the majority of the game, per Houston head coach DeMeco Ryans. After a back-and-forth game through the first half, the Chargers’ depth continued to pour it on during the final 30 minutes. And that goes for both sides of the ball. Unsurprisingly, that was reflected in […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - AUGUST 13: Center Jacob Spomer of the Los Angeles Chargers readies for play during the NFL preseason game between Houston Texans and Los Angeles Chargers on August 13, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Chargers came out and “out-physical’d” the Texans for the majority of the game, per Houston head coach DeMeco Ryans. After a back-and-forth game through the first half, the Chargers’ depth continued to pour it on during the final 30 minutes. And that goes for both sides of the ball. Unsurprisingly, that was reflected in this week’s grades from Pro Football Focus. Without further ado, for the first time this season, here are the best and worst performers from Chargers-Texans, per PFF. Offense Best OG Kayode Awosika – 90.1 C Jacob Spomer – 82.0 Trevor Penning – 78.1 OT Travis Burke – 73.8 WR Devonte Ross – 73.7 Spomer looked like a seasoned vet at times when in at center. He replaced Slaughter when the latter moved to left guard and I don’t think we saw any notable drop in play. As one of only two Chargers to receive a grade above 80.0, he has earned more looks as a prospective lineman of the future for the Bolts. Ross caught the lone touchdown of the night and had the third-highest receiving grade on offense (72.8). Penning was fourth in run block grade (73.1). and second in pass block grade (82.2) on the night. He was called for a holding penalty, however. Worst RB Kimani Vidal – 38.1 QB Trey Lance – 43.0 TE Jerand Bradley – 45.7 WR Dalevon Campbell – 48.3 OG/C Jake Slaughter – 51.1 TE Evan Svoboda – 51.1 Lance looked at times to be in control of the offense but he threw one egregious interception and almost threw another that was somehow dropped by the defender. His scrambling ability is still there which keeps his floor high, but he did not look any better at reading defenses on Thursday night. Slaughter was up-and-down during his 51 snaps played against the Texans. His run block grade of 46.4 was the lowest on the entire team, but a pass block grade of 72.5 helped him stay out of the trenches. This one is definitely a “gotta watch the tape” situation, in my opinion. He looked great in pass pro, especially when it came to handling Houston’s games and stunts up front. Defense Best LB Marlowe Wax – 91.9 LB Troy Dye – 88.9 LB Junior Colson – 87.0 EDGE Akheem Mesidor – 80.9 DT TeRah Edwards – 79.8 Jim Harbaugh said the thought the linebacker play of the Chargers was really good and based on these numbers, he was right. Wax was elite with a 91.9 overall grade which included a 90.0 in coverage (he should have had a pick!). Dye was great across the board (four of five grades above.a 73.0) while Colson finished top four in pass rush, coverage, and tackling. Mesidor looked to be shot out of a cannon during his limited snap count. He had one play where he smacked the living daylights out of the right tackle before getting into the face of quarterback Davis Mills. His pass rush grade of 74.6 was second best on defense. Worst EDGE Kyle Kennard – 35.7 DT Nick Barrett – 44.7 S Noah Avinger – 47.0 Jacob Guillory II – 51.6 DT Jahmeer Carter – 56.0 Kennard continues his rough transition to the NFL level after being the lowest-graded player on the entire team against the Texans. His 49.4 pass rush grade was the lowest on the defense while his run defense grade of 59.1 was the lowest among edge rushers. Barrett was by far the worst-graded tackler as he earned a 22.9, the lowest on the team by a whopping 45.3 grade points (68.2). Carter was solid in the box score, but his 53.1 pass rush grade hurt his overall score to get him into the bottom five.

full_text: HOUSTON, TX - AUGUST 13: Wide Receiver KeAndre Lambert-Smith of the Los Angeles Chargers runs with the ball after a reception during the NFL preseason game between Houston Texans and Los Angeles Chargers on August 13, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Chargers racked up almost 400 yards of offense (379) against the Texans which is an impressive feat given how good DeMeco Ryans has been at coaching up that unit in recent years. Defensively, they were top notch, as well. Houston recorded just 209 yards and turned the ball over three times while mainly being quarterbacked by veteran Davis Mills. Across the board, there were standouts everywhere at almost every position. Below are six players I thought stood out the most during Thursday night’s win over the Texans. OG/C Jake Slaughter Slaughter started the game at center and eventually moved to left guard in the second quarter. He looked comfortable at both positions, mainly in pass protection where he showed the capability to dissect and pass off stunts/twists by the defense. Right away, Slaughter looked the part with his high football IQ and elite athleticism. He needs to keep his pad level down a bit which is always comes with being a taller interior lineman, but that will naturally come with time. Regardless, this was a great first step. #Chargers @PFF pass blocking grades vs Texans: Travis Burke: 40.1 (0 sacks/2 pressures) Branson Taylor: 84.2 (0 sacks/0 pressures) Jake Slaughter: 72.5 (0 sacks/1 pressure) Kayode Awosika: 81.2 (0 sacks & 2 pressures) Logan Taylor: 62.0 (0 sacks/1 pressure) Josh… pic.twitter.com/9Xr6yctHk4 — RIBH (@RunItBackHerbo) August 14, 2026 DT Jahmeer Carter Carter entered a crowded interior defender room when he was signed this year as an undrafted free agent out of Virginia. He was always going to need to make a huge impression in camp to stand out in any way, and I believe he did just that on Thursday night. The 6’2, 311-pounder was stout in the run game and made two of the biggest plays on defense with a knifing tackle for loss and the only sack recorded by the Chargers on the night. QB D.J. Uiagalelei In the first chance for an impression in the battle for QB2, it was Uiagalelei that made the bigger impression with a cleaner and more efficient outing against the Texans. With six completions on nine attempts, DJU racked up 120 yards mainly aided by a 55-yard catch-and-run by running back Amar Johnson. Still, the throw hit Johnson in stride which allowed him to reach top speed in a moment before coasting nearly untouched up the sideline. Later on in the second half, Uiagalelei escaped a sack, hit a 180, and broke the pocket to the right before lofting a pass to Dalevon Campbell. The tall wideout brought it down and went for a gain of 33 yards (before, you know, the fumble). While Uiagalelei may have had the benefit of playing against the third-stringers and some easy yards, it’s hard not to come away from this game feeling like the battle to backup Justin Herbert just became a bit more heated. RB Amar Johnson Johnson was the star of Thursday night’s win with his 85-yard, two-touchdown performance. The second-year player out of South Dakota State scored the first two touchdowns of the game and authored the longest play between either team with a 55-yard catch-and-run that helped set up his second score. Johnson possesses sub-4.40 speed and he showed it by beating second level defenders to the corner multiple times. Johnson was a preseason darling for the Packers last year before the Bolts signed him and I think he may have played his way into the team’s RB4 role as a lock for the practice squad. Amar Johnson Shines. Forever A Jackrabbit. 💙🏈🐰 Incase you missed it. 👇🏻 pic.twitter.com/MnN6iOFl1X — GT SD Jack’s 🐰🐰 (@realredsd) August 14, 2026 WR KeAndre Lambert-Smith As a rookie, Lambert-Smith was the favorite target for Trey Lance during the preseason. That relationship picked back up right where it left off on Thursday night. KLS hauled in a team-high four receptions for 58 yards (second on the team) while tying Brenen Thompson for the team lead with six targets. He was also almost on the end of a would-be play-of-the-game when Lance lofted a deep ball up the right sideline on a third-and-long. It was thrown behind, but KLS’ adjustment allowed him to box out the defender which made the ball soar perfectly into his chest. Unfortunately he could not secure it and it ultimately fell incomplete. Still quite the night for KLS who continues to be right there on the fringe of making the active roster depending on just how many the staff wants to keep in their initial 53. TE Jake Pascuzzi A former Iowa tight end which doesn’t make me biased at all here, Pascuzzi finished his career at Tulane where he was a one-year starter. The receiving numbers were never there in his career, but it seems like those Hawkeye fundamentals were drilled in thoroughly nonetheless. Pascuzzi actually finished second behind KLS with three receptions for 39 yards, also good for third on the Bolts offense. Two of those receptions went for first downs which is nice efficiency for the undrafted rookie. The tight end room is stacked, but there’s a potential path for Pascuzzi to stick around as the team’s backup fullback behind Alec Ingold. Scott Matlock has been getting reps at tight end and offensive tackle this camp due to the fullback position now being a totally different role in Mike McDaniels’ offense. Pascuzzi now fits much better there with his skillset over Matlock. Backup fullback is not a rosterable position in the NFL, but it is good enough to be a practice squad lock.

(Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Good morning, Chargers fans! The Bolts may have found a guard who can pick up a stunt by the defensive line. Jake Slaughter looked comfortable in his first game at left guard playing next to both Branson Taylor and Travis Burke who rotated at left tackle. In the clip below, you can see Slaughter recover well after overcommitting to a linemen looping away before getting back to the edge player in time for Trey Lance to make a move and escape the pocket. In another, he passed off a twist with ease which allowed for a comfortable pocket before Lance attempted a deep pass that came oh-so close to being a massive gain. Some Jake Slaughter thoughts: better than I expected in pass pro at LG. In PFF's preliminary charting, just 1 pressure allowed vs. HOU. Some adjustments to be made in the run game + pad level. The Texans sent extra blockers his way early on which is a testament to how he was viewed by the opposition. Both wideout Brenen Thompson and Genesis Smith each had their moments as well. Thompson caught a pair of passes for 30 yards and looked comfortable running routes over the middle. Smith recovered from a DPI penalty to nearly make a one-handed interception in the end zone on the very next play. UDFA defensive tackle Jahmeer Carter was a surprise standout with two tackles for loss and a sack, helping lead the way for a stout interior that denied a pair of fourth downs on the night. title: Other rookie QBs are putting pressure on Ty Simpson before debut
summary: The pressure is on Los Angeles Rams rookie quarterback Ty Simpson before he ever steps onto the field. Several notable first-year signal callers have seen the field this preseason and have played admirably, further putting the heat on Simpson ahead of his expected NFL debut Saturday. It all kicked off with Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck […]
full_text: Woodland Hills, CA - August 11:Rams QB Ty Simpson (15) during Rams joint practice with the Dallas Cowboys on Tuesday, August 11, 2026. (Photo by David Crane/MediaNews Group/Los Angeles Daily News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images The pressure is on Los Angeles Rams rookie quarterback Ty Simpson before he ever steps onto the field. Several notable first-year signal callers have seen the field this preseason and have played admirably, further putting the heat on Simpson ahead of his expected NFL debut Saturday. It all kicked off with Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck in last week’s Hall of Fame Game. Beck went 15-of-19 for 188 yards and a touchdown, showcasing poise and his strong playmaking ability throughout. Although he was ruled out with a rib injury in Arizona’s second preseason game, Beck had shown enough to put himself in line to potentially start for the Redbirds sometime this season, which wouldn’t be surprising. Read more: Cardinals might not be the pushover we expect It’s a shame that Beck didn’t play Thursday against the Raiders, because then fans could’ve seen him pitted against top overall pick Fernando Mendoza. No national championship encore for us, but that’s okay. The lone QB taken ahead of Simpson in the NFL draft played well. Mendoza was efficient, going 10-of-16 for 97 yards and a touchdown in nearly three quarters’ work. The reigning Heisman winner is unlikely to dethrone expected starter Kirk Cousins after one solid performance, yet he has all the makings of a franchise quarterback, something desperately needed in Vegas. View this post on Instagram In the Steelers-Packers matchup Thursday night, Pittsburgh’s Drew Allar exceeded expectations in front of the home crowd. After an underwhelming finish to his Penn State career, lowlighted by a season-ending ankle injury, Allar commanded head coach Mike McCarthy’s offense with ease. The former Nittany Lions star, who was taken with the 76th overall pick, finished the 28-9 win over Green Bay with three total touchdowns. He even had a 74-yard throw on his first drive, which ultimately led to his first score of the night. Steelers rookie QB Drew Allar in his preseason debut: 🏈10-of-13 completions 🏈154 YDS 🏈3 Total touchdowns 🏈0 interceptions pic.twitter.com/88247O6wer — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 14, 2026 While again, we’re only talking about preseason here, Simpson will, fair or not, be compared to his fellow rookie QBs following Saturday’s game. The NFL media and fans love to jump to conclusions immediately after one game. And you can expect that the Simpson bust talk, or questioning the Rams’ judgment for taking him, will occur should he struggle in Kansas City. You just know it’s going to happen too because social media is a cesspool of icy cold takes. TST’s JB Scott noted that Stetson Bennett will likely have a superior supporting cast when he starts against the Chiefs Saturday. By the time Simpson takes the field, he’ll be playing with guys who, to put it kindly, aren’t the cream of the crop. So already, he’s being put at a disadvantage before ever taking the field. Due to his first round draft status, you can expect the pressure to be greater for Simpson this weekend compared to his fellow rookie quarterbacks. Outside of Mendoza, there’s no other signal caller from this year’s draft class who will be scrutinized more than the Rams’ QB.

title: What I’ll be watching for in the Rams opener
summary: The wait is over, Los Angeles Rams football is back. Time to box up those preseason thoughts, all the hype, speculation, and over-reaction. Don’t discard them, just shake them up and repurpose them as post-preseason game analysis. Fortunes will rise and fall, but the stars won’t shine, this production will be left to the understudy’s. […]
full_text: Sean McVay joins fans getting fired up for the preseason (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The wait is over, Los Angeles Rams football is back. Time to box up those preseason thoughts, all the hype, speculation, and over-reaction. Don’t discard them, just shake them up and repurpose them as post-preseason game analysis. Fortunes will rise and fall, but the stars won’t shine, this production will be left to the understudy’s. As expected, the Rams will sit as many as 40 players and the Chiefs are on the same platform . Simple schemes will be the rule. That doesn’t ensure the game will be boring, in last year’s three games, L.A. charted just under 1100 yards of total offense, 672 through the air and 418 on the ground. Here’s what I will be watching for in Saturday’s opening game with the Kansas City Chiefs Quarterback Now that the word has come down that Stetson Bennett will start, it will offer a fans to view both Bennett and Ty Simpson in an enclosed sample. And offers a chance to create some QB controversy. Bennett has shown improvement over his L.A. tenure and should have a solid command of the offensive principles, even as vanilla as they will likely be in an opening preseason game. His glaring problem, that appears to still persist to this day, is his decision making and the resulting lack of ball security. Although Simpson will face media (and fans too) applied post-game pressure, comparing his play to other rookie QB’s without the draft pedigree, on-field pressure will be mostly self-inflicted. In his first NFL action, if Simpson can simply get the team in and out of the huddle, show he can make the proper reads, and put the ball where it belongs, we fans can mark it down as progress. TRENDING: Ty Simpson has been FLASHING as of late at Rams training camp. Simpson’s processing skills and athletic instincts have reportedly “turned heads” since the pads came on. The Rams rookie QB is showing early signs of a PROMISING future 😳 pic.twitter.com/J7L5JkbBkO — Rookie Watch (@RookieWatxh) August 6, 2026 Running back There’s not a lot of rungs on the ladder for Jarquez Hunter to ascend. What he can do is to keep grinding and lock up RB#3. Ronnie Rivers could be vulnerable, last year his snaps were down substantially on both offense and special teams from past couple of seasons. He did fill a small role with 16 kickoff returns (2nd on team). Jordan Waters and Dean Conners will battle for a practice squad berth. Waters offers a combination of size/athleticism and played well last preseason. Conners is a faster/twitchier version of Ronnie Rivers. Shows the base traits of a third down back, tough runner, willing blocker, and good receiver. Wide receiver So far, there is still no clear-cut WR#3. So, it will be about trying to get a read on who is making hay for that role. Of the three odds-on contenders, Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpford, and Xavier Smith, I would expect Whittington to get the afternoon off. Mumpford might be locked in, but should probably play and Smith certainly should. The good news is that the backup receivers played pretty well last preseason. It has been widely reported that the Rams rotated their wideouts between the first and second units all through camp. Tyler Scott had some run with the first team on a couple of occasions, he was highly thought of coming into the league and although he has yet to put it together, I think he has the skills to pressure those just ahead on the depth chart. Rookie CJ Daniels had some early-camp buzz, now gets to do it against live action. While reports were quiet about Brennan Presley and Tru Edwards, Mario Williams showed connection with Ty Simpson on more than a couple of occasions. Tight end To start the season, the cupboard is full, but there are some interesting traits amongst the the backups. Seeing how the Rams line them up, will they lean right into the multi-tight end sets or save it for the regular season? A 13 formation of Max Klare, Dan Villari, and Rohan Jones would be make for some fun mismatches, all have good hands and the potential for run after catch yards. Although Mark Redman is more of a traditional TE, a bit heavy-footed, he’s got hands and is a fine blocker. Max Klare with the first team. pic.twitter.com/AFxTL5Ye0T — Allen Sales (@AllenSales) August 7, 2026 Offensive line As much as I would like to see Keagan Trost in live action, the offensive line depth, or rather the lack of it, may not allow it. Wyatt Bowles was, to my eye, the Rams best preseason lineman last year, showing at both guard and center. Be very cool to see him take another step forward and make the opening roster. With Justin Dedich still out, it is within striking distance. Austin Blaske and Bryce Henderson were interesting undrafted additions and it will be enlightening to see if they can bring something to the table. The remaining guys, AJ Arcuri, Dylan McMahon, Bill Murray, and Blake Hance are all veterans of some ilk and don’t really excite me. Special teams Like everyone else, just seeing an improved overall effort would be a start. Boring down a bit, who’s back for punt and kickoff returners could be interesting, I recall reading numerous names thrown into the returner hat. Hopefully the Rams don’t play it conservative and fair catch everything. Defensive interior It’s fair to want to see and expect a little more from Ty Hamilton, his snaps per game were up in the last year’s stretch drive and playoffs, but he needs to show some dominance against preseason opposition. I like Larrell Murchison, but I don’t see what he can prove by playing that he hasn’t already shown. Bill Norton had a nice 2026 preseason, maybe he can build on it. Tim Keenan is interesting, if he can return to his 2024 college form, he could be a real keeper. Have to admit, I’m indifferent towards the two undrafted rookies, Payton Zdroik and Jaxson Moi. Edge By most reportage, Josiah Stewart and Desjuan Johnson have had solid camps and will likely sit. With five backups, Keir Thomas, Tremon Fox, Wesley Bailey, Darryl Peterson, and Daniel Rickert, L.A. has enough for preseason games. I’ve always respected Thomas’ football prowess, but his tweener size and athleticism make him a tough fit. Fox has been around a few seasons without distinction. Undrafted Bailey has reportedly had reps with the first defense, showing off his stellar size/athleticism. Peterson will have to showcase versatility, IQ, and effort. Recently acquired, Rickert showed some ability to pressure QB’s in his senior college season. Off-ball linebacker Just yesterday, the Rams added former Round 3 draft pick Monty Rice, this hints to me that Shaun Dolac won’t be seeing much preseason action. Not sure if Rice will up to speed by Saturday, but may very well suit up as backup to Nikhai Hill-Green and Elias Neal. I’ll be watching undrafted Hill-Green to see if his college game can transition to the pro level. Pick 6 here by Sean Dolac. pic.twitter.com/LtzvpAEu4j — Allen Sales (@AllenSales) August 7, 2026 Safety Since I have put Nick Anderson on my post-OTA opening 53, his game evaluation will in my notes. Tanner Ingle has been around a few seasons and can compete at this level, his hair-on-fire play style is always a kick. I thought Nate Valcarcel did pretty well last in last year’s preseason games, looking to see if he’s added a little muscle and can still free-range out in center field. Alex Cook comes over from the UFL after bouncing around the NFL for three seasons. Cornerback Although not a big role, finding out who wins the CB#4 does set depth. I have seen clips of both Josh Wallace and Cam Lampkin working with the first defense. Reports are that Cam Lampkin had an outstanding camp. I would expect both to play, at least early in the game. After those two, there a bunch of bodies, but not a lot of game experience. Behind them, the Rams recently added Zech McPherson, a 2021 Round 4 draft pick. He never really broke through on defense with his drafting…

Revel said that facing the Rams in a joint practice on Tuesday “felt easy”, an opinion not many would have expected from a cornerback who has played […]

(Photo by David Crane/MediaNews Group/Los Angeles Daily News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images Dallas Cowboys cornerback Shavon Revel is not a household name, but after his comments about Puka Nacua and other L.A. Rams receivers this week, that could change overnight. Revel said that facing the Rams in a joint practice on Tuesday “felt easy”, an opinion not many would have expected from a cornerback who has played in seven career games and going against an offense with Matthew Stafford, Davante Adams, and Nacua. In a story posted at Dallas Morning News on Friday , Revel says that’s exactly how it felt to him. “That felt easy because I’ve been doing it every day against — in my opinion, personally — the best receivers in the league [Lamb and Pickens] and I felt that throughout this camp.” Revel says that after going against CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens in Cowboys practices everyday, the likes of Nacua and Adams is not up to his usual standards. Lamb and Pickens are one of the better duos in the NFL right now, but should that make Nacua “easy” to guard? Shavon Revel had a realization facing the Rams this week. “Damn, this is easy.” That’s because he is as confident as ever after going up against George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb every day. More on the Cowboys CB becoming who they hoped he could be: https://t.co/nNy59zT216 pic.twitter.com/wEnB4p2J8W — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) August 13, 2026 For what it’s worth, reports out of Oxnard on Tuesday did highlight Revel as one of the best players on the field, including a pass breakup on a fade pass from Stafford to Nacua in the red zone. Another report had Revel breaking up a pass from Stafford to Nacua on a go ball. Shavon Revel having a great day. Playing physical. Forced a fumble and has had two big PBUs on plays where the Rams were clearly testing him. One on a downfield ball to Nacua, another on a fade from the 10-yard line to Nacua. Hasn’t been perfect but it’s been his best day in… — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 11, 2026 👀 two *sacks* early for the #Cowboys first team defense against Matthew Stafford: Donovan Ezeiruaku and Isaiah Land 🔑 run defense looks wonderful Stafford also dropped back early and hurled a go ball to Puka Nacua … Shavon Revel was glued to him step for step: PBU 🔥🔥🔥🔥 — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) August 11, 2026 On a running play, Revel “popped” Rams running back Blake Corum and forced a fumble. Cowboys CB Shavon Revel just had the most casual hit stick I’ve seen. Went to pop a Rams RB and sent him flying and forced a fumble. — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) August 11, 2026 Revel, a third-round pick out of East Carolina in 2025, fell in the draft due to injury concerns. Some had him as a first-rounder prior to those concerns. He ended up returning in Week 11 and starting the final five games of the year. He’s now competing with former Rams cornerback Cobie Durant to start opposite of DaRon Bland, a position battle he may be winning after Tuesday. But beating out Durant to start? Now that sounds easy.

title: Will Aaron Donald have more sacks than Braden Fiske?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are anxiously awaiting the impending return of Aaron Donald. Donald’s return to the Rams will undoubtedly form the greatest defensive line ever to touch the NFL grass. However, Donald’s return does raise questions about how Sean McVay and Chris Shula will get all of their chess pieces on the field…namely Braden […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams are anxiously awaiting the impending return of Aaron Donald. Donald’s return to the Rams will undoubtedly form the greatest defensive line ever to touch the NFL grass. However, Donald’s return does raise questions about how Sean McVay and Chris Shula will get all of their chess pieces on the field…namely Braden Fiske. Is Braden Fiske going to see a reduction in playing time? Or will he be used in pass rushing situations exclusively? This naturally brings up an interesting question: Who will finish with more sacks — Aaron Donald or Braden Fiske? After walking away from football following the 2023 season, Donald’s potential return has become one of the biggest storylines surrounding the Rams. Head coach Sean McVay confirmed in July that Donald was going through a process to determine whether he wanted to return, and recent reports have shown the future Hall of Famer working out with other Rams defensive linemen…coincidentally Braden Fiske. If Donald does return, the question becomes less about whether he can still be productive and more about how the Rams will use him. That is where Braden Fiske enters the conversation. Fiske burst onto the scene as a rookie in 2024, recording 8.5 sacks — the third-most in a season by a rookie in Rams history. He also produced 51 pressures and 40 hurries from the interior. His second season was much quieter statistically, as he finished with just three sacks, but injuries contributed to a season in which he acknowledged he wasn’t playing at his best physically. Fiske has entered 2026 saying he feels healthy and ready for a bounce-back season. Myles Garrett’s presence should create opportunities throughout the Rams’ defensive front. Opposing offenses cannot afford to devote all of their protection toward Kobie Turner, Braden Fiske, or Aaron Donald when Garrett is capable of destroying a game from the edge. Fiske himself recently acknowledged that Garrett is not exactly a normal player and that his presence can change how offenses approach the Rams’ defensive line. We asked fans via our FanDuel reacts poll and the results were pretty telling. As expected, the vote went in favor of the 3x Defensive Player of the Year. But Braden Fiske did receive a 36% voting share; showing that there is fan optimism in the third year player. For Donald, the question is durability and workload. At 35 years old and coming off a two-year absence, expecting the three-time Defensive Player of the Year to immediately return to an 80-percent snap role would be unrealistic. A more specialized role could actually make more sense. Donald could be unleashed primarily in obvious passing situations, allowing the Rams to maximize his greatest remaining strength: getting after the quarterback. That could result in fewer total snaps but a surprisingly high sack total. Fiske, meanwhile, has youth on his side and already demonstrated that he can produce sacks from the interior. If he stays healthy and receives enough opportunities alongside Myles Garrett, he could return to — or even surpass — his rookie production. Donald has the higher ceiling, but Fiske has youth and break out potential. If Donald plays a limited role, Fiske could easily lead the Rams in sacks. If Donald returns looking anything close to the player Rams fans remember, however, it would be foolish to bet against him. Ultimately, the question isn’t whether Donald or Fiske can get to the quarterback…It’s which one gets there more often in 2026?
author: Steven Ridings

title: Chiefs have backup QB intrigue entering Rams matchup
summary: Ahead of their preseason opener, the Los Angeles Rams’ backup quarterback situation appears relatively straightforward. Their opponent, the Kansas City Chiefs, appear to be in the same boat, but have a potentially intriguing battle at the No. 3 spot behind Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields. As previously stated, the Rams’ backup quarterback battle behind Matthew […]
full_text: ST JOSEPH, MISSOURI - JULY 30: Quarterbacks Chris Oladokun #19, Garrett Nussmeier #14, Patrick Mahomes #15 and Justin Fields #6 walk toward the practice field during Kansas City Chiefs training camp at Missouri Western State University on July 30, 2026 in St Joseph, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ahead of their preseason opener, the Los Angeles Rams’ backup quarterback situation appears relatively straightforward. Their opponent, the Kansas City Chiefs, appear to be in the same boat, but have a potentially intriguing battle at the No. 3 spot behind Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields. As previously stated, the Rams’ backup quarterback battle behind Matthew Stafford is more cut-and-dried. The team’s first unofficial depth chart listed Stetson Bennett as the backup to the reigning MVP, with rookie Ty Simpson closely behind in the No. 3 spot. For the Chiefs, it’s more up in the air, even if the primary backup position behind Mahomes appears set ahead of the regular season. Read more: Rams depth chart revealed ahead of first preseason game In their first unofficial depth chart , Fields holds the QB2 role, with rookie Garrett Nussmeier at No. 3 and fifth-year signal caller Chris Oladokun at No. 4. All three players are expected to split reps against the Rams on Saturday. Patrick Mahomes will not play on Saturday, per Coach Reid. Justin Fields, Garrett Nussmeier and Chris Oladokun will split up the game. — Matt McMullen (@KCChiefs_Matt) August 13, 2026 At first glance, it’s somewhat surprising to see Nussmeier ahead of Oladokun. While Kansas City selected Nussmeier in the seventh round of this year’s NFL draft, Oladokun has more experience with the offense, including a surprise start in 2025. During a Christmas Day game against the eventual top-seeded Broncos, Oladokun was put in an impossible situation. KC was already eliminated from playoff contention. Mahomes and his backup Gardner Minshew were out with season-ending injuries, so it was his turn to start. All the Chiefs could do was play spoiler, and they did, albeit in one of the ugliest games of the year. Oladokun didn’t play overly well, but he didn’t cost his team the game in a closer-than-expected 20-13 loss. He went 13-of-22 passing for only 66 yards, but threw a first half touchdown to running back Brashard Smith that helped give the Chiefs a 7-6 advantage at halftime. After waiting four years on the practice squad, Oladokun nearly led a monumental upset in his first NFL start. Despite hitting Travis Kelce three times for 23 yards and having a 7-yard rush on the potential game-tying drive, a costly penalty and two incomplete passes doomed the Chiefs. Even in a losing effort, Oladokun earned respect around the league and undoubtedly from the locker room. He again came up short the following week in a two-point loss to the Raiders. Expect Oladokun to at least make things interesting at KC’s No. 3 spot, especially if he continues to split the reps throughout the preseason. Nussmeier is another interesting prospect, as he threw 42 touchdown passes in his final two seasons at LSU. Injuries hampered him during the 2025 campaign, but he still managed to become the third-ranked quarterback on The Athletic’s Dane Brugler’s draft board , behind Fernando Mendoza and Simpson. Missing time certainly hurt his draft stock, yet the former Tigers star made up for it in the Senior Bowl. Nussmeier completed 5-of-8 passes for 57 yards and rushed for the game’s opening touchdown. Although he threw an interception — which ultimately wasn’t his fault, as it went through the receiver’s hands — he wasn’t docked for it, earning MVP honors for his efforts. Former @LSUfootball QB Garrett Nussmeier takes it in for the score at the @seniorbowl 🙌 @Garrettnuss13 pic.twitter.com/bjLgSRbYFR — NFL Network (@nflnetwork) January 31, 2026 Nothing should be considered a lock as the Chiefs figure out what they have in Fields and especially in Nussmeier and Oladokun. The rookie from LSU offers a high upside, while Oladokun has some NFL starting experience. There isn’t anything resembling a quarterback controversy in KC, but there’s still plenty of excitement on the opposing sideline for Rams fans.
