title: Jason Pinnock-Tyler Nubin competition an awkward one between friends
summary: The New York Giants finally got their guy at defensive coordinator in 2026. The Giants wanted Dennard Wilson to run their defense after the messy divorce between Brian Daboll and Wink Martindale. Wilson has had a long and winding road through the NFL’s coaching ranks, but he coached under Mike MacDonald for the Baltimore Ravens […]
full_text: New York Giants safety Jason Pinnock (25) catches a ball in practice.﻿ | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The New York Giants finally got their guy at defensive coordinator in 2026. The Giants wanted Dennard Wilson to run their defense after the messy divorce between Brian Daboll and Wink Martindale. Wilson has had a long and winding road through the NFL’s coaching ranks, but he coached under Mike MacDonald for the Baltimore Ravens and is familiar with the “Ravens” style defense that Martindale installed. Instead, Wilson went to the Tennessee Titans, and former Titans defensive coordinator Shane Bowen came to the Giants. Now, Wilson has come from Tennessee to run the Giants’ defense for former Ravens’ head coach John Harbaugh Safety Jason Pinnock was there for it all, and noted the difference between Martindale, Bowen, and now Wilson after Practice on Wednesday. Pinnock said that the defense is similar, in some ways, to what Martindale ran… And also much more of an “attack-style” defense than what Bowen ran in 2024. “Front-wise, I guess, and a little bit tighter back end,” Pinnock said, comparing Wilson’s defense to Martindale and Bowen’s schemes. “You know, Wink was a bit more pressure-based. … But just the looks, everything, I won’t go too much in detail. But very similar.” The Giants’ new coaching staff has promised clean slates all around, and that means that everyone is fighting for their jobs, which also means guys like Pinnock have the chance to move up the depth chart. “It’s going to be tough, you know? It’s going to be however the cards are dealt,” Pinnock said.“‘Best man win’ type of thing. You’ve got so many packages you can play with. I played in this defense before. It’s like [with] Wink (Martindale), ‘22, ‘23. So, I’m very familiar with it. Kind of the same calls. It’s going to be fun. It’s going to be fun.” Of course, the Giants’ front seven looks just a bit different from the 2023 season. That year, the Giants didn’t have Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, Tremaine Edmunds, or Arvell Reese creating havoc up front. Now, the Giants boast one of the — if not the — longest and most athletic defensive fronts in the NFL. It’s a group of players that promises to be disruptive, both behind the line of scrimmage and using their length to clog passing lanes even when they can’t get to the passer.” Pinnock notes that the Giants’ front is going to make game-changing plays this year through their sheer length and athleticism. “I’ll start with Arvell. Yeah, I mean, he’s a freak, man,” Pinnock said. “Y’all was in that back corner? You caught that one here yesterday?” He said, talking about the highlight-reel one-handed interception Reese made in Tuesday’s practice. “Yeah, so there you go. So, that’ll answer that. That’s a big middle. That’s a big middle, bro, (inside linebacker) Tremaine (Edmunds) and him. That’s – good luck. And you talk about tips just from the D-line. We’re going to get a couple just off that. “And then (Colton) Hood, man, just a competitor and smart,” Pinnock said of the rookie cornerback. “He kind of reminded me of me. Like, I was a real, like – I diagnosed a lot, even though I was a corner, so that was kind of why the transition was a little bit easier. He’s smart. He’s smart. So, it’s going to help him in this league.” Hood is in the four-way competition to be a starting corner for the Giants, and it seems to be an active one. ‘May the best man win’, as Pinnock put it, is a common theme in the Giants’ secondary. In fact, Pinnock finds himself in competition with third year safety Tyler Nubin — a player who now wears his number. “That’s my brother, man. Like, (one) call away,” Pinnock said. “I’m at his baby shower. He’s at my baby shower. He’s going to be at my wedding. Like, that’s my guy. That’s my guy, so – man, this is what comes with the sport. We’re on each other. We’re probably each other’s biggest competitor” Pinnock has the unique perspective of having seen Nubin, as well as his fellow young DBs Deonte Banks and Dru Phillips as rookies, and then spending a year away from the team. Pinnock notes that Banks, in particular, is more focused than he was in his first two years. “I would say the focus,” Pinnock said, when asked the biggest difference in Banks between 2024 and 2026. “A little bit more attention to detail on how to study. And I was trying to guide him as much – different room but still give him guidance because that’s where I was drafted, as a corner. And then, for me, it was a bit more glaring, too, coming back because I had a year off. … But just sharper, man. Sharper, takes the game more seriously.” Of course, while Pinnock is one of the elder statesmen of the secondary, he’s still a young player in his own right. He’s going against a venerable veteran in Odell Beckham Jr. In fact, Pinnock made the 33-year old Beckham feel old earlier this off-season. “I had to confess to him in the locker room,” Pinnock said. “It was like 2016, 2017. I had him as my screensaver in high school. He was like, ‘Don’t tell me that. That would make me feel a little old.’ But it’s crazy. It’s kind of like idol turned rival.” “Doesn’t look like he lost a step to me,” Pinnock added, “from what I was watching when I was in high school.” If Beckham keeps stepping up in practice, he has a good chance of making the team. And if so, the Giants certainly hope he hasn’t lost a step.
author: Chris Pflum

title: Marcus Mbow at center? Giants won’t be playing him there any time soon
summary: The New York Giants are dealing with injuries at the center position right now. Starter John Michael Schmitz is out with a concussion. Veteran backup Lucas Patrick has been limited all summer by a knee issue, and missed several recent practices. That has left the Giants with 2025 practice squad players Bryan Hudson and Jake […]
full_text: Marcus Mbow | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants are dealing with injuries at the center position right now. Starter John Michael Schmitz is out with a concussion. Veteran backup Lucas Patrick has been limited all summer by a knee issue, and missed several recent practices. That has left the Giants with 2025 practice squad players Bryan Hudson and Jake Kubas at center, along with recently-signed veteran Brenden Jaimes. Some might think this would be the perfect opportunity to see second-year offensive lineman Marcus Mbow get some reps at the center position. The 2025 fifth-round pick was thought to have five-position flexibility when the Giants drafted him. To date, though, he has played only tackle. Offensive line coach Mike Bloomgren revealed on Thursday that the Giants did look at Mbow at center during the spring. Briefly. As in, for one practice. “It’s [Mbow at center] been talked about in the building,” Bloomgren said. “There was a day in OTAs where he took some snaps or snapped the ball a little bit. “Right now, he’s more comfortable playing tackle. And I’m pretty comfortable with what he’s doing out there.” So, maybe down the line Mbow will get a real look at center. Not now. Schmitz will return from his concussion soon. Patrick is a capable backup, if healthy. If he isn’t healthy, Hudson and perhaps Kubas will get chances to prove they can be the No. 2 center. If the Giants find them wanting, maybe they look outside the current roster for an answer. Could that be former Giant starting guard Greg Van Roten, who has some center experience? Perhaps. It is clear, though, that the answer won’t be Mbow. Not this season.

title: NY Giants 53-man roster projection: Locks, bubble players, long shots as preseason begins
summary: There are spots to be won, and lots of decisions to be made regarding the New York Giants’ 53-man roster before their regular-season opener on September 13 against the Dallas Cowboys. Where do things stand as the Giants prepare to open their preseason on Saturday against the Minnesota Vikings? Let’s look at the locks, bubble […]
full_text: There are spots to be won, and lots of decisions to be made regarding the New York Giants’ 53-man roster before their regular-season opener on September 13 against the Dallas Cowboys. Where do things stand as the Giants prepare to open their preseason on Saturday against the Minnesota Vikings? Let’s look at the locks, bubble players, and long shots as the true training camp portion of the season ends, and teams shift into more of a preseason mode centered around games. Quarterback Locks (2) — Jaxson Dart, Jameis Winston Bubble players (0) — None Long shot (1) — Brandon Allen [No change] John Harbaugh would not say whether or nto Jaxson Dart and other starters will play vs. the Vikings. Maybe we see a little of Dart and Jameis Winston. We will probably see a lot of Brandon Allen. My guess is that we do see a little of Dart. He is a second-year quarterback learning a new scheme, and Harbaugh does not like to pass up opportunities for players to learn and grow. “I value first team reps very much. And you have to measure that against the risk,” Harbaugh said. “So, there is risk as well. And that’s part of it, too. And you have to make that decision.” Harbaugh said the Giants have an individualized plan “by guy.” We will see what the plan is for Dart on Saturtday. Running back Locks (3) — Cam Skattebo, Tyrone Tracy, Devin Singletary Bubble players (1) — Dante Miller Long shots (2) — Eric Gray, Damon Bankston [No change] The only interesting development this week was head coach John Harbaugh praising Dante Miller. “He’s explosive,” Harbaugh aid. “He’s had catches. He caught one today long. He’s had runs where he’s shown acceleration.” Of course, he also said Eric Gray “knows how to run the football”, and Damon Bankston has “had big plays, too.” So, really it just seemed like Harbaugh trying to say something nice about everybody. I would think we see a lot of Miller, Gray, and Bankston on Saturday. Fullback Locks (1) — Patrick Ricard Bubble players (0) Long shots (1) — Grant Finley [No change] Finley, like Ricard, has a background as BOTH a fullback and defensive lineman. Can Harbaugh turn him into Ricard 2.0? Tight end Locks (3) — Isaiah Likely, Theo Johnson, Chris Manhertz Bubble players (2) — Tanner Conner, Thomas Fidone Long shot (0) [ Change: Fidone moved from long shot to bubble] Second-year tight end Thomas Fidone had a good week of practice, resulting in a bump up for him. Still, I don’t see how Fidone or Tanner Conner can make the team. Wide receiver Locks (5) — Malik Nabers, Darius Slayton, Calvin Austin, Darnell Mooney, Malachi Fields Bubble players (4) — Odell Beckham Jr., Braxton Berrios, Dalen Cambre, Jalin Hyatt Long shots (4) — Ryan Miller, Xavier Gipson, Isaiah Hodgins, JuJu Smith-Schuster [ Change: JuJu Smith-Schuster moves from bubble to long shot] I hate moving guys down because of injuries, but the best ability is availability. While other players have been on the field making plays, Smith-Schuster has been in the training room working on what Harbaugh calls his “old knee.” Odell Beckham will play Saturday vs. the Vikings. My gut says he won’t be out there for long. As for Saturday, doing well in practice is nice. For bubble players looking to win a roster spot, though, making plays in games will go a long way. Offensive line Locks (7) — Andrew Thomas, Jon Runyan, John Michael Schmitz, Francis Mauigoa, Jermaine Eluemunor, Marcus Mbow, Daniel Faalele Bubble players (5) — J.C. Davis, Lucas Patrick, Bryan Hudson, Josh Ezeudu, Aaron Stinnie Long shots (5) — Evan Neal, Ryan Schernecke, Jake Kubas, Jarrod Gray (International Exemption), Brendan Jaimes [No change] With John Michael Schmitz (concussion) and Lucas Patrick (knee) ailing, Bryan Hudson and Jake Kubas will have an opportunity to make an impression. Both players were on the Giants’ practice squad last season. If neither plays well, and there is concern about Patrick’s knee, could the Giants turn back to someone like Greg Van Roten as center insurance? Defensive line Locks (4) — D.J. Reader, Darius Alexander, Shelby Harris, Chauncey Golston Bubble players (4) — Bobby Jamison-Travis, Leki Fotu, Zacch Pickens, Josh Tupou Long shots (2) — Anquin Barnes Jr., Marlon Davidson [ Change: Sam Roberts released] Sixth-round pick Bobby Jamison-Travis has had a quiet camp. He needs to show disruption at the point of attack. The rest of the “bubble” and “long shot” players need to show the Giants why they shouldn’t be scanning the waiver wire for upgrades when teams make cuts to get to the 53-man roster limit. I think there could easily be at least one defensive lineman on the roster who isn’t a Giant today. Off-ball linebacker Locks (4) — Arvell Reese, Tremaine Edmunds, Micah McFadden, Jack Kelly Bubble players (2) — Darius Muasau, Zaire Barnes Long shots (1) — Anfernee Orji [No change] I don’t know if we will see No. 5 overall pick Arvell Reese on Saturday. We should see a lot of Micah McFadden and Jack Kelly, though, and that might be fun. Edge defender Locks (3) — Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, Kayvon Thibodeaux Bubble players (1) — Khalid Kareem Long shots (2) — Trace Ford, Caleb Murphy [No change] I still see only the three edge defenders making the 53-man roster. Cornerback Locks (5) — Paulson Adebo, Greg Newsome II, Colton Hood, Dru Phillips, Deonte Banks Bubble players (3) — Art Green, Nic Jones, Korie Black Long shots (2) — Ugochukwu Amadi, Sam Webb [ Change: David Long, D.J. James released; Ugochukwu Amadi and Sam Webb signed.] The Giants are a mess at cornerback right now. Ugochukwu Amadi and Sam Webb, who were just signed on Thursday, are probably going to have to play a significant number of snaps on Saturday. I won’t move him to the ‘locks’ category yet, but Art Green is trending toward making the 53-man roster. He is a core special-teamer who practices with the first special teams unit, and he has made some plays while getting increased reps with the rash of injuries at cornerback. Safety Locks (3) — Jevon Holland, Tyler Nubin, Ar’Darius Washington Bubble players (2) — Elijah Campbell, Jason Pinnock Long shots (3) — Beau Brade, Raheem Layne, J.T. Woods [ Change: J.T. Woods added to roster] If there is a competition developing between Tyler Nubin and Jason Pinnock, it is an awkward one. “I’m at his baby shower. He’s at my baby shower. He’s going to be at my wedding,” Pinnock said this week. “Like, that’s my guy. That’s my guy, so – man, this is what comes with the sport. We’re on each other. We’re probably each other’s biggest competitor, and we’re on each other, bro. Like, it’s just – it’s what it is. It comes with the nature.” Special teams Locks (1) — Jordan Stout (punter) Bubble players (2) — Dominic Zvada (placekicker), Ben Mann (long-snapper) Long shot (1) — Ben Sauls (placekicker) [No change] I am not sure Ben Sauls can wrestle the placekicking job away from Dominic Zvada at this point. I do believe Sauls can kick in the NFL. Totals Locks: 41 Bubble players: 26 Long shots: 24 NOTE: The Giants have 91 players since they are carrying one player (Gray) with an International Exemption

title: NY Giants news: Malik Nabers takes step forward
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about after Day 14 of Giants training camp. Who is the Giants’ top performer so far at camp? | ESPN.com TE Isaiah Likely. The offseason acquisition has been the Giants’ No. 1 receiver with Malik Nabers not participating in team drills. He’s been quarterback Jaxson Dart’s […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about after Day 14 of Giants training camp. Who is the Giants’ top performer so far at camp? | ESPN.com TE Isaiah Likely. The offseason acquisition has been the Giants’ No. 1 receiver with Malik Nabers not participating in team drills. He’s been quarterback Jaxson Dart’s safety net, leading all first-team receivers in catches by a wide margin. “Zay’s done a great job,” offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said. The way Likely smoothly gets in and out of breaks has just looked different from incumbent starter Theo Johnson. He also seems to have the best handle on the new offense given his familiarity with coach John Harbaugh and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman from Baltimore. Given the way Dart likes to throw to his tight ends, it suggests that Likely is in for a breakout season given the chemistry they already have developed. Harbaugh on preseason playing time "I value first-team reps very much. You have to measure that against the risk. There is risk, as well." John Harbaugh talks about the risk and reward of playing the Giants' starters in the preseason: pic.twitter.com/azk1sfEVOz — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) August 13, 2026 The somewhat awkward position battle unfolding at Giants camp | New York Post Jason Pinnock hasn’t reacquired his old No. 27 jersey number from his former protégé Tyler Nubin, but he has begun to steal away some starting safety snaps. Pinnock and Nubin are close enough friends that they are invited to each other’s baby showers — and Nubin to Pinnock’s upcoming wedding — but that doesn’t mean the battle for playing time is not intense. Quite the opposite, actually. The Giants listed Nubin and Holland as starters and Pinnock and Washington as backups on their first unofficial depth chart. Holland’s place is secure, while Nubin has gone from the beneficiary of early quiet praise from Harbaugh to rocky footing. “That’s my brother,” Pinnock said, “[but] this is what comes with the sport. We’re on each other. We’re probably each other’s biggest competitor, and we’re on each other’s ass. It just is what it is.” Do Giants need reinforcements at RB, or can Cam Skattebo, Tyrone Tracy Jr. carry the load? | The Athletic Last year, the Giants finished 18th in yards per carry (4.3), 25th in rushing success rate and 16th in explosive run rate. However, some of the heavy lifting in those numbers was done by quarterback Jaxson Dart, who rushed for 487 yards and nine scores last season. When you remove QB runs, the Giants fell to 25th in yards per carry (4.0), 27th in rushing success rate and 20th in explosive run rate. Those numbers beg the question: Do the Giants have the necessary components to be as effective on the ground as they want to be? From idol to teammate: New York Giants players in awe of Odell Beckham Jr. | USAToday.com “I think as a player, he’s still the same caliber player, but I’ve never been around him in a building,” said Winston. “I only knew him as this football icon, the guy that made one-handed catches, and if you put the ball in his hand, he was going to make a play. “But to see him being the teammate that he is — it’s very funny seeing he and Malachi (Fields). Because Malachi — most of the young guys — they’re Odell Beckham Jr. fans. It’s true. Jalin Hyatt got 13 because he’s an Odell Beckham Jr. fan. So, it’s fun to see him putting the past in the past and focusing on getting better every day.” Giants’ John Harbaugh pushes back on ‘way overblown’ narrative | NJ.com So what does Harbaugh think of the notion that he could wear down the Giants by conducting this sort of camp? “I feel like it’s just football practice,” he said, adding that he wants players who love football. “So these practices out here, I think it’s way overblown about how hard they are. They’re good, crisp, sharp, efficient practices. We’re chasing the fundamentals. We’re trying to understand situations. We’re trying to build our systems out, so we can execute under pressure and be our best. That’s what we’re working toward.” Mike Lupica: It’s no regular preseason game for John Harbaugh, Giants | New York Daily News Whatever the Giants are going to be — and whether or not they can be what they once were — all begins on Saturday afternoon against the Vikings. Preseason game or not. This is where the John Harbaugh Era begins, with the new coach under more pressure on his way through the door as any Giants coach has ever faced. Whether or not Dart is on the field Saturday, Giants fans will let Harbaugh know — long and loud — just how happy they are that he is on that field…Then Harbaugh hit the open market. The Giants needed someone exactly like him so much they probably would have thrown in naming rights to the big, ugly gray bowl if he’d asked for that. And from the day he was hired, he really has been swept along by the sound of applause. Giants fans don’t just want Harbaugh on that wall. They need him on that wall. Sometimes even the first preseason game feels as if it matters. It’s because of how much Giants fans want their team to matter again. title: Jets vs Buccaneers Game Thread
summary: The long NFL offseason ends for the New York Jets tonight at 7:00 pm EDT. The Jets are at home in East Rutherford, New Jersey to take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in both teams’ 2026 preseason opener. NFL teams in recent years have increasingly held their starters out of preseason games in a bid […]
full_text: FLORHAM PARK, NEW JERSEY - JULY 29: Aaron Glenn head coach of the New York Jets looks on during training camp at Atlantic Health Jets Training Center on July 29, 2026 in Florham Park, New Jersey. (Photo by Adam Hunger/Getty Images) | Getty Images The long NFL offseason ends for the New York Jets tonight at 7:00 pm EDT. The Jets are at home in East Rutherford, New Jersey to take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in both teams’ 2026 preseason opener. NFL teams in recent years have increasingly held their starters out of preseason games in a bid to avoid injuries prior to the regular season. Jets head coach Aaron Glenn has decided to go the opposite route this year, with the starters slated for about one half worth of snaps spread across the three preseason games. That means the starters will likely see just one or two drives per game before the backups start to fill in. Once the starters exit the game we get to watch a bunch of back of the roster type players play marginal NFL football while fighting for the final open roster spots. Tonight is a big night for the so-called bubble players. The biggest thing for the two teams will be coming out of this game without any serious injuries, if fortune allows. For the bubble players, it’s an audition, not just for their respective teams, but for every team in the NFL. With the shortened preseason schedule there are few opportunities to put good things on tape for the rest of the league to see. Tonight is one of those opportunities. Players who don’t end up making it through final cuts have a chance here to showcase their skills for the entire league, which might earn them a shot with a different franchise down the road. One thing to keep an eye on is the order of when players enter the game. This tends to correspond pretty closely to the team’s depth chart, so we get an early glimpse at who might be leading their positions in the battles for roster spots. It’s the Jets and the Buccaneers in the first of three preseason games for both teams. Jets football is back! Enjoy the game everybody.

title: Scouting Jets defensive tackle Junior Tafuna
summary: The Jets recently claimed defensive tackle Junior Tafuna off waivers from the Houston Texans. Today, we break Tafuna down in detail. The 25-year old Tafuna is listed at 6’3” and 305 pounds and was a three-time all-Pac 12 second-teamer who went undrafted out of Utah. He spent last season on the Houston Texans’ practice squad. […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-AUGUST 23: Detroit Lions guard Zack Johnson #77 defends against Houston Texans defensive tackle Junior Tafuna #53 during the second half of an NFL football game between the Houston Texans and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Saturday, August 23, 2025 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images The Jets recently claimed defensive tackle Junior Tafuna off waivers from the Houston Texans. Today, we break Tafuna down in detail. The 25-year old Tafuna is listed at 6’3” and 305 pounds and was a three-time all-Pac 12 second-teamer who went undrafted out of Utah. He spent last season on the Houston Texans’ practice squad. Background Tafuna was a three-star high school recruit who headed to Utah but went on a mormon mission initially so he didn’t play for them until 2021. In his first season, Tafuna was the Pac 12’s defensive freshman of the year and an all-conference second-teamer after racking up 33 tackles and 4.5 sacks. Over the next three seasons, he failed to deliver the same kind of impact production as he only had three more sacks. However, he still played well enough to earn second-team recognition twice more and then, after the move into the Big 12 in 2024, he was an honorable mention. He ended his career with 108 tackles, 15 tackles for loss, 7.5 sacks, eight passes defensed and two interceptions. Tafuna was widely expected to be a late round draft pick in the 2025 draft after being invited to the scouting combine and performing well at the senior bowl where he had two sacks in the game itself. However, he wasn’t selected and ended up signing for the Houston Texans. After final cuts, he ended up on their practice squad and didn’t see the field in his rookie season. The Jets picked him up earlier this month when he was waived by the Texans. Let’s move onto some more in-depth analysis of what Tafuna brings to the table, based on in-depth research and film study. Measurables/Athleticism Tafuna is undersized for an interior defender at the NFL level, although he has adequate length. His measurables are solid but unspectacular. He ran a 5.04 in the 40-yard dash with 24 bench press reps and average agility and explosiveness numbers. He actually ran a 4.6 in high school but was just 220 pounds at the time. Usage Having played as a running back, linebacker and defensive end in high school, Tafuna was originally recruited with the intention of playing on the edge. However, when he returned from his mission, he had added weight and the team opted to convert him into a defensive tackle role instead. Within that role, he lined up all over the line, but primarily in the B-gap. Motor Tafuna is considered someone with a high motor, who hustles and gives a good effort. He played between 400 and 500 snaps in each of his four seasons, including as many as 69 in one game, so he can handle a starter’s workload. Pass rush Tafuna’s pressure rates were low throughout his career and his sacks dried up after a promising first season. He only had one full sack and two-half sacks in his last two seasons, with zero quarterback hits other than that. He did register five pressures against Utah State last season, though. He can be effective on stunts and collapsing the pocket. Run defense Tafuna moves well down the line and has good quickness. He also improved his run defense consistency over the course of his college career. However, he might need to add some strength because he can struggle to hold his ground in the trenches. Even so, he has a strong upper body and can flash with moments of explosiveness or dominance. Technique Tafuna attacks blockers and has strong hands and although at times he can be late with them, or hold them too low, his technique is generally pretty solid. He doesn’t bring much to the table in terms of pass rush moves but his pure strength makes him a bull rush threat when he can get under his blocker’s pads. Special teams Tafuna’s only roles on special teams at Utah were rushing kicks and punts, but he didn’t have any blocked kicks in college. He had one defensive penalty. Tackling Tafuna’s tackle efficiency was excellent last season as he didn’t have a single missed tackle. He had 11 during his first three seasons. He had one forced fumble during his college career but it came on an impressive play where he hit Bucky Irving hard in the hole and stripped the ball away from him cleanly. Coverage Tafuna only dropped into coverage once in his college career, but he had some good production against the pass with two interceptions and eight passes defensed. He has a knack of getting his hands up to deflect passes, at least two of which were intercepted by a teammate. Instincts/Intelligence Tafuna is a player who is capable of making reads and identifying keys. He also reacts well. He was on the Pac 12 academic honor roll in both 2021 and 2023. Attitude/Demeanor Tafuna is a tireless worker with a high character, who became a team leader as a sophomore and was a captain in his final season at Utah. He is an emotional motivator and a good mentor, who did plenty of work in the community in addition to his mission in Cabo Verde. He reportedly set a good example by putting a lot of work into his preparation and on-field focus. On-field discipline wasn’t a major issue as he had eight defensive penalties in his career with the only two penalties he had in 2024 both being for delay of game. This included one that came on 3rd-and-1 to extend a drive. He also had a roughing the passer penalty in NFL preseason action. Injuries Tafuna only missed two games in 2024, both due to an undisclosed non-football injury. Otherwise, he was durable with 45 starts and three more appearances off the bench in his career. However, he was banged up with bumps and nagging injuries in his middle two seasons. Scheme Fit Tafuna’s role within the Jets’ current defense would mostly likely be as a defensive end in odd-man fronts. He was a teammate of current Jet Kingsley Jonathan while in Houston, albeit for just two weeks. Conclusions Tafuna is a player who was arguably unlucky not to be drafted, with the fact he was an older prospect perhaps having been a factor in that. Nevertheless, he wasn’t able to make his mark with the Texans, so he’s back to square one as he tries to earn a role with the Jets. New York are far from loaded at the interior defensive line positions and guys like David Onyemata and Harrison Phillips might not be here after this season, so there could be a good opportunity here to become part of the pipeline. Tafuna will face competition from some of the Jets’ other young 300-plus pounders though.

summary: No, not Brandon Graham. Nor Brandon Gowton. The Philadelphia Eagles are signing free agent linebacker Brandon George, according to a report from NFL insider Jeremy Fowler. George, 25, is a local area guy, having grown up in Reading, Pennsylvania before playing college football at Pitt. He signed with the Kansas City Chiefs as an undrafted […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 30: Kansas City Chiefs linebacker Brandon George (50) during training camp on July 30, 2025 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images No, not Brandon Graham. Nor Brandon Gowton. The Philadelphia Eagles are signing free agent linebacker Brandon George , according to a report from NFL insider Jeremy Fowler . George, 25, is a local area guy, having grown up in Reading, Pennsylvania before playing college football at Pitt. He signed with the Kansas City Chiefs as an undrafted rookie free agent following the 2025 NFL Draft. Based on the Chiefs’ pre-draft interest in George , there seemed to be some thought he might make their roster. He instead spent the entire 2025 season on injured reserve. George was then waived by the Chiefs earlier this year in May to make room for their 2026 UDFA signings. Now in Philly, George will be fighting an uphill battle to make the roster; the Eagles already have a lot of talent and depth at off-ball linebacker (though it’s worth noting Chance Campbell has recently been limited in practice due to a groin injury). He can strengthen his case to stick around by really standing out on special teams. At the very least, George will help to fill practice and preseason reps. As of this writing, the Eagles have yet to announce a corresponding move to make room for George on their roster. Stay tuned for updates. George scouting report via NFL.com’s Lance Zierlein : Inside linebacker who boasts a burly frame and outstanding pro-day testing numbers. George was a mainstay on special teams during his six-year career, spending only one season (2024) as a full-time starter. He’s inconsistent in making reads and fitting up the run properly, but he’s big and strong. He can leverage his gaps when he’s in position. He’s a build-up runner who lacks the necessary burst to patrol from sideline to sideline, and he’s a liability in coverage. George’s testing, measurables and special-teams experience might appeal to teams, but likely as an undrafted free agent. title: Eagles Film Review: Tyler Steen is a perfectly capable starting guard
summary: Over the past few weeks, I’ve been spending a lot of time watching offensive line film as part of my work with The Scouting Academy. One of the five offensive linemen I have to evaluate for the course is Tyler Steen, which made this pretty perfect timing considering how many of you have asked me […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 20: Tyler Steen #56 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during an NFL football game against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on December 20, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Over the past few weeks, I’ve been spending a lot of time watching offensive line film as part of my work with The Scouting Academy. One of the five offensive linemen I have to evaluate for the course is Tyler Steen, which made this pretty perfect timing considering how many of you have asked me for a more detailed look at his game. After watching hours (and hours…) of clinics, I was interested to see whether my opinion of Steen had changed as I studied him, and it has! I came away from this study more impressed with Steen as a run blocker than before, while slightly more concerned about his pass protection. It is also important to remember the context here. This was Steen’s first full season playing right guard at the NFL level. The Eagles’ offensive line also played poorly, and Lane Johnson missed half the season. Overall, there is plenty to like. There is also plenty that needs to improve. Just FYI, I didn’t include film here to back up my work as I usually do, because I’m writing this while on holiday and the film I used for the Scouting Academy isn’t available to share publicly or record in the normal way. However, before I went away, I recorded a video on Steen’s film for my Patreon , so if you want to see me break down his play in video form, please check it out there! Right, enough pointless chat, let’s go! Strengths Athletic Ability and Movement Skills This is easily the biggest reason to remain optimistic about Steen. He is an excellent athlete for an interior offensive lineman. His first-step quickness immediately stands out on film. Steen can explode out of his stance and cover ground extremely quickly, particularly when he is asked to work laterally or climb to the second level. There are difficult reach blocks that Steen makes look relatively straightforward because of how quickly he can get himself across a defender’s face. When the Eagles ask him to reach defenders on outside zone runs, he has the foot speed to get to the defender’s outside shoulder and establish positioning before the defender has an opportunity to cross his face. That’s obviously a big help when you consider what the Eagles will do this year. Steen does not need everything to happen directly in front of him. He can pull, climb, and work horizontally very effectively. He can briefly assist another offensive lineman before quickly transitioning onto a linebacker. He looks comfortable operating in space and rarely appears labored when asked to change direction or cover significant ground. There are some impressive snaps where Steen gets out of his stance almost immediately, reaches what initially appears to be an extremely difficult landmark, and gets himself into the perfect position to seal the defender. You can improve an offensive lineman’s technique, but it is much harder to manufacture the type of movement ability Steen already possesses. His athleticism gives him a relatively high ceiling because there are blocks he can physically reach that plenty of NFL guards simply cannot. Zone Blocking As referenced above, Steen’s movement skills make him particularly effective in the zone-run game. I came into this study expecting to be more critical of his run blocking, but there is a lot to like about the way Steen operates when the assignment is primarily about positioning rather than pure displacement. His initial phase on zone concepts can be excellent. He gets off the line quickly, understands where he needs to get his body, and possesses the lateral quickness to establish leverage. On outside zone, there are snaps where Steen reaches the outside shoulder of a defensive lineman incredibly quickly and gets himself into an ideal position. There are also good examples of Steen working to the second level, locating linebackers and using his movement skills to seal them away from the football. He moves naturally in space and doesn’t look uncomfortable while adjusting to moving targets. This is a big part of the zone run game. Run Game Processing and Combination Blocks Steen also showed more encouraging mental processing in the run game than I expected. I thought his work on combination blocks was consistently impressive. He generally understands how to work alongside the center or tackle without creating unnecessary space between the two blockers, and he appears comfortable determining when he needs to remain attached to the defensive lineman and when he can climb to the second level. There were many excellent examples of his work with Cam Jurgens. There were times that Steen recognized that Jurgens needed some initial assistance, helped secure the first-level defender with one arm, and then immediately climbed once it became clear Jurgens had control of the block. Offensive line play happens incredibly quickly, and poor timing on combination blocks can ruin an entire run. Leave too early, and the first-level defender can split the block. Stay attached too long, and the linebacker runs freely to the ball. Steen shows a good understanding of that relationship. Initial Hand Placement There are also examples of Steen displaying very good hand placement. On his better snaps, his hands remain tight and inside the defender’s frame. His elbows don’t flare excessively, and he can get his hands underneath the defender’s shoulder pads and establish initial control by winning with good low pad level. When his lower body and upper body are working together, the result can look excellent. He can use his feet to establish position before using his hands to control the defender, and there are snaps where he effectively uses that leverage to turn or drag a defender away from the play. Steen’s initial punch can also carry some force when he is balanced. The issue is that his hand usage becomes much less consistent once the defender begins fighting back, but the flashes are significant because they demonstrate Steen’s ability to maintain technically sound hand placement. Weaknesses Pass Protection Technique This was my biggest concern after watching Steen. His pass protection was worse than I expected. The athletic tools are clearly there, which almost makes some of the issues more frustrating. Steen should have the movement skills to become a dependable pass protector, but there are too many technical inconsistencies right now for me to consider him particularly reliable when isolated one-on-one. His footwork and hand placement are not always synchronized. There are snaps where Steen delivers his punch before he has established a stable base underneath him. When that happens, he doesn’t have enough strength behind the strike and leaves himself vulnerable if the defender defeats the initial contact. He can also overset. Steen is athletic enough to cover a lot of ground very quickly, but occasionally that becomes a negative. He can move too far outside, giving the defender an easy path back inside. For an interior offensive lineman, that is a major problem. The quarterback’s location must influence how Steen approaches the rep. He cannot consistently allow interior rushers a two-way go. There are snaps where he becomes too square to the defender or opens himself too far and loses the half-man idea he should be trying to maintain (for those who are unsure what I mean by this, as a lineman, if you get yourself into a favorable position, you can target half the opponent’s body, making it easier for you to win the rep). The defender then has options in both directions. Steen’s athleticism allows him to occasionally recover from imperfect positioning, but relying on athletic recovery is not a sustainable approach in NFL pass protection. Defensive athletes are too good. The technical landmarks need to become more consistent. Hand…

title: Should the Eagles’ offensive starters play in the preseason?
summary: Have you heard? The Eagles have a brand new offense! Yeah, I know, I know, it’s been a well-kept secret, but it’s true. It sure sounds pretty complicated! Lots of new plays and stuff! After last season’s disappointing offensive showing under former offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo, his replacement, Sean Mannion, is here with a brand […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 07: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts #1 runs a drill during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 7th, 2026 at the Jefferson Health Training Complex on August 7th, 2026 in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Have you heard? The Eagles have a brand new offense! Yeah, I know, I know, it’s been a well-kept secret, but it’s true. It sure sounds pretty complicated! Lots of new plays and stuff! After last season’s disappointing offensive showing under former offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo, his replacement, Sean Mannion, is here with a brand new scheme that everyone hopes will usher in more efficiency and better production. The goal is for the Eagles to have, you know, a functional, modern NFL offense that will allow them to both run and pass the ball effectively. No one knows exactly what this thing is going to look like just yet, but we do know that there will be an adjustment period as Jalen Hurts and Co. get used to the new normal. There will be new formations, new plays, and with the departure of A.J. Brown to New England, new players to incorporate. On Saturday, the Eagles will be in Baltimore to take on the Ravens, the first of three preseason games the team will play this month. Under Nick Sirianni, the Eagles have very rarely, if ever, played their starters during the preseason and no one is expecting anything different on Saturday night. Defensively, Vic Fangio’s stars shouldn’t need much, if any, time in games this summer, although Fangio certainly wishes they would play a little more than they will. But given all the changes and new personnel, should Sirianni ask his offense to suit up for some preseason action over the next few weeks? If the goal is to come out of the gate with some momentum and familiarity, the answer should be “yes.” We all know why the offensive starters, particularly the veteran-laden and oft-injured offensive line, Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert, won’t play. Protecting them from injury is of paramount importance, and the coaching staff has clearly determined the benefits of playing offensive starters in preseason games do not outweigh those injury concerns. And normally, I’d agree. There is an inherent danger in something precisely like this happening to Jalen Hurts, to be sure. Texans believe QB Graham Mertz tore his ACL during Thursday night’s preseason opener vs the Chargers. There is expected to be additional testing to confirm the injury. pic.twitter.com/BP6NvwUn0r — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 14, 2026 Joint practices held by the Eagles against other teams are usually when Sirianni gets his starters the most game-like action, albeit under controlled circumstances. No doubt, that will happen in the next few weeks, too. But there’s something to be said for game-action. Wouldn’t it make sense for Jalen Hurts to play even just one quarter in two of the team’s three preseason games? By all accounts, the changes being implemented by Mannion are voluminous. But not only that, Hurts also has an entirely new, and unproven, receiver corps to throw to. Sure, Smith will slide in nicely as the top dog, Barkley and Tank Bigsby are known commodities, and Hurts has developed a very nice rapport with Goedert. But with first round wideout Makai Lemon still out of practice with a hamstring injury, giving Hurts some time in the preseason to gain some trust in Darius Cooper, Dontayvion Wicks, Elijah Moore and, to a lesser extent, Hollywood Brown, is a risk worth taking. Historically, starters played at least two quarters in at least one preseason game every summer. In recent years, however, that standard has changed league-wide, although some teams still put their starting QB out there for a few series in a game or two. But most, including the Eagles, do not. And I get it. Every team’s nightmare scenario is their franchise QB lying on the ground clutching his knee in the 2nd quarter of a fake game played in August. But given how much newness there is in the Eagles’ offensive operation, every opportunity to get players on the same page against opposing defenses at game speed before those games count in the standings is beneficial. One can imagine this passing offense stumbling around in the first few weeks of the regular season as the receiving corps tries to develop chemistry with their quarterback, and Mannion gets the rhythm of playcalling. Of course, even in the preseason, Mannion’s playbook would be extremely limited. It would be the most generic and vanilla version of what he will do. But even if it’s just to shake off the rust, I think it would benefit for this year only for them to get some action in the preseason. No one wants to see Hurts and the offense start the season stuck in the mud. It’s not going to take long for the fanbase to turn on the new OC and the QB if things start off rocky. I know the Eagles won’t heed this advice, and I understand their reasoning. Injuries are a sure way to destroy a season before it ever begins. But in this case, I’d roll the dice.

title: Eagles News: Ty Robinson among players on the roster bubble
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles 2026 training camp bubble player power rankings – PhillyVoice1) iDL Ty Robinson: Robinson had a bad rookie season and he began camp getting reps with the developmental players, but he has steadily gotten more meaningful reps, and has gotten better as camp has progressed. […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 01: Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Ty Robinson #95 looks on during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 1st, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles 2026 training camp bubble player power rankings – PhillyVoice 1) iDL Ty Robinson: Robinson had a bad rookie season and he began camp getting reps with the developmental players, but he has steadily gotten more meaningful reps, and has gotten better as camp has progressed. He’s also just a second-year player and a high fourth-round pick at that, even if he was an older prospect when he entered the NFL. The Eagles are not going to give up on him this soon, especially with questionable iDL depth beyond the top four guys. He will very likely be on the roster. 2) RB Will Shipley: Shipley had a golden opportunity to be the RB2 last season, but he didn’t make a convincing enough argument and the team traded for Tank Bigsby. Still, Shipley returns kicks, he’s the personal protector on the punt team, and again, he’s a recent draft pick that the team will not be quick to give up on. The Eagles’ preseason slate starts Saturday. These 12 players will have the most on the line vs. the Ravens. – Inquirer Ty Robinson, DL. Robinson may have begun camp with the developmental defense in team drills, but he has been moving his way up the depth chart recently. The 2025 fourth-rounder out of Nebraska had a strong showing on Monday as a pass rusher, forcing his way into the backfield on multiple occasions against the second-string offense. Robinson could use some standout preseason performances if he wants to make a case for the initial 53. Willie Lampkin, OL. Lampkin hasn’t played a football game since Aug. 16, 2025. At that time, the 2025 undrafted free agent out of North Carolina was a member of the Los Angeles Rams. He had a strong start to camp, especially in the preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys. But Lampkin was injured in the second game of the preseason against the Los Angeles Chargers, and he was ultimately waived at the end of camp with an injury designation. The Eagles signed him to the active roster and placed him on injured reserve for the rest of the year. Now, Lampkin is set to return to action this preseason as he vies for a depth role, at both center and guard. Eagles Training Camp Notes: Practice ends after a fight breaks out – BGN I’d go stock up™ on Mac McWilliams, who was taking first-team nickel corner reps today. He’s stacking his best days of the summer recently. I’d go stock down™ on Hollywood Brown. The veteran receiver has been the target on most of Hurts’ interceptions in training camp this summer. Brown also had a bad drop while wide open on a bubble screen. Brown received $5 million fully guaranteed when the Eagles signed him, so, the money doesn’t make it a no-brainer for the team to move on from the veteran receiver. But he just hasn’t had a great camp and he’s been outshined by other Eagles receivers. Brown got some extra work in with Hurts after practice to presumably help getting on the same page. Roob’s top 10 Eagles who have exceeded expectations in training camp – NBCSP Darius Cooper, WR: When camp began, I felt like Cooper had a chance to make the roster. After a few days, I thought he had a chance to not just make the team but to contribute. Now, I look at him as a roster lock with a real chance to play a significant role on offense. He’s been that good. Cooper was impressive last summer, but he’s been even better this year. Way better. Probably the Eagles’ best overall WR this summer. We’ve all seen training camp wonders who don’t contribute once the season starts. I don’t think that’s the case here. This kid can flat-out play. Eagles WR Darius Cooper is the talk of training camp. Just don’t tell him — or ask him – The Athletic The best training camp practice of Darius Cooper’s career came Monday. Jalen Hurts found him all over the field — deep down the sideline, across the middle, in traffic, making adjustments on the ball. Without any context, one would have thought Cooper was already a regular starter with the franchise quarterback. Kennady, Darius’ wife, needed to work that morning. She could not attend her husband’s standout session. “How was practice?” she asked him later that night. “It’s great,” he responded, “but there are some things I can work on.” Cooper, the second-year wide receiver, does not have a social media account. He’s not reading The Athletic’s practice observations. He’s not tuned into podcasts or talk radio. What he failed to realize is that his practice session had gone viral among ardent Philadelphia Eagles followers. Kennady already knew. “Unless you’re here, you don’t get the full story because he’s so humble and he’s always working to get better,” Kennady said after practice Thursday. “So I’m not sure exactly how it went, but from the reports I heard, it was a great day.” “When someone says to Darius, ‘Wow, man, you had a great camp day,’ Darius always says, ‘I could have done better’,” explained Veronica Watkins, Darius’ mother. “He’s always looking to improve himself.” Eagles 53-man roster predictions: Where do things stand entering the first preseason game? – PHLY Edge rusher (6): Jalyx Hunt, Jonathan Greenard, Nolan Smith, Arnold Ebiketie, AJ Epenesa, Joshua Weru. Let’s talk about Weru. … The Kenya native with a background in rugby has been one of the bigger surprises of Eagles training camp so far. At 6-foot-4, 244 pounds, he’s explosive off the ball with long arms and a surprising amount of power considering both his size and relative unfamiliarity with the sport. Weru has an uphill battle to make the 53-man roster, especially with the extra spot on the practice squad for an international player pathway program player available for either him or Bernard, but I’d argue he’s flashed enough in practice that the Eagles shouldn’t risk another team poaching him off their practice squad. To that end, it will be instructive how they use him in the preseason. Outside of Weru, Each of the other edge rushers have seemingly done enough to make the team. Epenesa could be a practice squad stash as well, but I think he’s been solid enough to be on the roster if healthy. The Main Characters of the 2026 NFL Preseason – The Ringer SEAN MANNION — The preseason will offer us the first glimpse of the changes Mannion has planned. We expect to see Jalen Hurts operate from under center more often than he has in the past, which will be a major departure for him. Historically, Philadelphia has mostly kept Hurts in the gun, where he poses more of a run threat on option plays. Hurts hasn’t been very productive on option keepers in recent seasons, but the threat that he’ll pull the ball still opens up space for Saquon Barkley, who led the NFL in EPA on “read option” carries last season, per Sports Info Solutions. Mannion says that the Eagles will “lean into” Hurts’s rushing ability. That suggests Philly will still regularly line up in the gun since there are few concepts that get the quarterback involved in the run game from under center (outside of QB sneaks). The 28-year-old QB also showed up to camp looking notably leaner and quicker, which could make those option keepers more effective than they were a year ago. Among quarterbacks with at least 10 option keepers last season, Hurts had the lowest success rate, and only Bo Nix lost more EPA on those plays, per Sports Info Solutions. So there’s a lot of room for improvement in that area, and a faster Hurts should be more capable of burning defenses that are keyed in on Barkley. It will be interesting to see how Mannion incorporates the QB run-option game into the modern West Coast offense. We’ve seen coaches from the Shanahan-McVay tree use pistol as a middle ground between under center and shotgun…
author: Brandon Lee Gowton

title: Nick Sirianni talks Eagles’ preseason expectations
summary: We had a chance to hear from Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni one last time before the team’s first preseason game on Saturday night, and he talked about what he’s looking for from players and from an operational standpoint. He also complimented Jalen Hurts’ consistent approach, and how he’s handled being asked to do different […]
full_text: We had a chance to hear from Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni one last time before the team’s first preseason game on Saturday night, and he talked about what he’s looking for from players and from an operational standpoint. He also complimented Jalen Hurts’ consistent approach, and how he’s handled being asked to do different things. Here’s head coach had to say: On the first preseason game Sirianni explained that what they’re looking for on Saturday is the execution of the whole operation. It’s the first run for the coaches in a game-like setting, so it’ll be a good opportunity to work through the operation. Otherwise, he’s looking for everyone to be clean with their assignments and for good fundamental football. He noted that it’s the same standard they have everyday in practice, too. “We want all our guys to play with extreme effort.” The head coach said that some guys are going to get more reps than they are used to getting, and they’ll be looking for players to show great effort, great physicality, and great mental toughness. Sirianni wouldn’t talk about who would be the starting QB for the Eagles on Saturday night, and said that players at many positions will be substituted in and out in different situations. Having someone along the offensive line have to move from the left to the right side, or a DB going from outside to nickel, are all things that could happen in a game, and it’s beneficial to practice those situations. The head coach admitted that the reps on Saturday will be good for the young offensive lineman, but also pointed out that they have tough practices and are getting live reps up front every day. He also said they do a lot of 1-vs-2 periods, and what better experience for the young OL than going against Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, and Moro Ojomo. He said that in terms of starters and who would play where, everything is fluid at this point and still changing. Sirianni wouldn’t pinpoint one specific position he’s most looking forward to watch on Saturday, and said that he’s interested in watching everyone in live action. The head coach also talked a bit about the balance of getting the experience they need — including from OC Sean Mannion as a play caller — without giving away any kind of competitive advantage. He explained that they learned back in 2021 to be extra careful about what they showed in the preseason, because other teams came prepared as a result. Still, he thinks there’s a way to get the operational things worked on without giving anything away. “Anything you don’t want people to see, you can’t put on tape.” On Jalen Hurts “I think he looks great, in every aspect. When he has to run the ball, he’s running it well and looks fast and explosive. When he’s passing it — I think he’s been so consistent through camp. I just think he’s getting better and better, and more comfortable, as each day goes by. And I love his consistency right now, and I love the way he’s playing right now. I’m really excited for him and this season and the things I know he can do. I’m just so pleased with how he’s attacked everything, and I’m really excited for him and pumped for this year.” On the offensive scheme Sirianni was asked about this new style of offense doing more in the middle of the field and balancing that with his focus on not turning the ball over — something that happens more often in that part of the field. The head coach explained that his job is to win as many games as possible, not to lead the league in total offense. He acknowledged that it’d be great to lead the league in offense because that would mean they were pretty good, but ultimately the goal is to win. “My job is to win as many games as we can, and that will always be the goal, and we know that part of that is taking care of the football. And our guys know how to do that, and have done a good job of that — and our defense has done a good job of getting their hands on some of the balls that are out there. No, the focus will always be, how do we take care of the football and how do we play with great fundamentals while still being explosive.“ On the WR depth Sirianni said that it’s still too early to tell how things will end up roster-wise at wide receiver, but Darius Cooper has been consistent and has made some really good catches. “There’s still a lot of time left. He’s a having a good camp. There’s still a lot of time left. It’s about being consistent on a daily basis. He’s done a good job being consistent on a daily basis. And he makes some really good catches, really elite hands, and we know he’s tough and things that he can do. But I’ve been pleased with where he is.”

title: Riley Nowakowski raves about confidence of Drew Allar
summary: Drew Allar’s first NFL preseason appearance provided the Pittsburgh Steelers with plenty of reasons to be encouraged about the future of their quarterback position. The rookie third-round pick looked poised and decisive in his debut Thursday night, helping lead the Steelers to a 28-9 victory over the Green Bay Packers, completing 10 of 13 passes […]
full_text: Aug 13, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers fullback Riley Nowakowski (37) celebrates a touchdown pass from quarterback Drew Allar (16) against the Green Bay Packers during the second half of a game at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Drew Allar’s first NFL preseason appearance provided the Pittsburgh Steelers with plenty of reasons to be encouraged about the future of their quarterback position. The rookie third-round pick looked poised and decisive in his debut Thursday night, helping lead the Steelers to a 28-9 victory over the Green Bay Packers, completing 10 of 13 passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns while adding a rushing score, finishing with a 154.8 passer rating. But perhaps just as encouraging for Pittsburgh is the progress Allar has made away from the stat sheet. Rookie tight end/fullback Riley Nowakowski, who caught a touchdown pass from Allar in the preseason opener, has noticed a significant change in the young quarterback’s presence since he first arrived in Pittsburgh. “You’ve seen his confidence skyrocket,” Nowakowski said. “I think he does such a good job of commanding the huddle compared to when he came in. You can even hear it in his cadence. He’s really been using his cadence as a weapon and just being able to really have us feel like, ‘Oh, shoot, this guy’s got control of our offense.” #Steelers rookie TE/FB Riley Nowakowski on QB Drew Allar's leadership presence: "You've seen his confidence skyrocket. I think he does such a good job of commanding the huddle compared to when he came in. You can even hear it in his cadence. He's really been using his cadence as… pic.twitter.com/yywpnc5OCz — Brendan Howe (@bybrendanhowe) August 14, 2026 Allar showed accuracy, arm strength and athleticism against Green Bay. He connected with Kaden Wetjen on a 75-yard completion that set up his rushing touchdown before later finding Wetjen for another score. He also threw a touchdown to Nowakowski, helping turn three of his drives into touchdowns. The performance came after a training camp in which Allar had already been drawing praise from head coach Mike McCarthy and offensive coaches for his poise, ability to absorb information and willingness to respond to coaching. Still, the Steelers aren’t rushing to make conclusions based on one preseason performance. Aaron Rodgers remains Pittsburgh’s starting quarterback, while Mason Rudolph and Will Howard are also competing for roles in a crowded quarterback room. What makes Allar’s development especially interesting, however, is that the Steelers aren’t simply evaluating his physical ability. They are watching for the traits that could eventually allow him to take control of the franchise. According to Nowakowski, that process is already underway. title: The Morning After: Writing is on the wall for Steelers RB Kaleb Johnson
summary: If Acrisure Stadium was powered by anticipation, it could have stored enough to last an entire season in the moments leading up to the Pittsburgh Steelers’ preseason opener against the Green Bay Packers. It marked the first time that Will Howard and Drew Allar would take the field as NFL quarterbacks, albeit in an exhibition […]
full_text: Aug 13, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers running back Kaleb Johnson (20) warms up before the game against the Green Bay Packers at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If Acrisure Stadium was powered by anticipation, it could have stored enough to last an entire season in the moments leading up to the Pittsburgh Steelers’ preseason opener against the Green Bay Packers. It marked the first time that Will Howard and Drew Allar would take the field as NFL quarterbacks, albeit in an exhibition state. But for the young signal callers, it was a chance to show they could perform when the lights are bright. Additionally, several young defenders had showcase moments of their own, and a young running back’s lack of playing time could be the writing on the wall we all feared. It’s the morning after game day, so let’s dive in on what could end up being a very memorable 2026 preseason opener. It’s okay to have faith in Drew Allar Both Howard and Allar had highlight moments, but the majority of the attention (understandably so) is on the rookie out of Penn State who went 10-of-13 for 153 yards, two touchdowns, and an additional score on the ground. This naturally led us down caveat street, as Steelers fans are more weary than most about big moments in the preseason. Kenny Pickett and the Steelers’ starters scoring five touchdowns in five drives in 2023 did irreversible damage to the perception of preseason to a lot of fans, and frankly, they are justified for that. However, I would say this: don’t let the shortcomings of one quarterback cause you to never believe in another. For a quick comparison, I pulled Pickett’s totals from that preseason (what a lovely way to spend my morning, I know). In five drives, he went 13-of-15 for 199 yards and two touchdowns – Allar practically matched that in one game. And before you start shout-typing that Pickett did it against first and second-team players while Allar was largely competing against the third-team, believe me – I get it. I’m not sitting here today proclaiming Allar to be the second coming of Josh Allen. I am saying, however, that it’s okay to let yourself believe. It’s okay, after seeing what he did in his first taste of NFL action, to say, ‘alright, there may be something there with this guy.’ Allar was considered a first-round talent ahead of last college football season for a reason. Then, of course, everything that could have gone wrong for Penn State went wrong, he got injured for the season, and that was that. And even prior to the 2025 season, he was stuck in an RPO offense when his best attribute is his ability to sling the ball – something even Penn State assistant coach Terry Smith admitted on 93.7 The Fan earlier this year. “I’ve been known as the truth teller here at Penn State,” Smith said . “And I think unfairly to Drew, our system wasn’t built for him. It wasn’t made for him. Some of the decisions were taken out of his control.” Apparently, all it took for Allar to begin improving was three months away from his former offensive coordinator Andy Kotelnicki and head coach James Franklin. He has shown more progression in three months with the Steelers than he did in four years at Penn State. His throwing motion has less movement, his footwork is better, though still a work in progress, and he made routine plays look routine in his debut. I’d like to see him run with the second-team in Week 2 to see what he looks like against better competition, but his performance against Green Bay exceeded expectations. So enjoy this little ride through August. Because if he continues with this type of play, maybe it’ll be enough for the Steelers to give him a real shot to be QB1 in 2027. Writing is on the wall for Kaleb Johnson Travis Homer took the first-team reps at running back to start the game, with Lew Nichols also rotating in and getting meaningful carries. After the first 30 minutes, though, Kaleb Johnson had a grand total of zero offensive snaps and finished the night with two carries for three yards. If we are taking into account Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren, both of whom didn’t play, that would put Johnson at RB5 in the rotation. Johnson has been a heavy talking point throughout the offseason. He carried the ball just 28 times as a rookie for 69 yards and [insert mandatory mention of the kickoff folly against the Seahawks here]. The Steelers told you without saying a word how they feel about the former third-round pick. If they are able to pull off a pick swap in the 2028 draft via trade, they should do it. It’s better to get something for him, which they probably can. As my friend Alan Saunders said, “They got something for Kendrick Green.“ Regardless of how they move on from Johnson, it looks like a forgone conclusion that he won’t be on the roster come September. Germie Bernard’s stock is rising fast It got somewhat lost in the midst of the Drew Allar glitz and glamour, but Germie Bernard had a terrific debut in his own right. The second-round pick caught four passes for 61 yards, including a very nice 25-yard catch-and-run that saw him break multiple tackles down the right sideline. While Roman Wilson has had the stronger camp, the Michigan product had just one catch for seven yards on Thursday, so don’t be surprised to see Bernard get more opportunities in the final two preseason games as the battle for WR3 continues. Defensive standouts There were too many notable performances on defense for them to all have their own category, so I’ll give my quick notes on a handful of guys: LB Jamin Davis: Two sacks, led the team with eight tackles. Very nice showing for the former first-round pick. Don’t think he’ll find a spot on the Steelers’ roster, but he’ll make someone’s team DT Gabriel Rubio: Panned the draft pick, but wow he looked very solid on the interior. Six tackles, filling gaps all evening. Impressive stuff from No. 96. DB Devan Boykin: No one will judge you if you just said, “Who?” Boykin was signed as an undrafted free agent following the 2026 NFL Draft and had a very nice season at Indiana in 2025, picking off two passes and helping the Hoosiers win the National Championship. He had four tackles, a tackle for loss, and a terrific play on the ball in which he nearly came down with an interception. DB Doneiko Slaughter: Beautiful play on a screen pass to Marshawn Lloyd, plowing through Christian Watson for the tackle to force fourth down Let us know what you think in the comments . title: 5 takeaways from the Steelers’ 28-9 win over the Green Bay Packers
summary: Steelers football is back, and so is BTSC’s takeaways column. The Mike McCarthy era got off to a promising start in Thursday’s 19-point win over Green Bay, and as always, there’s plenty to learn from the game. 1. It’s just the preseason I’ve started every preseason Week 1 takeaways column with this section since I […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Lew Nichols #35 of the Pittsburgh Steelers hurdles over Brandon Cisse #2 of the Green Bay Packers during the first quarter at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Steelers football is back, and so is BTSC’s takeaways column. The Mike McCarthy era got off to a promising start in Thursday’s 19-point win over Green Bay, and as always, there’s plenty to learn from the game. 1. It’s just the preseason I’ve started every preseason Week 1 takeaways column with this section since I started this series. It’s a necessary disclaimer for all the takeaways, overreactions and analysis to follow in the month of August. Preseason football is fun. It’s an important part of the roster-building process. And it certainly gives us some key insights into how the team will operate. But it doesn’t have a lot in common with the regular season product. Schemes aren’t necessarily vanilla — the Steelers put some interesting ideas out on Acrisure Stadium’s new field Thursday — but those plays are still carried out by variations of the 90-man roster that haven’t built much chemistry with each other. Due to teams rotating and pulling different combinations of starters and backups, the matchups between teams are rarely even. And coaches care more about testing players in various scenarios than the final score, which is, of course, meaningless at the end of the day. Trust me, I’ve found the “Drew Allar is the Steelers’ next franchise quarterback” posts as entertaining as anyone. But don’t buy into the hype — or some of the less optimistic narratives — just yet. Preseason football isn’t real football. And even if it was, there’s still plenty of time for things to change. 2. The Steelers’ quarterback battle gets off to a strong start Now for the overreactions: The Steelers have their next franchise quarterback in Drew Allar! Maybe they have two or three — Will Howard and Mason Rudolph looked pretty good out there too, no? In all seriousness, though, all three of the Steelers’ passers played well enough last night that how the quarterback hierarchy will shape up heading into the regular season hasn’t gotten any clearer. Mason Rudolph was ruthlessly efficient, going 10/11 for 93 yards to start. His best play of the game was probably his lone incompletion, where the veteran QB2 channeled his inner Ben Roethlisberger to heave what would’ve been a touchdown pass if rookie receiver Germie Bernard had been able to get a second foot cleanly in-bounds. Mason Rudolph is the forgotten QB in Pittsburgh pic.twitter.com/shl2daR1cB — Chase Daniel (@ChaseDaniel) August 13, 2026 Outside of that play, it wasn’t a spectacular performance, but Rudolph looked like a quarterback who’s been-there, done-that — an attractive trait for a prospective Aaron Rodgers backup. Next up was 2024 sixth-rounder Will Howard, playing in his first game since the 2024-25 College Football Playoff National Championship, believe it or not. He looked impressively composed despite the long break. Howard put up another efficient stat line — 7/9 for 86 yards — highlighted by a two-minute drill touchdown drive to end the first half. Like Rudolph, Howard’s best play came on an-almost touchdown pass: a well-layered seam pass to tight end Robert Tonyan that placed the Steelers on the 1-yard-line. Didn’t count as a TD but Will Howard has been targeting TEs up the seam/on benders all camp. Great throw to get this up and down from Howard. Got hot on that drive. #Steelers pic.twitter.com/5Fwq8O4Hml — Rob Gregson (@NFL_Rob) August 14, 2026 Coming out of college, Howard was never seen as some high-end athlete or arm talent, but he made some throws off-platform and on the move Thursday night, which was an encouraging side of his game to see. Back-to-back big throws by @Steelers QB Will Howard 🎯 GBvsPIT on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/A63di1TNah — NFL (@NFL) August 14, 2026 The last quarterback to play for the Steelers was rookie third-rounder Drew Allar, who followed up Rudolph and Howard’s almost-touchdowns with three real scores: the first on the ground on a successful read-option, and the last two on short, rollout passes to fellow rookies Kaden Wetjen and Riley Nowakowski. Drew Allar's best plays from 153-yard, 3 total TD performance in preseason win over the Packers. @AllarDrew @Steelers pic.twitter.com/0wH4wfcEkY — NFL (@NFL) August 14, 2026 Pre-draft, the one-liner on Allar was that he’s raw but talented, but his 10/13, 153-yard, two-touchdown passing performance showed some solid poise for his first NFL outing. He wasn’t prime Peyton Manning back there — I’ll have to re-watch his performance, but Allar seemed a tick late on some reads and had mild happy feet in the pocket. But of course there will be some nitpicks this early in his career, especially after Mike McCarthy spent much of the spring reworking how the former Nittany Lion plays the game in the first place. Upside is why the Steelers drafted Allar, and that was abundantly clear Thursday night. Allar didn’t have any truly “wow” throws, but the ball leaps from his hand in a way it doesn’t with Howard and Rudolph, and the rookie’s rushing touchdown was a refreshing dose of size and mobility from the pocket. Keep in mind that Skylar Thompson also lit up the preseason for the Steelers last year. Don’t read too much into anything. But backup quarterbacks were always going to be the focus for the franchise-passer-needy Steelers this month, and they couldn’t have gotten off to a much better start. 3. Worried about the offensive line? Wait a few weeks The Steelers’ offensive line has started to pick up some national media hype over the offseason as one of the league’s most exciting young groups, and for good reason: Zach Frazier and Troy Fautanu look like rising stars. Mason McCormick has developed into a solid starter. There’s a lot of depth, and the team added two more premium draft picks to the group this year. All that excitement, just for the starting five to falter against a Micah Parsons-less Green Bay front to open the preseason, allowing two fairly quick and ugly sacks on starter Mason Rudolph, and failing to get much push in the run game. Right tackle Dylan Cook struggled mightily in pass protection, while Fautanu looked to still be getting used to left tackle, committing two penalties. It certainly wasn’t encouraging, but keep in mind that every Steelers starter on the offensive line, minus Frazier at center, is playing on the opposite side of where they took most of their starting snaps last season. Combine that with a new offense, new coaching, new teammates blocking next to them, and a new practice philosophy that’s less physical than what Mike Tomlin brought to the table in years past, and you’re looking at some expected growing pains as the unit builds chemistry. Offensive line success is a complicated formula. I’m not guaranteeing it’ll all work out, or vice versa, in 2026. But it will certainly take some time. Thursday’s showing was disappointing, but there’s little reason to panic this early in the process. 4. The roster hierarchy is revealed I don’t put much stock into depth charts this time of year, but how coaches order the playing time of the team during the preseason does tend to lend some insight to the hierarchy of the roster. For instance, it was notable to see Travis Homer play with the “ones” at running back as the next man up behind Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle, who both got the night off. Homer has a solid roster chance thanks to his special teams skill set and capability as a dump-off target, and his playing time Thursday seemed to reflect that. A bit more surprising was Lew Nichols being the next runner up, building on what’s reportedly been a strong camp. The reigning Isaac Redman Award winner was the Steelers’ most effective back against Green Bay, running hard for 36 yards and a touchdown with a 3.6-yard…
