title: NFL Top 100 Players: Seahawks’ Sam Darnold soars to 21 after Super Bowl win
summary: As the NFL Top 100 was nearing the 20’s, and with Devon Witherspoon missing the Top 100, many fans of the Seattle Seahawks were worried their Super Bowl winning quarterback was not going to make it. That is, until Friday. Darnold came in at 21, making a 51-spot jump from last years ranking, with glowing […]
full_text: As the NFL Top 100 was nearing the 20’s, and with Devon Witherspoon missing the Top 100 , many fans of the Seattle Seahawks were worried their Super Bowl winning quarterback was not going to make it. That is, until Friday. No. 21 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Seahawks QB Sam Darnold! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/ayBrzUkqDS — NFL (@NFL) August 14, 2026 Darnold came in at 21, making a 51-spot jump from last years ranking, with glowing endorsements from some of the best defenders in the league, including Byron Murphy II who said, “Top five quarterback in the league. And not five either.” Grey Zabel also gave his stamp of approval of Darnold, stating, “That’s my guy. That’s my QB. That’s a guy you want to go to war for and protect him at all costs.” Derek Stingley, Houston Texans star and one of the best cornerbacks in the league, had this to say about Darnold, “Nothing seems to rattle him. Like, if he has pressure in his face, it seems like he still somehow makes the right throw.” He ranked fifth in the league in 2025 in passing yards with 4,048 yards as well as fifth in DVOA. He also tied for ninth in touchdown passes and tied for fourth in game winning drives in 2025. There are currently four quarterbacks that have yet to be unveiled, so by the players estimation, Darnold is the fifth best quarterback in the league (unless your name is Byron Murphy). title: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald addresses controversial Terrion Arnold signing
summary: Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald spoke about the team’s controversial decision to sign former Detroit Lions first-round pick Terrion Arnold, who is facing several felony charges in Florida. Following Friday’s practice for their preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys, Macdonald was asked several questions about the decision, from how they view him as a […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - DECEMBER 22: Cornerback Terrion Arnold #0 of the Detroit Lions gets set during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears, at Soldier Field on December 22, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald spoke about the team’s controversial decision to sign former Detroit Lions first-round pick Terrion Arnold , who is facing several felony charges in Florida. Following Friday’s practice for their preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys, Macdonald was asked several questions about the decision, from how they view him as a player to his fit in the culture. Macdonald declined to comment on anything regarding Arnold’s current legal proceedings, saying the team would allow the league and court processes to play out. “I think it was an opportunity to bring on a player that we felt strongly about during the draft process,” Macdonald told the media. ‘We also understand that it’s a serious situation with a legal matter. There’s a process behind it, so we respect that. That’s how we’ll operate too, just letting that process play out and let the league decide if and when his return to play is.” Seattle hosted the former Alabama star for a tryout on Sunday , which Macdonald described as “great.” Macdonald said that he spoke to several people, whom he respects, about Arnold, and they supported him as a person. He added that he had informal one-on-one conversations with players prior to signing the former first-round pick and that he was confident in the team’s locker room and team. “I referenced the folks that had been in his corner throughout the process as well and we respect those people. We’re not going to ignore those folks that we really respect, and have a strong opinion about it as well,” Macdonald said. “When you put all of those things together, it felt like it was a good opportunity for the team.” While the team has agreed to terms with Arnold, Macdonald said the Seahawks are still working through a timeline for him to join the team, meaning he won’t be suiting up for the Seahawks in their preseason opener on Saturday night. Additionally, the NFL has the option to place Arnold on the Commissioner’s Exempt List, which would bar him from playing any regular season games. “All I know is that there’s an availability, if the league lets it happen, that he could play. In terms of when that happens and how that goes down, it’s just part of that process,” Macdonald said. “The facts of the case, all those things about the comments of what happens, that’s not our responsibility to have a comment on that nor can we. I think we just have to understand that there’s a process at play, and we’re going to let it play out.” When asked about Arnold as a player, Macdonald lauded Arnold’s physicality and speed, saying that his skill set fits the identity of the secondary. The Seahawks head coach said Arnold is used to some of the pattern matching that the Seahawks do from his time at Alabama and that he believes there’s a spot for him if he becomes the best version of himself. “We want players to come in and be the best version of themselves,” Macdonald said. “We believe that if you do that, then the team’s going to be better for it as well. Terrion [Arnold] will be the same process with him if or when he gets here.” The signing is meant to bolster a Seahawks cornerback group that lost Riq Woolen this offseason and is set to rely on inexperienced players, like Nehemiah Pritchett and rookies Julian Neal and Michael Dansby, to fill the role.

Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks’ campaign as defending Super Bowl champions will feature a last dance. Entering NFL season 13, Seahawks DE DeMarcus Lawrence tells me "this will be my last year." He's coming off productive, ballhawk year & Lombardi. Stayed healthy last season after tough last year with Cowboys, found food & recovery routine that helped him to 6 sacks, 3 FF/FR, 20… — Jori Epstein (@JoriEpstein) August 14, 2026 Lawrence arrived in Seattle last offseason on a three-year, $32.5 million deal that will have no guaranteed money remaining after this upcoming season. The long-time Dallas Cowboy remained a productive player in his first year outside of Dallas, playing and starting 16 games for the NFC’s best team while rotating in for just under 60% of the defensive snaps. It was another strong season for the five-time Pro Bowler, as he collected six sacks, 11 tackles for loss, three forced fumbles, and, incredibly, two fumble return touchdowns. Originally a second-round pick, taken 34th overall by the Cowboys in the 2014 NFL Draft, Lawrence spent the first 12 seasons of his career with them. Despite multiple seasons derailed by injury, Lawrence will retire in the top 10 of the franchise’s all-time sacks list, ranking 10th with 61.5. The 2025 season brought the veteran his first ring and now, in Lawrence’s final NFL season, he and the Seahawks will look to go back-to-back and send him off into the sunset in style.

The Seattle Seahawks defeated the New England Patriots 29-13.(Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks begin their 2026 preseason on Saturday against the Dallas Cowboys, their only home appearance of their three-game preseason slate. Not that there was much reason to suspect otherwise, but Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed following Friday’s practice that Saturday’s game will be light on starters on offense and defense. However, one big change from last season is the rotation of quarterbacks Drew Lock and Jalen Milroe. “George [Holani] should get some work tomorrow,” Macdonald said. “A lot of our established starters won’t be playing [against the Cowboys]. They’ll be going through the warm-up and everything, but George should see some action to some degree.” “The quarterbacks, we’re going to rotate in some form or fashion,” Macdonald continued. “We have an idea of how we want it to work, but don’t want to be put in a corner there. It’ll be great. Both guys will get experience playing with different units. “Normally the quarterback goes until he doesn’t go and then the next guy goes and closes the game out. With this game, I think we’re going to rotate to some extent.” Macdonald revealed that, at least for the Cowboys game, Drew Lock will get the start before Jalen Milroe comes in at some point. When Milroe was a rookie, he played just about exclusively with the third-team offense, including for a full-game start in the preseason finale versus the Green Bay Packers. Throughout training camp, Milroe has had scrimmage reps with the likes of A.J. Barner, Elijah Arroyo, and Jadarian Price, and by most accounts he’s made enough strides to practice with more established members of the Seahawks offense. With all due respect to Drew Lock, if we aren’t going to see Sam Darnold much (if at all) over the next three weeks, almost all of preseason is going to be heavily focused on how much Milroe has developed as a quarterback. It should be interesting to watch!

title: What are the Seahawks getting in Terrion Arnold, the football player?
summary: The Seattle Seahawks have made the big, if not controversial decision to sign former Detroit Lions first-round cornerback Terrion Arnold, who’s currently facing several felony robbery and kidnapping charges. When Arnold was arrested earlier this summer, the Lions wasted little time in releasing the former Alabama star. However, Arnold drew interest from several teams once […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 14: Terrion Arnold #6 of the Detroit Lions intercepts the pass intended for Rome Odunze #15 of the Chicago Bears in the second half of the game at Ford Field on September 14, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks have made the big, if not controversial decision to sign former Detroit Lions first-round cornerback Terrion Arnold , who’s currently facing several felony robbery and kidnapping charges. When Arnold was arrested earlier this summer, the Lions wasted little time in releasing the former Alabama star. However, Arnold drew interest from several teams once he was cleared to work (and travel domestically without an ankle monitor), and the Seahawks were among those teams whose initial interest turned into something much more than that. Even though Arnold’s contract is expected to be incredibly cheap, the issue is whether or not he’ll be allowed to play in the regular season. The best case scenario is the charges are dropped and the NFL decides not to take further action by suspending him anyway. Either way, Seattle clearly believes Arnold can help a cornerback room that is far from settled with Riq Woolen gone. It’s only sensible to focus on the football side of the Arnold story. What kind of player are the Seahawks getting? Are his penalty issues correctable? What are his strengths? This is where we hit the emergency button and paged Ryan Mathews, who’s the Senior Editor for Pride of Detroit , the excellent Detroit Lions SB Nation site. They’re plugged into the Lions 100 percent of the way, with Jeremy Reisman doing fantastic work as a credentialed Lions reporter. In a special 5 Qs and 5 As, I asked Ryan about Arnold’s time in Detroit, and whether or not the Seahawks made a good acquisition from a football standpoint. All embedded tweets were inserted by us, not by Ryan. 1.) I’ve harped on this for a bit given how Seahawks fans viewed Riq Woolen’s penalty issues before he left for Philadelphia: Terrion Arnold has been flagged 17 times when you count offsetting/declined penalties. He’s only played 24 games total. What gives? The Lions ask a lot of their outside cornerbacks. Playing press man is a non-negotiable, and that requires a level of physicality that continues throughout the route. As a rookie, Arnold racked up eight of those aforementioned penalties in his first four weeks in the NFL, so there is proof that a lot of the handsiness he was getting flagged for early on was corrected with coaching. Every Terrion Arnold defensive penalty in his rookie season: (He wore 0 as a rookie) I forgot the one penalty where he just tackled Bobo on a non-target. I'd say his Year 2 penalties are a little less obvious than all the rookie moments. pic.twitter.com/msSTELFq58 — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) August 14, 2026 Every Terrion Arnold penalty in 2025 (only played 8 games due to injury). A couple ticky-tack ones (LOL at the first CLE hold) but my best cope is he's miscast in man. He's in position most of the time but can be very handsy. Last penalty is same one 2x for replay purposes. pic.twitter.com/Os4eScLBp1 — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) August 14, 2026 2.) The Seahawks run a lot of zone coverage. Detroit tends to run a lot more man coverage compared to the rest of the league. Is this a case where Arnold may not have been a schematic fit through his first two seasons? Arnold definitely fit in Detroit’s system, but again, what the Lions ask of their outside cornerbacks is a lot to handle. They’re oftentimes left out on an island in coverage, and they’re expected to get their noses dirty in the run game. It’s a lot on a player’s plate, but veterans like Carlton Davis and D.J. Reed have shown an ability to thrive in these roles. It’s important to remember that one of the biggest hurdles so far in Arnold’s career has been staying on the field. After playing 16 games his rookie season, Arnold missed a significant amount of time with a shoulder injury, playing just eight games last year. He initially avoided surgery, but re-aggravated the injury in the Thanksgiving Day game against the Packers, putting him on IR for the rest of the season and forcing him to finally get surgery. 3.) What’s the best thing Arnold has done well over his first two seasons? The best thing Arnold did over his first two seasons came in the phases of the game where he could be physical. Registering a tackle on a route near the line of scrimmage, contesting a ball at the catch point, making those bang-bang plays where the instincts married the physicality were when Arnold was at his best in Detroit. Lions CB Terrion Arnold with a very good tackle on Tyler Johnson. He slips out to the flats but Arnold closes quickly and wraps up for the tackle. #OnePride pic.twitter.com/OxmoKvw4qn — Russell Brown (@RussNFLDraft) September 10, 2024 @Bischoff_Scott and I have been saying it for a few weeks now. Lions CB Terrion Arnold is getting closer and closer to that first career INT. Great PBU from him here. #OnePride pic.twitter.com/RkRqwfun6y — Russell Brown (@RussNFLDraft) October 15, 2024 Some great coverage from Lions CB 6 Terrion Arnold at the top of the screen. He’s been playing really well for the Lions defense. #OnePride pic.twitter.com/Q4lFNbU9Gg — Russell Brown (@RussNFLDraft) November 14, 2025 4.) Did he make any tangible improvements from his rookie season to last (before his season-ending injury)? One of the biggest training camp darlings in the summer of 2025 was Terrion Arnold. Beat writers were singing his praises, there were videos of Arnold’s great play flooding the timeline, and most importantly, the coaches identified him as a player who was making that jump in Year 2. His coverage was stickier in one-on-one’s vs. the likes of Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. He was coming across as a more confident and technically refined player… until the season started. It was one step forward and two steps back in nearly every game. If his coverage was solid, there were lapses in run defense. If the run defense was strong, the coverage was lacking. 5.) Assuming he can actually play suspension-free this season, did the Seahawks just get themselves a moldable, promising corner who can be a major contributor on the league’s best defense? There was always enough there with Arnold’s play to believe he could put it all together. More reps–and honestly, more help from the front-seven in generating pressure–would help his development and confidence. Going to a team like the Seattle Seahawks feels like the right kind of ecosystem for Arnold to reach his developmental ceiling. Thank you very much to Ryan for getting back to us so quickly! That’s why Pride of Detroit is forever awesome.

summary: After broken neck, 49ers’ Robert Jones ready to fight for a job: ‘I do have to hit again’ (paywall)“Jones used a bone-stimulation machine to promote healing for four months, took regular hospital trips for two-hour stints in a hyperbaric chamber and wasn’t permitted to run until he was medically cleared in March….“When we got to […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 23: Head coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers and head coach Jim Harbaugh of the Los Angeles Chargers shake hands after the NFL Preseason 2025 game between Los Angeles Chargers and San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on August 23, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images After broken neck, 49ers’ Robert Jones ready to fight for a job: ‘I do have to hit again’ (paywall) “Jones used a bone-stimulation machine to promote healing for four months, took regular hospital trips for two-hour stints in a hyperbaric chamber and wasn’t permitted to run until he was medically cleared in March….“When we got to training camp and it was the first padded practice, it was in my head: ‘I do have to hit again,’” Jones said. “I was a little cautious, but once I got going, I felt good. After I got that first hit in, it helped my confidence. I knew I was good, I was healthy and I was able to do this.” The fact that Jones is doing this in the NFL is wildly unlikely given his background. Jones didn’t play organized football until his junior year at Rockford (Ill.) East High School, didn’t play offensive line until his freshman year at Highland (Kan.) Community College, and wasn’t drafted after his two seasons at Middle Tennessee State. “The NFL was never really on my radar,” Jones said. “I was really using football as a vehicle to get my degree. I tried to lock in on that while I was still learning the sport.” Jones grew up in Chicago dreaming of becoming a basketball star. But that ended when he didn’t make his high school team. The message: He was too big. But the 280-pounder was soon approached by a football assistant coach, David Hampton, a former NFL running back. “He told me, ‘Man, you’ve got to play football. You’re a walking meal ticket,’ Jones said. That wasn’t immediately obvious. As a junior, Jones was a backup defensive lineman who quit the team after about five games because, he said, his mom was “terrified” about her only son playing such a violent sport. After Jones returned to earn a starting role as a senior, he was moved to the offensive line when he arrived at Highland. It didn’t click overnight: He didn’t start until his sophomore year. “After that,” Jones said, “the rest is history.” That history includes last year’s painful chapter. Jones suffered his broken neck early in practice, but he was able to finish: He thought he’d suffered a shoulder stinger. Jones even did some post-practice work with a teammate before he finally went to the trainers, who sent him for a CT scan. “That’s when they told me: ‘You broke your C5,’” Jones said.” 6 Winners and 4 losers from the 49ers’ preseason opener “Eason had a play where he sniffed out a screen and forced an incompletion. Kris Kocurek will appreciate that, as defensive line coaches are always saying something along the lines of, “If you’re getting after the quarterback for the first time all game, it’s probably because they want you to.” Eason stood his ground against double teams, pushed the pocket against rookie Jackson Slater, and looked like he belonged in his debut.” 49ers receiver Jordan Watkins produces in another promising NFL preseason opener “I think my diet has been a big part of me being able to stay healthy, especially getting through this camp,” he said. “I’m a really big sweet tea drinker, and I’m trying to stay away from sweet tea and sweet coffee.” Watkins, a fourth-round pick from Ole Miss in the 2025 NFL Draft, spent last season around 195 pounds. This year, he said his weight fluctuates from 202 to 205, and he has dropped body fat, too. He said he eats a lot of protein and has cut out carbohydrates — except for breakfast — from his diet. Watkins’s diet consists of primarily steak, chicken and vegetables, he said. This summer has signified a new start for Watkins, who is competing to become the team’s primary punt returner, too. He handled two punts on Thursday night with a fair catch and a 4-yard return. “It’s been a fun journey, and I feel like I’m getting better,” said Watkins, who ran a time of 4.37 seconds in the 40-yard dash at the NFL Scouting Combine. “Knowing that everybody in the stadium is looking at you, and everyone on the sideline is expecting you to catch the ball. It’s just you and the ball.” 49ers vs. Titans PFF grades: Best and worst from the game, plus snap counts “Defensive tackle Gracen Halton was the 49ers’ highest-graded run defender (75.0), recording a game-high four stops. Cornerback Darrell Luter Jr. came in second with a 74.1 run-defense grade.” 49ers QB Kurtis Rourke released from hospital after rib injury in preseason opener “The San Francisco 49ers announced that quarterback Kurtis Rourke was released from the hospital on Thursday night.”

title: 49ers preseason snap counts and grades: More questions than answers at left guard
summary: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Jordan Watkins is going to be sore this morning after playing a team-high 58 offensive snaps and another five as the return man. Then you have the other side, with the newly signed Zamir White only seeing the field for six snaps late in the game at running back. Let’s […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - JUNE 03: Robert Jones #65 of the San Francisco 49ers looks on during a team OTA practice at SAP Performance Facility on June 3, 2026 in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Jordan Watkins is going to be sore this morning after playing a team-high 58 offensive snaps and another five as the return man. Then you have the other side, with the newly signed Zamir White only seeing the field for six snaps late in the game at running back. Let’s look at the snap counts on the offensive side of the ball from the 49ers’ first preseason game: Offense 58 – Jordan Watkins (WR) 51 – Adrian Martinez (QB) 44 – Austen Pleasants (LT), Brandon Parker (RT), Connor Colby (RG), Drake Nugent (C), Robert Jones (LG) 37 – Hayden Rucci (TE) 35 – Malik Turner (WR) 34 – Brayden Willis (TE), Trenton Irwin (WR) 33 – Carver Willis (LT), Doug Kramer (C), Enrique Cruz Jr. (RT), Isaac Alarcon (RT), Josiah Deguara (TE), Kion Smith (RG) 29 – KhaDarel Hodge (WR) 26 – Kurtis Rourke (QB) 25 – Sincere McCormick (RB) 24 – Khalil Herbert (RB) 22 – De’Zhaun Stribling (WR), Patrick Taylor (RB) 13 – Wesley Grimes (WR), Will Pauling (WR) 6 – Zamir White (RB) Quarterbacks Rourke graded nearly 20 points higher (76.9) than Martinez (57.7), in news that shouldn’t surprise anybody. It was the inverse for rushing grades for both quarterbacks, as Martinez (78.2) won that battle over Rourke (56.3). Rourke avoided a sack that he should get credit for. Martinez was 4-for-13 against the blitz, 12-for-25 when you remove screens, and 4-for-10 on throws beyond 10 yards. Martinez was credited with one turnover-worthy throw and had two drops. Rourke’s average depth of target skyrocketed to 14.3 when blitzed, which is pretty cool to see him get more aggressive. Running backs It feels like you’re nitpicking when you talk about running back performance. Sincere McCormick led the way with a 69.6 grade, while Patrick Taylor (59.6) lost five yards on five carries. Taylor missed a wide-open hole to the left and decided to cut it back when nothing was there. Taylor did get credit for breaking three tackles. Each of the other running backs broke one tackle apiece. Offensive line I’m not a fan of how PFF evaluates offensive linemen, so I take these with a grain of salt. Carver Willis was the highest-graded lineman with an 84.4 grade. He had a 90.1 run blocking grade, but a 55.5 pass blocking grade. Somehow, that averages out to 84.4. Willis allowed three pressures on 23 pass blocking snaps. Austen Pleasants had a 90.9 grade at left tackle, while Connor Colby had a 75.1 at right guard. Colby gave up a pretty bad pressure, but he made no obvious mistakes other than that and competed well. No player had a lower grade than Robert Jones at 34.1. His pass blocking grade was 13.2, despite only allowing one pressure. He also had a penalty. Jones looked like a guy who is going to get in the way and survive. With that said, he didn’t look “bad,” per se. Wide receivers Respectfully skipping over the tight ends, as the three who will play during the season didn’t step onto the field. De’Zhaun Stribling was the highest-graded player by a long shot at 80.9. More importantly, 70.6% of his snaps came in the slot. Stribling also caught all three of his contested targets. He was not credited with a drop for the throw on the first series that was behind him. Jordan Watkins lined up out wide on 92.3% of his snaps, catching five passes for 58 yards. It was good to see Watkins work and win over the middle of the field. He would’ve had another first-down reception had it not been for a penalty. Malik Turner (63.6) seems to have gotten penalized for things out of his control. Had he not dealt with several errant passes, we’re likely talking about a grade similar to Stribling’s. That’s another reason you’ll never hear me cite “yards per route run.” Stribling’s was 4.13, while Turner’s was 0.96. Turner can’t throw it to himself. Defense 53 – Ephesians Prysock (CB) 45 – Darrell Luter Jr. (CB), Jakob Robinson (CB) 35 – Ashtyn Davis (SS), Jalen Stroman (SS) 31 – Sebastian Valdez (DT), Titus Leo (DE) 30 – Gracen Halton (DT), Jaden Dugger (LB) 29 – Tatum Bethune (LB) 26 – Marques Sigle (FS), Nick Martin (LB), Ogbo Okoronkwo (DE), Patrick McMorris (FS) 25 – Quinton Bell (DE) 23 – Jalen Graham (LB) 22 – James Thompson Jr. (DT), Xavier Thomas (DE) 21 – Bryson Eason (DT) 18 – Alfred Collins (DT), Romello Height (DE) 16 – Eli Apple (CB), Garret Wallow (LB) 14 – Larry Worth III (FS) 8 – Jack Jones (CB) Defensive line Bryson Eason (77.3) and Gracen Halton (73.6) led the way for the defensive line. Ogbo Okoronkwo (3) and James Thompson Jr. (2) were the only players credited with more than one pressure. Halton was the only player with more than one run stop. He had four. That’ll play. Thompson Jr. had the highest win percentage as a pass rusher at 18.2%. Okoronkwo was next at 14.3%, followed by Sebastian Valdez at 13.3%. On the flipside, Alfred Collins (28.2) and Romello Height (35.4) were the lowest graded players from the trenches. Collins missed a tackle, which hurt his grade, but he also got pushed around a bit by the Titans starters. Neither of them won a rep as a pass rusher. Linebackers Larry Worth and Tatum Bethune had a sack. Worth also had a run stop. Nick Martin’s average depth of tackle was 5.8 yards. Jaden Dugger (63.8) had a stop and a pair of tackles, while Garret Wallow was the lowest graded player among the group (26.8). Dugger was dinged for allowing a screen pass to go 16 yards, although I’m not sure how you pin that on him. Wallow’s grade was due to coverage, as he allowed both of his targets to go for 22 yards, including 21 yards after the catch. In fairness, it was another screen, and he had to defend a slot receiver on one of those. Secondary Ashtyn Davis(76.8) led the way. He had an interception go right through his hands on a great read. Ephesians Prysock only allowed two receptions for 19 yards on six targets. He also had a pass breakup in the end zone. Raheem Morris will want to see better tackling as Prysock, Jalen Stroman, and Marques Sigle all missed a tackle. He doesn’t get credit for one because he didn’t make contact, but Jack Jones missed one on the play where he suffered a hand injury. Robinson, Darrell Luter Jr., and Eli Apple all gave up first downs that ended up being receptions for at least 10 yards.
author: Kyle Posey

title: Did the 49ers find a defensive gem in the 4th round of the draft?
summary: There was much made of the San Francisco 49ers’ draft strategy in 2026 and from previous drafts. It’s clear the 49ers have their own board, which is put together with physical and character traits that are desired by the organization. After one preseason game, the 49ers’ rookie class was on display against the Titans. De’Zhaun […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 13: Gracen Halton #93 of the San Francisco 49ers rushes up against Pat Coogan #79 of the Tennessee Titans in the second half at Levi's Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images There was much made of the San Francisco 49ers’ draft strategy in 2026 and from previous drafts. It’s clear the 49ers have their own board, which is put together with physical and character traits that are desired by the organization. After one preseason game, the 49ers’ rookie class was on display against the Titans. De’Zhaun Stribling was stellar with seven catches. Ephesians Prysock showed off his speed and length at cornerback. Jaden Dugger flashed while playing multiple spots on the defense. Gracen Halton might have made the biggest impact on Thursday night. The defensive tackle spot has needed an upgrade and now with Osa Odighizuwa and Halton, the team may have found a formidable defensive tackle duo. Unfortunately, Alfred Collins experienced the same issues from last season on Thursday and was routinely moved by Tennessee’s offensive line. C.J. West is still recovering from injury. Halton’s explosive first step was the story against Tennessee. On 15 pass rushing snaps, Halton generated a pressure and a QB hurry. However, against the run, Halton looked excellent, registering four defensive stops on 15 run defense snaps. Finishing with the highest run defense grade (75.0), Halton showed potential to be a three-down defensive tackle. While Romello Height gets most of the attention as a pass rush specialist on obvious passing downs, the rookie struggled a bit. It was assumed the third-down package would consist of Nick Bosa, Odighizuwa, Mykel Williams (DT), and Height. It is still one preseason game, but the pass rushing package could be Bosa, Osa, Halton, and Mykel. This may sound hyperbolic, but the duo of Odighizuwa and Halton is the best 49ers defensive tackle duo since DeForest Buckner and Arik Armstead. What was once a weakness on the defensive line looks to be a strength in 2026. The 49ers might have found a gem in the fourth round. Drafting an impact player in the middle rounds has been the 49ers’ specialty, but it’s hard not to be excited about Halton and his potential.
author: Jason Aponte

title: 6 Winners and 4 losers from the 49ers’ preseason opener
summary: The San Francisco 49ers had their first preseason game, where we witnessed Adrian Martinez throw the ball 30 times and the running backs show us what three yards and a cloud of dust looks like. The scoreboard doesn’t matter in the preseason. You want to see players making plays. The box score can be deceiving, […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - AUGUST 13: Tatum Bethune #48 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates a tackle for a loss during a preseason NFL game against the Tennessee Titans on August 13, 2026 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers had their first preseason game, where we witnessed Adrian Martinez throw the ball 30 times and the running backs show us what three yards and a cloud of dust looks like. The scoreboard doesn’t matter in the preseason. You want to see players making plays. The box score can be deceiving, as not all tackles are created equally. Let’s get into the winners and losers from Week 1 of the preseason. Winners Tatum Bethune Bethune had the biggest highlight of the evening when he ran through rookie running back Nicholas Singleton’s face for a sack. Bethune was the aggressor all night and likely cemented himself onto the roster. Most of his tackles came near the line of scrimmage. Bethune wasn’t hesitant and was flying around. He should be a core special-teamer for the 49ers this season. He was impressive. Bryson Eason Eason can play. He was on the field for 24 snaps and left an impression. Eason made an impact without showing up in the box score with plays like this: 4th play of the game for the 49ers D. Halton and Height get credit for the tackle but it's Bryson Eason who has the right guard fighting for his life playing on one leg and forces the running back to redirect. Doesn't show up in the box score, but this is how you make the roster pic.twitter.com/vPDLb7CxHz — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) August 14, 2026 Eason had a play where he sniffed out a screen and forced an incompletion. Kris Kocurek will appreciate that, as defensive line coaches are always saying something along the lines of, “If you’re getting after the quarterback for the first time all game, it’s probably because they want you to.” Eason stood his ground against double teams, pushed the pocket against rookie Jackson Slater, and looked like he belonged in his debut. De’Zhaun Stribling Stribling didn’t start too hot: he missed a block against edge rusher Jermaine Johnson, resulting in a tackle for loss; then, technically, dropped a pass; and followed that up by stumbling on a route on fourth down. The jitters wore off after that as Stribling caught his final six targets and continued to get open cleanly even when the ball wasn’t thrown in his direction. It’s refreshing to see a wide receiver have zero issues catching the ball. Stribling still needs to evolve as a route runner, but he’s winning down the field already against starters. If Brandon Lloyd shaved off two tenths from his 40 and played in a Kyle Shanahan offense. That’s Stribling. That’s a compliment. Kurtis Rourke Rourke ran out of multiple sacks and avoided the negative plays behind a second-string offensive line. Talk about impressive. He was a tick late on a couple of throws early on, but the more Rourke dropped back, the more he threw with anticipation. We’ll see if the 49ers feel like he made Mac Jones expendable a couple of months from now, but Rourke looked comfortable in muddy pockets and never panicked. I was most impressed with his scrambling ability and encouraged by Rourke’s willingness to push the ball down the field. Losers Adrian Martinez Martinez stepping out of bounds then throwing it underhand before the half for what would have been an easy interception had he stayed in bounds is enough to land him here. Thirty attempts with an average of 5.3 yards is comical. He took a pair of sacks he shouldn’t have. Martinez overthrew wide receivers left and right. He missed Jordan Watkins and Malik Turner on sure-fire touchdowns down the field. It was a rough watch for a quarterback who probably shouldn’t take another snap in the preseason for this team. Nick Martin Oy. Martin looks like a player who has no idea what’s happening in front of him. Watching him side by side with Tatum Bethune further proves this. Bethune would be at the line of scrimmage throwing his body into an offensive lineman, while Martin is still bouncing up and down in the same spot. Martin led the team with eight tackles, but even the ones at the line of scrimmage deserve an asterisk. For example, he had a clean shot on Will Levis, but he fell off the tackle as the whistle blew. Early on in the game, Martin came off the field on passing downs for Garret Wallow. A personal foul won’t help his cause, nor will running into the middle of a blocker after you’re late triggering, leading to a big play. Martin gave the team no reason to move forward with this charade. Romello Height Height wasn’t gunshy, which is what you want to see, but he also looked like a one-trick pony against the Titans starting left tackle. He actually got put on his backside and was handled rather easily. When Height was on the move, he was at his best. Still, in 1-on-1 situations, he left a lot to be desired. It’s early, but it wasn’t a great first impression for the first defender the 49ers drafted this year. Having a penalty doesn’t help, either. Marques Sigle It was the same Sigle from Kansas State and the same Sigle from his rookie year on Thursday. Leaving his feet to tackle, a step late as he’s determining whether he should trust what he sees, bracing for blocks instead of running through the block. It’s funny to hear the defensive backs all say, “We like this scheme because there isn’t much thinking and we can just play,” when in reality, they’re doing the same things as last year and playing similar coverages. Ashtyn Davis did all of the things we needed to see from Sigle at safety. Winners Malik Turner Turner was great. He only caught two of his six targets for 23 yards, but he could’ve easily had close to 80 yards had he received accurate throws. Turner was wide open on a couple of passes that went to Stribling on the other side. He also won down the field. It was an impressive showing for the big-bodied receiver fighting for a roster spot. Gracen Halton Halton’s effort stood out. He chased down a screen that went for 12 yards, and that alone would’ve been enough to land him here. Having a sack where he worked to the half of man — something Martin should take note of — had to bring a smile to Kocurek’s face, even if the play was nullified because of a penalty. Halton had a tackle for loss, another stop after a clean win, and was feisty against double teams, not giving up after initially losing. That’s the fight you want to see from an undersized defensive tackle. Honorable mentions James Thompson Jr. Jordan Watkins Sebastian Valdez Ashtyn Davis
author: Kyle Posey

title: 3 stars for the 49ers: Did Kurtis Rourke make Mac Jones expendable?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers played the Tennessee Titans in both teams’ preseason openers on Thursday night, with the Titans coming out on top by a final score of who cares; it’s the first preseason game.  What we are here to take away is who the top performers were in a game where there are plenty […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - AUGUST 13: Kurtis Rourke #14 of the San Francisco 49ers runs the ball during a preseason NFL game against the Tennessee Titans on August 13, 2026 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers played the Tennessee Titans in both teams’ preseason openers on Thursday night, with the Titans coming out on top by a final score of who cares; it’s the first preseason game. What we are here to take away is who the top performers were in a game where there are plenty of 49ers players who are vying to make this roster. Some players stood out (see the three players below), while others didn’t help their case. These are the three players who stood out the most on Thursday night for the 49ers’ first dress rehearsal of the 2026 season: 3rd Star – LB Jaden Dugger Multiple players on defense were considered to earn a star on Thursday. Ephesians Prysock for his end zone pass breakup against first-round pick Carnell Tate in the first quarter. Or even Gracen Halton for bullying the freshly paid Peter Skoronski for a sack, which was negated by a Jakob Robinson holding in the secondary. But no player on the 49ers defense capitalized on their training camp hype like Dugger. Entrenched in a battle against Nick Martin for the SAM linebacker spot, Dugger made a quick and solid first impression. As with most of the 49ers starters, Dugger didn’t play too long, resulting in just a pair of tackles, but No. 53 was certainly noticeable. On Tennessee’s second play from scrimmage, Cam Ward looked to scramble, but Dugger wouldn’t allow it. After dropping back about ten yards off the line of scrimmage, Dugger made an instantaneous read and broke towards the quarterback with a great pursuit and met Ward at the 24-yard line, holding the play for just a two-yard gain. Dugger followed up with a great arm tackle on the Titans’ next drive to hold a Tyjae Spears run to just four yards. It was a quick appearance from Dugger in his first NFL game time, but an effective one from the rookie as he looks to position himself as a starter on the San Francisco defense. 2nd Star – QB Kurtis Rourke If Kurtis Rourke can continue to look as good as he did on Thursday night, Mac Jones could be an expendable piece as we get closer to the trade deadline. Rourke looked every part of an NFL quarterback in his first look since the 49ers drafted him in 2025. The quarterback impressed while playing just three drives (a rib injury ended his night prematurely), completing 12-of-14 passes for 101 yards. What impressed most about Rourke in his debut was his ability to keep plays alive with his legs and keep his eyes upfield. Facing an early fourth down on the 49ers’ opening drive, the pocket collapsed on Rourke pretty quickly. But instead of panic, Rourke was able to escape the grasp of Cody Barton to avoid the sack, then remove himself from the traffic, and move forward for a gain of six to extend the drive. On San Francisco’s next drive, Rourke was able to keep the play alive with his legs, scrambling to his right, keeping his eyes downfield. He found Patrick Taylor in the end zone in about the same spot Brock Purdy hit Jake Tonges last season in Week 1 in Seattle. However, unlike Tonges, Taylor couldn’t keep both feet in bounds, resulting in an incomplete pass, but still a good rep on film for Rourke. Rourke is in a battle with Adrian Martinez for the third quarterback spot on the roster, and if Rourke wasn’t ahead of Martinez before Thursday, he definitely created some distance with his game against the Titans. 1st Star – WR De’Zhaun Stribling I don’t think we’ll see Stribling take another snap in the preseason. We have collected all the information we need on him. Stribling was far and away the 49ers’ most impressive player on Thursday night, hauling in seven catches for 63 yards, leading all pass-catchers. It was obvious the offensive game plan was centered around Stribling, with Rourke’s first pass targeting the 49ers’ first selection of the 2026 draft. Things would only get more impressive from there for Stribling. His third reception of the game would be Jauan Jennings-esque, hanging on to a pass with a Titans defender draped all over him right at the marker for a first down. Stribling would also be responsible for the 49ers’ longest play from scrimmage on a play that should tell 49ers fans he is NFL-ready. Facing a third-and-5, Rourke threw a beautiful back shoulder pass on a go route run by the receiver. Stribling made an incredible adjustment to the ball, contorting his body to haul in the pass and keep both feet in bounds. When it was all said and done, it was a gain of 32. Eight plays later, the 49ers would find the end zone for their lone touchdown on the night. Stribling was far and away the best player red and gold on Thursday night. Four months ago the conversation surrounding Stribling was about if the 49ers reached too far for him. Now it’s about just how high his ceiling is.
author: Andrew Pasquini

title: 49ers News: Rookies make a strong first impression in Titans preseason game
summary: What Kyle Shanahan and others said after 49ers’ 19-13 loss vs. Titans“Yeah, [Saleh and I are] not the biggest note takers, but we’re more FaceTimers. So, we sat there and FaceTimed a little bit the last two nights, just talking about what we saw from each other. It’s a little bit easier when you’re in […]
full_text: De'Zhaun Stribling (15) catches a pass from Kurtis Rourke (14) in the first half as the San Francisco 49ers played the Tennessee Titans in a preseason game at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif., on Thursday, Aug. 13, 2026. (Photo by Carlos Avila Gonzalez/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images) What Kyle Shanahan and others said after 49ers’ 19-13 loss vs. Titans “Yeah, [Saleh and I are] not the biggest note takers, but we’re more FaceTimers. So, we sat there and FaceTimed a little bit the last two nights, just talking about what we saw from each other. It’s a little bit easier when you’re in different conferences. You don’t have to lie as much. You can be a little bit more honest, but I know he definitely isn’t always. He’s still trying to find things out and so am I, but it was good for us to practice against each other, have someone that you know. Especially seeing [Tennessee Titans defensive coordinator] Gus [Bradley] and stuff and [Tennessee Titans defensive run game coordinator/defensive line coach Aaron] Whitecotton, who was here for a little bit, [Tennessee Titans defensive pass game coordinator/cornerbacks coach] Tony Oden. It was good to catch up with all those guys this week.” 49ers rookie WR De’Zhaun Stribling stars in preseason opener, outshining Titans’ Carnell Tate (paywall) “Stribling caught the first pass of the game and remained a go-to guy on third downs over the course of three offensive drives. Hold your third-and-De’Zhaun outbursts for the end. Three of his catches came on third downs, including two conversions via a 32-yard back-shoulder bomb that Stribling grabbed up high and an 11-yard reception that Stribling turned into a first down with several yards after catch. Maybe he stepped out of bounds before converting the latter, but whatever, it’s preseason. He was downed a yard shy of the sticks on the other third-down catch.” 49ers QB Kurtis Rourke’s first game action in 601 days ends with injury (paywall) “Before his premature exit, Rourke completed 12 of 14 passes for 101 yards, and he rushed for 14 yards on three carries. The 2025 seventh-round pick left shortly after he was whacked by two defenders on a three-yard scramble midway through the second quarter. “They said ‘ribs’ and he was struggling to breathe, so they took him to the hospital just to check on everything, make sure it’s all right,” head coach Kyle Shanahan said. “The X-rays here didn’t show it was broken or anything, but we’ll see what we find out tomorrow.” 49ers preseason takeaways: De’Zhaun Stribling hype train rolling, Kurtis Rourke injured (paywall) “ Halton has had a nasty streak during training camp, and that showed up in back-to-back plays Thursday night. He would have had a sack, working through Titans starting linemen Peter Skoronski and Dan Moore Jr., if not for a defensive holding penalty in the secondary. On the next snap, Halton threw an offensive lineman to the side and wrapped up running back Tyjae Spears for a loss of a yard. “Once I get hot, it’s over with,” Halton said. “I win one, and then next thing you know, I’m in my head like, ‘OK, I got this.’ So I build that confidence, and it’s over.” What we learned as De’Zhaun Stribling stars in 49ers’ preseason-opening loss “Halton, a fourth-round pick from Oklahoma, is constantly around the ball and causing disruption in practices. He took advantage of his action on Thursday with three tackles in the first half, including a stop of running back Tyjae Spears for a 1-yard loss. Halton had a 14-yard sack of Cam Ward nullified by a defensive holding penalty on Jakob Robinson. Dugger started at the 49ers’ “fever backer” position and played the entire first half. He did not wait long to show some of his immense physical talent. On the second defensive snap, he ran down Ward to hold him for just a 2-yard gain on a scramble. Four plays later, he got stuck on right tackle JC Latham’s block on a third-and-10 play and could not prevent a short pass to that side going for 16 yards.”
author: Yinon Raviv

title: Ahead of the Buccaneers first preseason game, Vita Vea is ‘hoping’ contract talks continue
summary: Vita Vea’s future with the Buccaneers remains a storyline worth watching, and former NFL running back Maurice Jones-Drew offered an encouraging update on where things stand with Tampa Bay’s defensive anchor. Jones-Drew said he recently spoke with Vea, who has remained in the Tampa area rather than returning home to California as he prepares for […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - AUGUST 9: Vita Vea #50 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers watches practice during training camp at AdventHealth Training Center on August 9, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Vita Vea’s future with the Buccaneers remains a storyline worth watching, and former NFL running back Maurice Jones-Drew offered an encouraging update on where things stand with Tampa Bay’s defensive anchor. Jones-Drew said he recently spoke with Vea , who has remained in the Tampa area rather than returning home to California as he prepares for the season. “We spoke a little bit about kind of where he’s living,” Jones-Drew said. “He’s saying he’s staying in the Tampa area. He doesn’t want to go home [back to California] because he may get a little bit bigger.” More importantly, Vea appears hopeful that conversations regarding his contract will continue as he also wants to build up Tampa Bay’s young defensive players. “He’s hoping the talks continue there on his contract,” Jones-Drew added. “He’s still coaching his guys. We saw the defensive line look really good with Reuben Bain, and [Vea is] excited.” Despite the uncertainty, it’s that Vea remains involved with his teammates. Jones-Drew noted that Vea hopes he gets the chance to play alongside them. For the Buccaneers, keeping Vea in Tampa long term would preserve one of the defense’s most important veteran leaders and interior playmakers.
author: Gil Arcia

title: Tampa Bay Buccaneers news: Preseason opener vs. Jets
summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are scheduled to face off against the New York Jets in their preseason opener tonight at 7 p.m. ET inside MetLife Stadium. After facing off in joint practices earlier in the week, the Bucs and Jets get to showcase themselves on a larger stage with brighter lights. Bucs Nation, how do […]
full_text: FLORHAM PARK, NEW JERSEY - AUGUST 11: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Aaron Glenn head coach of the New York Jets during a joint practice between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and New York Jets at Atlantic Health Jets Training Center on August 11, 2026 in Florham Park, New Jersey. (Photo by Adam Hunger/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are scheduled to face off against the New York Jets in their preseason opener tonight at 7 p.m. ET inside MetLife Stadium. After facing off in joint practices earlier in the week, the Bucs and Jets get to showcase themselves on a larger stage with brighter lights. Bucs Nation, how do you feel about the preseason opener? Let us know in the comments section below. Today’s Buccaneers news Why the Buccaneers’ Offensive Line is Poised to Dominate This Season | Tampa Bay Buccaneers On SI The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are expected to field a starting offensive line with Tristan Wirfs, Luke Goedeke, Cody Mauch, Ben Bredeson and Graham Barton. Wirfs is one of the best offensive tackles in the league, and the rest of the group is improving with experience. They have performed well in training camp so far and this position group could be a real strength of the team. title: Ranking the Titans’ 5 projected cornerbacks from best to worst
summary: The Tennessee Titans totally revamped the cornerback room this offseason. They signed three unrestricted free agents to notable contracts. After trading Roger McCreary and Jarvis Brownlee last season, they cut L’Jarius Sneed earlier this summer. With a new-look cornerback room, we’ve ranked the Titans’ projected five cornerbacks from best to worst. Alontae Taylor The Titans […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - AUGUST 15: Marcus Harris #26 of the Tennessee Titans walks across the field during an NFL preseason football game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on August 15, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans totally revamped the cornerback room this offseason. They signed three unrestricted free agents to notable contracts. After trading Roger McCreary and Jarvis Brownlee last season, they cut L’Jarius Sneed earlier this summer. With a new-look cornerback room, we’ve ranked the Titans’ projected five cornerbacks from best to worst. Alontae Taylor The Titans paid Alontae Taylor handsomely to be their No. 1 cornerback . He’s flexible enough to occasionally play nickel, but the belief is that Taylor will exclusively defend the boundary for Saleh’s defense in Tennessee. The Titans paid him lucratively to be a high-level outside cornerback. Cor’Dale Flott Cor’Dale Flott was the Titans’ other prized signing in free agency , inking a three-year contract worth $45 million. He’s an ascending cornerback whose advanced metrics (passer rating allowed, ball production) have increased with each passing season. Flott may end up being the Titans’ most impactful cornerback. Marcus Harris The Titans are extremely excited about having Marcus Harris as the nickelback this season. The sophomore defender is essentially being unchallenged for that position. Harris flashed impressive play in stretches as a rookie, and Coach Saleh has been excited about working with him this offseason. Joshua Williams Mike Borgonzi signed Joshua Williams in free agency partially due to his familiarity with them from their shared days together with the Kansas City Chiefs. Williams is expected to be the new Darrell Baker Jr. He’s a big and long cornerback, and should be the primary reserve option off the bench behind Taylor and Flott. Keydrain Calligan The Titans are holding an open competition for the fifth (and probably) final spot at cornerback during training camp. The contenders include Micah Robinson, Keydrain Calligan, and undrafted free agents like Latrell McCutchin. We wouldn’t rule out another addition, but Calligan was arguably the best option during OTAs and minicamp.

title: Commanders 20, Dolphins 7: Five takeaways from Washington preseason win
summary: The Washington Commanders took the field for the first time this preseason, with a Friday night showdown with the Miami Dolphins at Northwest Stadium.   Well, some of them, anyway.   Washington announced that 26 players would sit this one out, including quarterback Jayden Daniels. Established offensive and defensive linemen also stayed on the sideline. […]
full_text: The Washington Commanders took the field for the first time this preseason, with a Friday night showdown with the Miami Dolphins at Northwest Stadium. Well, some of them, anyway. Washington announced that 26 players would sit this one out, including quarterback Jayden Daniels. Established offensive and defensive linemen also stayed on the sideline. So did Terry McLaurin, Stefon Diggs, Bill Croskey-Merritt and most prominent skill players. There was still plenty to glean from this exhibition, as the Commanders progress toward the regular season. Rookies Sonny Styles and Antonio Williams suited up for their first NFL action, with a few other regulars. That experience was a plus. So was the information gathered about position battles and who might fit well into the 53-man roster — Drew Stevens took another step ahead in the kicking battle — despite the fact the Commanders didn’t show much schematically. And while preseason games are played at a lower competition level, the fact that a Commanders defense starved for turnovers in 2025 had three interceptions. There was also an early injury concern in this one, but the Commanders finished the night with a 20-7 victory over the Dolphins. Feels good to be back pic.twitter.com/dgxQRzlB2l — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) August 15, 2026 While Mark Tyler will bring you Studs and Duds on Saturday, here are five quick takeaways from the watching the 2026 preseason opener live: Marcus Mariota’s injury trouble Veteran quarterback Marcus Mariota started Friday night’s game with Daniels out, but his outing didn’t last long. He came up lame on Washington’s fourth offensive snap. Mariota threw an incomplete pass, conducted a run play and then threw a 22-yard strike to Dyami Brown. As you can see in the video below, he took a shot after delivering that pass and was knocked hard to the ground. Mariota’s knee was also noted to buckle on the following first-down play. Marcus Mariota —> Dyami Brown pic.twitter.com/9S7DxXd16b — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) August 14, 2026 Mariota started limping after handing the ball off to Kaytron Allen and eventually went to the ground. Trainers examined his right knee on the field, though Mariota was able to walk off the field on his own. He spent time in the medical tent and eventually left the field with a trainer. Marcus Mariota is headed back to the locker room with assistant head athletic trainer Mark McCracken. pic.twitter.com/mlwVDhnkWT — Nicki Jhabvala (@NickiJhabvala) August 14, 2026 In two words, not good. The Commanders didn’t make a formal announcement about the nature of Mariota’s injury – they aren’t obligated to do so until the regular season – but any issue with Mariota isn’t great. He’s a valuable asset on this team, someone capable of orchestrating the offense should Daniels be unavailable. Mariota’s way better than other backup options in Sam Hartman and Athan Kaliakmanis, so his health is paramount in the regular season. Per, The Athletic ’s Nicki Jhabvala , head coach Dan Quinn said after the game that he didn’t have an update on Mariota and would provide one on Sunday, when he’s next scheduled to speak to the media. In other injury news, cornerback Fred Davis II was carted off the field and linebacker Ale Kaho left early, heading to the locker room in the fourth quarter after recording an interception. Davis II told Commanders reporter Ben Standig that he had a full-body cramp. Sonny Styles, Antonio Williams see first NFL action The Commanders kept most of their starters in street clothes for Friday night’s game. Not No. 7 overall NFL draft pick Sonny Styles. The Ohio State product started this game and wore the green dot calling defensive plays during his short time in the game. Styles played just one defensive series – Leo Chenal was his wingman – and had three total tackles against the first-team Miami offense. Here’s what Styles had to say about his short stint in the game: Sonny Styles says he wishes he had another series but was happy to get out there and see the stadium pic.twitter.com/GEZ7aZnvqy — JP Finlay (@JPFinlayNBCS) August 15, 2026 It wasn’t a great defensive series for the group, largely composed of backups, but Styles’ experience was an important thing. He got his feet wet, helped the defense line up and didn’t get hurt. That’s a win for a rookie expected to be an every-down defender. Williams entered this game to start the fourth offensive series and caught his first pass in the third quarter. It was 16-yard completion from Kaliakmanis, executed with a nice throw and quality route. Antonio Williams with his first NFL reception – 16yds pic.twitter.com/gUOZgOJ9Lj — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 Robert Henry Jr. and the Fatman Croskey-Merritt, Rachaad White and rookie sixth-rounder Kaytron Allen have received most training camp focus among running backs, which makes some sense. Croskey-Merritt and White are established. White’s part of the 2026 draft class, and prefers to go by “Fatman,” for goodness sakes. Robert Henry Jr.’s an undrafted free agent with less pedigree, even though he piled up stats at Texas-San Antonio last season. He was surely impressive in this one, with some explosive runs and solid pass protection. Henry did a good job setting up his blocks before showing solid burst working in space. Henry brought all that to bear on this excellent 22-yard touchdown run: Robert Henry Jr. takes it 22 yards for his first NFL TD! pic.twitter.com/xbeWJqwLgR — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) August 15, 2026 Overall, Henry had 12 carries for 75 yards and the touchdown (above), for a 6.3-yards-per-carry average. He was also active in the return game, as the Commanders try to find ways for him to contribute Allen saw plenty of action as well, and found the end zone in the first half with the type of tough run he was brought here to execute. Kaytron "Fatman" Allen's first NFL TD! pic.twitter.com/AahNU3eKdz — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) August 15, 2026 Allen led the team with 85 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries and also has some moves. FatMan has some WIGGLE! pic.twitter.com/EzlOyTsKGO — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 15, 2026 A few thoughts Quan Martin Safety Quan Martin is battling for a starting safety spot, with competition from veteran Jeremy Reeves. And, on a day where most key players sat, Martin played and Reaves didn’t. Is that a sign of who’s in front of that camp battle, or did the coaches give a ninth-year vet preseason game off and let a younger buck play? Per The Athletic , Quinn said that playing Martin and Will Harris together at safety was by design. Dan Quinn said after the game that this could change in the next preseason game, indicating there's a chance Martin is inactive for the next one and Reaves starts. Nothing certain yet, but made it clear it was by design to give Martin and Harris extended time at safety in this… — Nicki Jhabvala (@NickiJhabvala) August 15, 2026 Regardless, Martin tried to put his best foot forward in this one. While Dolphins quarterback Quinn Ewers clearly wasn’t on the same page with his receiver, Martin capitalized with an interception that shifted momentum to the Commanders in the first half. Quan with the pick 😮‍💨 #MIAvsWAS @wusa9 pic.twitter.com/jxqMd16qyJ — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) August 14, 2026 You have to make plays when they’re available and Martin did that. His position battle will surely continue, possibly throughout the preseason for who will play safety next to Nick Cross and be featured in three-safety sets. Sam Hartman, Athan Kaliakmanis and the No. 3 QB Mariota’s injury left most of the game to young quarterbacks battling to be the team’s No. 3 quarterback. Sam Hartman was the first man off the bench for Mariota. He had some good throws and more than a few he’d like back while going 8-for-15 passing for 80 yards and an interception. Kaliakmanis was slightly more efficient in his time, which started with the second half’s second…

full_text: The NFL announced that Washington Commanders DE Dorance Armstrong has been suspended for 1 game for violating the personal conduct policy. Armstrong is recovering from a torn ACL, and was placed on the active/PUP list before the start of training camp last month, but was taken off of it on Aug. 7 . Armstrong has been at practice, but is still sidelined and his availability for the season opener in Philadelphia against the Eagles wasn’t guaranteed. The suspension officially starts on Aug. 30 and he’s eligible for reinstatement on Mon., Sept. 14. He will be eligible to participate in all preseason activities, including games. Nick Allegretti’s calf injury removed the early favorite from the competition ; what initially looked like temporary replacement work has now become a much broader evaluation. Julian Good-Jones handled the primary duties in Wednesday’s joint practice with the Miami Dolphins , but did very little to give any impression that Washington had found its answer. Against Miami, Good-Jones had some difficult reps against the Dolphins’ defensive tackles and was driven backward on multiple occasions. The Contenders: Brunskill and Hill Add Veteran Experience Good-Jones and Matt Gulbin initially absorbed the opportunities created by Allegretti’s injury before Washington subsequently added Trey Hill and veteran Daniel Brunskill.Brunskill has appeared in 108 NFL games and adds 71 career starts to a group that otherwise lacks significant starting experience behind Allegretti. Seeing Good-Jones still handling the lion’s share of the snaps tells me that Brunskill hasn’t displaced him yet, but it is nice to have that experience in the room when needed now. With Allegretti being out, several of the team’s center options will be on display against the Dolphins. The most useful detail the staff can get from that game-time situation is how well each option communicates with his fellow linemen and the quarterback. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Roundtable Three storylines to watch in the first preseason game on Friday night The WR/RB Depth Chart Shuffle With Stefon Diggs now in the fold, the top of the wide receiver depth chart is solidified, but the back end of the room is wide open. I anticipate the Commanders keeping seven receivers, but will a versatile weapon like tight end Colson Yankoff force the coaches’ hand and steal a spot? What to Watch: The running back rotation will be a fun watch. Jacory Croskey-Merritt has added significant mass this offseason and offers legitimate home-run upside, while Rachaad White remains the most reliable option for passing downs. However, keep your eyes on Kaytron “Fatman” Allen. This will be our first look at him in live pads, and I have a sneaky suspicion he will shoulder the bulk of the carries and quickly endear himself to the home crowd. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Last Man Standig (paywall) One of the Commanders’ surprise standouts is becoming hard to ignore Colson Yankoff’s athleticism got him into the NFL. His development as a pass-catching tight end could earn him a much larger role. Now a tight end, Yankoff went from an unknown 2024 UDFA to making the Week 1 roster as a core special teams contributor. Former Commanders tight end Zach Ertz declared Yankoff “one of, if not the fastest guy on the team, which is crazy for being as big as he is.” A more tight end-friendly offensive scheme featuring frequent two- and three-TE sets creates additional opportunities. The Commanders have flexed Yankoff away from the formation, giving him chances to operate in space. “He’s got good speed. We’ve split him out some to say, ‘Can he use space?’” Head coach Dan Quinn said. “So, it’s in the passing game that we featured him more.” For more from Ben Standig, click here Commanders.com Mailbag: Reviewing the joint practice with the Dolphins Whose stock are you buying more of and whose stock are you holding onto based on camp and the joint practice? This is fun because I get to participate in something the boys on the “Command Center” podcast do a lot. For buying stock, there are a lot of players to choose from, but I have to go with Odafe Oweh. The dude was in the backfield a lot during 11-on-11 drills and causing all kinds of havoc for Malik Willis and the rest of the Dolphins’ quarterbacks. He’s proving to be worth the investment the Commanders made in him. And for holding on, I’m going to go with Mike Sainristil. He reminded people yesterday that he has a nose for the ball, which continues to be his best strength. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) Efe Obada retires after trailblazing an unlikely path to the NFL In 2002, Obada and his sister were smuggled into London via the Netherlands by a stranger. Their mother was supposed to join them shortly afterwards. The goal was a happier, better life, but that failed to materialize. After reaching London, the siblings were abandoned and, due to visa issues, their mother never came. Initially, they lived on the streets before being taken into care, moving between multiple foster homes. “What a lot of people don’t see about my journey is that the Disney version’s out there. And it’s great because I can use it as a tool, as a means to inspire and motivate, and shed some hope in my community,” Obada tells The Athletic . “Everyone’s like, cool story, cool story . But these are lived experiences and some of these things that I’ve had to overcome involve a long-lasting effect. It’s not something that just goes away overnight. Therapy did help. But because I have lots of trust issues, it was very hard for me to find someone I could trust and to let my guard down and be open and communicate with. “I fell through a lot of the cracks. I know the system tries to help and uplift, but I’ve lived it. full_text: The Washington Commanders just gave their fanbase the ultimate NFL offseason whiplash, packaging a franchise-altering blockbuster signing and a devastating injury into the exact same week. By bringing the talented receiver Stefon Diggs to D.C., general manager Adam Peters signaled that the future is officially now. But just as fans were getting through the first wave of tweets about Diggs’ first practice, All-Pro left tackle Laremy Tunsil went down with a torn triceps—a brutal blow that sidelines him for months and potentially the entire 2026 season. Consider what offensive coordinator David Blough said about each of them in this week’s training camp press conference: Stefon Diggs I think Stef on adds an element of experience – [he’s] savvy [and] understands timing & leverage. He’s played a lot of meaningful football, a lot of yards. I think through having him for three practices, you feel his leadership too. You feel him bringing the guys together, challenging everybody to keep pushing forward. In just a couple days, you guys have seen, four catches the other day. He had at least two or three today. The ball finds him, because he finds space. He moves the chains; he has [done that] his whole career, so, he will certainly move the chains a lot for us this year, but all those [other players] will be ready to execute when we dial it up for them [as well]. Laremy Tunsil/Brandon Coleman When you lose a player like [Laremy Tunsil], man, it’s hard. But, DQ [and] ourselves as offense, we believe in the next man up and we’re gonna just keep plugging away. And so there will be things that have to change, but we have all the trust in the world in Brandon [Coleman] . He’s played really well at left tackle over the last few years and we’re excited to feature some of the things he does well too. From having to play all those starts his rookie year to different experiences last year, and us sharing with him that he was gonna be the left tackle and him lighting up, eager for the opportunity to go after this thing — I think he has demonstrated everything that we’re looking for to protect that side for us. When a team simultaneously fires a rocket booster into its passing game and yanks the anchor out of its offensive line, how does a fan base respond? This week’s Reacts survey of Hogs Haven readers reveals a community almost perfectly split into three distinct camps, reflecting a keen understanding of the high-wire act that is the 2026 season. Visit our partners at FanDuel The Centrists (37%: Confidence Unchanged) The largest portion of the fanbase is taking a distinctly D.C. approach: bureaucratic neutrality. For these fans, the net-zero nature of the week leaves expectations exactly where they started. This group understands that the 2026 Commanders comprise a team built on depth of talent at most position groups. Adding Stefon Diggs to a receiving corps that already boasts Terry McLaurin gives offensive coordinator David Blough an enhanced set of weapons. The perimeter spacing will be challenging for defenders, and the pick-your-poison dilemmas for opposing defensive coordinators are real. However, the pragmatic 37% also know that Jayden Daniels requires a clean pocket to stay healthy for the full season. Losing Tunsil may cancel out the tactical advantage of the Diggs signing. You can have the most expensive sports car in the neighborhood, but it won’t go far if someone lets the air out of the front-left tire. Fortunately, the team’s depth provides a capable player in Brandon Coleman as the premium spare tire ready to keep the car moving forward. Brandon Coleman played 998 snaps at LT in 2024, including the playoffs, as a rookie. He was charged by @PFF with 10 sacks allowed. Not ideal but he never looked lost. He played a couple of games late last year & looked fine. The #Commanders suffered a blow, but not screwed. — Chris Russell AKA the 🐓🐓! (@Russellmania621) August 10, 2026 The Cassandra view (32%: Less Confident) Then there are the scar-tissue traditionalists. Decades of heartbreaking franchise history have trained a third of the fan base to always look for the structural flaw. For them, Tunsil’s injury is a flashing red light. Laremy Tunsil wasn’t just a starter; he was the insurance policy for the franchise’s most valuable asset. Head coach Dan Quinn wants to build a culture of physical dominance, and Tunsil was the cornerstone of that identity on offense. Without an elite blindside protector, the entire geometric calculus of the blocking schemes changes. This 32% isn’t ignoring Diggs’ talent; they are simply worried that by the time Diggs breaks away from a defensive back, the opposition pass rush will have already collapsed the pocket from the left side (and maybe the center, too). Discussing the Commanders post Tunsil injury with @ByKevinClark : "I loved the Stefon Diggs signing. I loved the way things were trending in Washington. The Tunsil injury changes everything.. No other way to put it. This stinks for everybody" — Grant Paulsen (@GrantPaulsen) August 10, 2026 The Pollyanna view (31%: More Confident) Remarkably, nearly a third of the fan base emerged from this chaotic week more optimistic than before. While adding a route-running technician like Diggs is plenty of reason to celebrate, this group’s confidence hinges heavily on a specific roster contingency: Brandon Coleman. I'm less worried about the Tunsil injury after rewatching some of Brandon Coleman at LT last year. I thought he did a really nice job stepping in especially in pass protection. The offense didn't leave him 1-on-1 too often but when he was, he was solid pic.twitter.com/M0EzDKUAfT — Nick Akridge (@nick_akridge) August 10, 2026 The young tackle is no longer a developmental project luxury—he is now the literal bodyguard of the offense. The optimistic 31% are leaning into the coaching staff’s ability to adapt. With David Blough’s new-look offense and Coleman’s still-developing physical upside, the optimists believe the drop-off from Tunsil will be a manageable slope rather than a cliff. If Coleman can provide even league-average stability at left tackle, the addition of Diggs elevates this offense from an intriguing unit to a potential top-10 powerhouse behind a healthy Jayden Daniels, unlocking the elite dual-threat skills that secured him the 2024 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year award. I was also pleasantly surprised with him in the run game. We know he's athletic but he was also moving dudes. He can get a bit aggressive and lunge but overall not too concerner. (Watch the LT on every play, highlighting him every time takes surprisingly way too long to edit) pic.twitter.com/Qs7Y53Y2cv — Nick Akridge (@nick_akridge) August 10, 2026 The 2026 Outlook Ultimately, these survey results indicate a highly knowledgeable fanbase that recognizes the 2026 season will not be boring. The margin for error is slim, but the ceiling remains tantalizingly high. If the coaching staff can successfully patch together a unified and well-functioning offensive line, the Commanders have the firepower to orchestrate something truly special in the NFC East. The game is scheduled to start at 7:00 PM EDT.
