title: Washington Commanders 91-man 2026 preseason Game 1 roster/depth chart
summary: Reviewing the roster limit As you are probably aware, the NFL CBA allows each team to have 90 players on its offseason roster, but it also makes provisions for a 91st player who joins the team via the International Player Pathway (IPP) program. For the last several years, the Commanders have made use of this […]
full_text: Reviewing the roster limit As you are probably aware, the NFL CBA allows each team to have 90 players on its offseason roster, but it also makes provisions for a 91st player who joins the team via the International Player Pathway (IPP) program. For the last several years, the Commanders have made use of this IPP exemption, as they have again this season, so Washington’s offseason roster limit is once again 91 players. Washington’s 91st player via the IPP is currently edge rusher TJ Maguranyanga , who spent the 2025 season with the Commanders as well. Incredible level or roster change since the beginning of training camp I’m not sure how obvious it’s been to casual observers, but in the 15 days that have passed since players took the field for the first day of training camp, the Commanders have announced 22 roster transactions! There is at least one more to come when the team announces Laremy Tunsil ’s revised status by the end of the month (he may not go onto IR until the initial cutdown to 53 players for ‘technical’ reasons). I have grouped the transactions by type rather than chronological order for ease and digestibility: Retired (3) LB Nick Bellore CB Ahkello Witherspoon DT DJ Davidson Released/waived (8) Edge Andre Carter TE Anthony Firsker CB Tre Hawkins OG Tyler Cooper OG Tim McKay OG Sala Aumavae-Laulu WR Chris Hilton Jr S Robert McDaniel Signed (10) WR Stefon Diggs WR River Cracraft OT Nicholas Petit-Frere P Matt Haack OL Max Scharping OL Trey Hill OL Daniel Brunskill ILB Curtis Jacobs DT Byron Cowart CB Fabian Moreau You will notice, perhaps, that there have been 11 departures but only 10 new players signed. This is because, on the first day of camp, I had already listed Rasul Douglas on the depth chart — listing 92 players at that time — without a corresponding move. Nick Bellore ’s retirement, announced at the start of camp, was that corresponding move. Accounting for Laremy Tunsil Conversely, while today’s chart lists 91 players, we know already that one of those players, LT Laremy Tunsil , will not be on the active roster in Week 1. Timing counts for a lot with players who suffer major injuries in training camp. Here’s a quick explanation of the considerations under the relevant NFL rules: 1. The Pre-Cutdown Rule (Season-Ending) If the Commanders place Tunsil on IR during training camp before the final 53-man roster reduction deadline on August 30, 2026, he is automatically ruled out for the entire season . He would not be allowed to practice or play for Washington at any point during the year. If doctors determine, post-surgery, that Tunsil will not be able to return to play prior to mid-February, then the Commanders might choose to exercise this option. 2. The Cutdown Day Exception (Designated to Return) NFL rules allow teams: a. to designate, on cutdown day, up to two injured players to return from IR during the season b. alternatively, the team can carry him onto the initial 53-man roster and move him to IR the following day (Option A is almost certainly the one that the Commanders would choose in Tunsil’s case) This approach allows Tunsil to keep his season alive since it leaves the door open for him to return after sitting out a minimum of four games (obviously, in Tunsil’s case, it would be closer to 4 months than 4 games). If doctors determine, post-surgery, that Tunsil’s return to play could happen prior to mid-February, then the Commanders might choose this option to keep all possibilities on the table for their left tackle. The only cost to the team is the opportunity to carry one more player on the training camp roster for two weeks. Not your typical depth chart The chart below is only a depth chart insofar as it assigns players to positions and stacks them in an order. The primary purpose of the chart is to keep track of the 91 guys that currently comprise the training camp roster, not to predict gameday alignments. You will note, for example, that I have 12 offensive position stacks and 13 defensive position stacks on the chart, despite the fact that a team can only field 11 players at one time. You will also note that each player’s name appears only once regardless of the fact that he may play in multiple alignments or positions ( e.g., an interior offensive lineman who can play center and both guard spots will appear at only one of those positions, not all of them ). Again, this is by design since the goal is to provide handy visual reference of the 91 individual players while also offering an overall snapshot of team strength and depth. The bias, though, is to provide a visual list of the full roster, not so much to create a game-ready depth chart. Finally, you will also note that, where players are capable of playing more than one position (and likely to do so on game days), my decision on where to align them may be very different from your idea of where they belong. A few changes since the previous iteration of the preseason 91-man depth chart Position consolidation At s ome position groups where players frequently change alignments, I have consolidated the chart somewhat. With the offensive line, for the most part, starters align in the same position nearly all the time, barring injury, though backup offensive linemen tend to cover at least two different positions. For the OL, I have not consolidated the chart. Here are my notes on recent consolidation of certain other position groups: Inside linebacker It’s unclear how many ILBs will be on the field at the same time from down to down. Traditionally, in a 3-4 defense, there would be two, but Daronte Jones could opt for just one in certain 3-safety alignments, or three in 4-3 alignments or when using one of them as a ‘walk up’ LB as part of a simulated or actual pass rush. I have one group for ILB displayed graphically in 3 stacks. Defensive line Similary, DL personnel packages and alignments are expected to be fluid in Daronte Jones’ scheme. Daron Payne , for example, could line up as a 3-tech on 1st down, nose tackle on 2nd down, and 5-tech on 3rd down. Like the ILBs, I have one group for the DL, displayed graphically in 3 stacks. Slot/Z receiver The Commanders are blessed with a lot of players — Stefon Diggs , Luke McCaffrey , Jaylin Lane , Antonio Williams — who have the ability to play either in the slot or as the ‘z’ receiver (or even ‘x’ when Terry McLaurin is off the field). Here is the alignment by offensive snap count for these receivers in 2024 and/or 2025 (as indicated in chart): Rather than dividing the group into slot vs ‘z’ on the chart, I have grouped 8 receivers into two stacks on the right side of the offensive chart. Running back With Bill Croskey-Merritt ’s offseason work as a pass catcher and the proven ability of Rachaad White , Jeremy McNichols and Jerome Ford to run inside and/or outside zone in addition to being capable-to-outstanding receivers out of the backfield, I have eliminated the 3rd-down back distinction and presented the team’s 6 RBs graphically in 2 stacks. Other notes on players of interest: Cornerback With the retirement of Ahkello Witherspoon and reports that Trey Amos is expected to be healthy enough to play Week 1, I have moved Mikey Sainristil from backup slot corner to wide corner in the stack with Rasul Douglas . This simply reflects my belief that his primary competition is now with Douglas rather than with Amik Robertson . I expect the rest of training camp and preseason to have a big impact on which players we see in which roles in the defensive secondary during the September regular season games. Safety Recent camp reports taken in the context of comments by Dan Quinn have led me to list Jeremy Reaves ahead of Will Harris for one of the safety positions. This simply reflects the appearance, based on camp reports, that Reaves is winning whatever competition is taking place; I’m confident that both players will make the 53-man roster and that both will get snaps in regular season games (though Wednesday’s joint practice…

title: 2026 NFL preseason Week 1: Game takeaways, analysis
summary: The NFL preseason is underway! How did rookies and players in new places perform in their debuts?
full_text:
The first week of the  2026 NFL preseason kicked off Thursday, giving us our first look at rookies and players making debuts with new teams. It continued with three games Friday.

 How did players in new uniforms perform? Who stood out? Which first-year players showed promise?

 Our NFL Nation reporters picked out what you need to know about top debuts and more as the NFL returns.

 
 Quick links: 
 Full schedule | Where to watch 
 Depth charts  | Sign up to play fantasy 

 
 

 Friday's games 
 Buccaneers 24, Jets 16 

 

 Buccaneers: As he has done throughout camp, undrafted free agent rookie cornerback Ayden Garnes made the most of his moment, picking off Bailey Zappe 's pass and returning it 47 yards for a touchdown. Second-round draft pick Josiah Trotter recorded two tackles. Outside linebacker David Walker , a 2025 fourth-round draft pick who missed all preseason last year because of a torn ACL, registered two quarterback pressures.

 Third-round pick Ted Hurst III hauled in two catches despite poor quarterback play from Connor Bazelak ;  Jalon Daniels showed far better command of the offense. Tight end Bauer Sharp went 4-of-5 on targets, and wide receiver Dean Patterson  went 5-of-7.

 First-round pick Rueben Bain Jr. will make his debut next week. -- Jenna Laine 

 Next game: vs. Kansas City Chiefs (Aug. 22, 7:30 p.m. ET, ESPN)

 

 Jets: Fourth-round QB Cade Klubnik was the surprise starter after Geno Smith (ankle) was ruled out as a precaution. Klubnik strengthened his case for the No. 2 job, leading the starting offense to a field goal and touchdown in his only two series -- a curiously short outing. Coach Aaron Glenn arguably should have let the former Clemson star play the entire half. Facing the Bucs' backups, Klubnik (5-for-7, 56 yards) didn't make any big mistakes and kept the chains moving, hitting Garrett Wilson for two third-down conversions.

 It was a nondescript debut for edge rusher David Bailey , the No. 2 pick. Playing with the starters, he registered one tackle and one QB pressure in eight snaps, getting double-teamed on three of his six pass rushes.

 First-round wide receiver  Omar Cooper Jr . got into the open field for a 26-yard reception while playing with the backups. He was leapfrogged on the depth chart by Isaiah Williams . It was a quiet night for the veteran newcomers, most of whom received limited action. -- Rich Cimini 

 Next game: at Pittsburgh Steelers (Aug. 21, 7 p.m. ET, NFL Network)

 Broncos 27, Falcons 7 

 

 Broncos:  On a team that returns 20 of 22 starters from the AFC Championship Game, there are not a lot of roster spots in play, but in Denver's win over the Atlanta Falcons , rookie fourth-round RB Jonah Coleman showed off his decisive running style with 24 yards on four carries. He also displayed the physicality the Broncos wanted to see while playing with the starters in the first half.

 Undrafted rookie wide receiver Cameron Ross , who has flashed athleticism in camp, had a 24-yard carry in the first half when the first- and second-team offense was on the field, a sign that he has already gotten the coaches' attention. Undrafted cornerback Sam Fresch prevented what would have been a Falcons touchdown when he knocked away a pass by  Jack Strand  with 1:54 to play in the game. -- Jeff Legwold 

 Next game: vs. Green Bay Packers (Aug. 21, 9 p.m. ET, ESPN)

 

 Falcons: All eyes were on quarterback  Tua Tagovailoa in his first start of any kind with the Atlanta Falcons . It was not an auspicious beginning.

 Tagovailoa looked uncomfortable and didn't get much help from his offensive line. He completed 3 of 5 passes for 22 yards. All four targets went to tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. , a result fantasy football enthusiasts might find interesting.

 It didn't get much better for the Falcons once Tagovailoa left the game. Veteran quarterback Cooper Rush , a recent signee, was 7-of-19 for 62 yards and two interceptions, including a 96-yard pick-six by Jahdae Barron . -- Marc Raimondi 

 Next game: at  Indianapolis Colts (Aug. 22, 1 p.m. ET)

 Commanders 20, Dolphins 7 

 

 Commanders: Linebacker Sonny Styles played in the first series, a 14-play Miami touchdown drive. Styles wasn't much of a factor, though he wore the green dot and called the plays. He finished with three tackles but looked like a rookie playing his first game, still getting comfortable.

 A few rookies had strong games. Undrafted free agent running back Robert Henry Jr . showed juice on his runs and scored from 22 yards out. He finished with 75 yards on 12 runs. Henry hit the holes fast and used good vision to knife through narrow openings. Center Matt Gulbin showed some power inside in the second quarter. Third-round receiver Antonio Williams caught one pass for 16 yards and didn't play until the third quarter. Running back Kaytron Allen doesn't have Henry's burst but managed 85 yards on 23 carries and a 1-yard touchdown. -- John Keim 

 Next game: at Detroit Lions (Aug. 22, noon ET)

 

 Dolphins:  Wide receiver Caleb Douglas shot up the depth chart during the Dolphins' first two weeks of training camp and showed why in his only snaps of the game. On third-and-5, quarterback Malik Willis hit Douglas on a slot fade. The rookie shook off defensive pass interference, tipped the ball to himself with one hand and corralled it in for a 28-yard reception.

 Second-round rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez finished with a tackle and a pressure in 13 snaps, and defensive end Max Llewellyn recorded half a sack.

 Willis, who signed a three-year deal with the Dolphins this offseason, was sharp in his lone series of the game -- a 14-play, 93-yard touchdown drive that spanned more than seven minutes. He completed 4 of 5 passes for 43 yards, adding 9 more yards on the ground. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques 

 Next game: vs. New York Giants (Aug. 22, 4 p.m. ET, ESPN)

 

 Thursday's games 

 Cardinals 27, Raiders 14 
 

 Cardinals:  No. 3 draft pick  Jeremiyah Love showcased his quick feet and power running during his time on the field Thursday night. It resulted in 11 carries for 58 yards, an average of 5.3 yards per carry. He showcased his ability to find holes and the strength to take on hits. He also had three catches for 14 yards with a long of 7 yards.

 Second-round pick Chase Bisontis left the game in the third quarter with a knee injury and did not return. He went down holding the back of his left knee and was rolling in agony as he was attended to by trainers.

 Wide receiver Reggie Virgil , Arizona's fifth-round pick, made an impressive one-handed catch for a 24-yard gain.  -- Josh Weinfuss 

 Next game: vs.  Dallas Cowboys  (Aug. 22, 10 p.m. ET, NFL Network)

 

 Raiders:   The Raiders' quarterback battle between Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza was on full display. Cousins played only the opening drive, which resulted in a touchdown. After he completed a 10-yard pass to Jack Bech and a 16-yard pass to Tre Tucker , he found tight end Michael Mayer for a 13-yard touchdown, which capped off a 10-play, 68-yard drive to begin the game. Cousins completed 5 of 6 passes for 50 yards.

 As for the No. 1 pick, Mendoza, he showed off his resilience, a trait admired by the coaching staff. His first drive wasn't great -- he had two incompletions and the Raiders were forced to punt. His second was a different story. He completed a 19-yard pass to rookie wide receiver Malik Benson , fitting the ball through a tight window. Rookie running back Mike Washington Jr . then rushed for 53 yards before Mendoza zipped the ball over the middle to Bech for a 6-yard touchdown pass on third down.

 His third drive resulted in a three-and-out. But his fourth and final drive of the evening ended with him putting the Raiders into field goal range. He finished the night completing 10 of 16 passes for 97 yards. Mendoza did struggle against pressure. He was pressured on 38.9% of dropbacks, going 2-for-6 with 11 yards and a 42.4 passer rating. He was sacked once.  -- Ryan…

title: 2026 NFL training camp awards: Best position battles, more
summary: As training camps wind down and preseason picks up, we handed out awards to some players, teams and position battles that have stood out the most.
full_text:
NFL training camps are well underway across 32 teams as we transition to preseason games . And if training camp is school for NFL teams before the 18-week-long exam of the regular season, then we can't leave school without giving out some yearbook superlatives.

 Superlatives are, of course, rampant at this time of year, as training camp is a time to be superlative in our estimation of players and teams. Everyone is deserving of all the awards; every team will win every division. For these superlatives, I went after the true cream of the rising crop: the optimistic Bengals ... the ever-dramatic Browns ... and of course, the Branson Taylor - Kayode Awosika battle in Chargers camp.

 I have 10 fun awards and recognitions to hand out. From "most likely to succeed" to "best shape of his life," these are the players and teams that have made an impression on me over the early days of 2026 training camp.

 

 Jump to: 
 Most likely to break your heart 
 Best vibes  | Biggest position battle 
 Most cursed camp battle   
 Most likely to succeed with new offense 
 Most likely to succeed with new defense 
 Best shape of his life 
 Day 3 rookie everyone fell for 
 Busiest medical tent  |  Preseason MVP 

 

 

 Most likely to break your heart: Aaron Donald and the Los Angeles Rams 
 Do I want to be the guy betting against the three-time Defensive Player of the Year and single best defensive player of my (and perhaps any) generation of football? No. But someone has to be the stick in the mud here.

 Training camp inevitably generates towering expectations, and the Rams are perfectly primed to stand atop the preseason mountain. Offseason trades for edge Myles Garrett and cornerback Trent McDuffie added star power to a defense punching above its weight in 2025. Sprinkle a little Donald on there, and we have what ...? The best defense in football? The best defense of the past decade?

 Maybe -- but probably not!

 First things first: Donald is not yet a Ram , and when he becomes a Ram, it is extremely unlikely he starts out playing 40 snaps per game. He is 35 years old. In the past five seasons, only Cameron Heyward and Calais Campbell have played at least 40 snaps per game as 35-plus-year-old defensive tackles. Widen it to 30 snaps per game, and you catch a John Jenkins year in 2024. Those guys were already at NFL-level conditioning, and it's going to take Donald (as unbelievably talented as he is) time to get there.

 When Donald joins Garrett and McDuffie in the Rams' astronomical effort to improve their defense, he will do his part elevating them from ... fourth in DVOA. The Rams were fifth in defensive success rate and sixth in defensive EPA per drive. This was a good defense last season. I admire the Rams' acknowledgement that it lacked star power -- a fact that did show up in the postseason -- and general manager Les Snead's willingness to take big swings to add blue-chip players to that side of the ball. But it's inaccurate to represent the Rams as a team that missed out on the Super Bowl because it lacked an elite defense. Los Angeles missed out because the Seahawks were very good  and it lost in the brutally thin margins of professional football.

 The new additions will give the Rams an edge in the postseason, where elite, field-tipping players really show up in the game-planning process. But the Rams still have to get there, which means quarterback  Matthew Stafford needs to stay healthy all season. It means the retirement of offensive tackle Rob Havenstein and potential suspension of Alaric Jackson can't hurt the pass protection too much. It means 33-year-old  Davante Adams and the physical Puka Nacua , who could face disciplinary action because of the lawsuit filed against him in March , must stay on the field, as well.

 

 The NFL is not a run-it-back league. Injuries have too big of an impact in a 17-game season. Schematic changes force too much evolution year over year. And in the case of a defensive tackle returning from a four-year retirement, it simply is unreasonable to "run it back" on his impact. Donald is going to be a rotational player on a great defense, and if he makes just one game-changing play in the postseason, the juice will be worth the squeeze. But the Rams have to get to playoff football first, and he needs to get in a uniform to boot.

 

 The Rams are rightfully a huge preseason favorite, but as Bill Barnwell's column this week reminds us, their 1-in-8 chance to win the Super Bowl looks bigger now than it is in reality. Don't let the Reunion Rams break your heart with inflated summer expectations.

 
 

 Best vibes: Baltimore Ravens 
 Here's the quick summary:

 
 Nnamdi Madubuike is back practicing after a neck injury threatened his career last season. 
 No. 1 receiver  Zay Flowers got a fat extension worth $34 million per year. 
 According to ESPN Ravens reporter Jamison Hensley, rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane is having a training camp unlike any rookie he has seen in 27 years of covering the Ravens. 
 Tyler Loop , who ended the Ravens' season with a missed kick against the Steelers, apparently can't miss this summer. 
 New head coach Jesse Minter and defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver have the defense humming -- but QB Lamar Jackson and the rest of the Ravens' key offensive players  are also gushing about new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle. 
 Calais Campbell  is back , which is heartwarming. 
 
 

 Even the first big threat to the immaculate vibes -- a left leg injury scare for top cornerback  Nate Wiggins , who was carted off the field earlier this week -- ended OK, as sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport that testing revealed no structural damage. Training camp vibes have absolutely zero correlation with regular-season wins, of course. But it's better than having terrible vibes!

 
 

 Biggest training camp battle: Los Angeles Chargers left guard 
 Can you name the five players who are competing for starting left guard in the Chargers' offense? (If you can, seek help!)

 They are as follows: rookie Jake Slaughter (a college center), 2022 first-round tackle Trevor Penning (acquired from the Saints last year), second-year pro  Branson Taylor  (a practice squad player for much of last season), veteran  Kayode Awosika  and veteran Trey Pipkins III . On Aug. 4, head coach Jim Harbaugh said he'd like to name a starter after the next 10 practices. That was six practices ago. To this point, no player has taken a lion's share of the snaps.

 

 Most teams are playing their first preseason game this week; there are plenty of other training camp battles underway across the league and there's plenty of time to declare a winner here. But any competition of five players indicates that there has been a lack of emergence -- that the staff is still fishing for someone to declare himself a cut above the rest.

 This is a particularly big issue for the Chargers' interior offensive line, which has been notoriously poor in the Justin Herbert era. Last season, after star offensive tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater  went down with injuries, the Chargers' offense became untenable. Herbert was hit 12.9 times per game last season, a preposterously high number usually reserved for true dual-threat quarterbacks, not occasional capable scramblers such as Herbert. New offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel brings a quick-pass offense that should alleviate some of the concerns. But scheme can do only so much to hide a liability at guard on third-and-8.

 It's worth remarking that, while having Alt and Slater back will certainly help, the Chargers' other two interior positions will also feature new players. Former Patriots first-rounder  Cole Strange  follows McDaniel from Miami to start at right guard, and Tyler Biadasz (released by the Commanders this offseason) is the veteran at center. Both are improvements from 2025 but still are average starters. The interior will already be the part of the Chargers' line that opposing defenses attack, and…

title: Confident Caleb Wlliams has Bears flying high
summary: Williams is starting to show the grasp and confidence Johnson believes will help the Bears take the next step.
full_text:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- If the goal of Tuesday's lengthy, humid practice was to "create evidence" for Ben Johnson and his coaching staff to know where the Bears stand at the halfway point of training camp, Caleb Williams gave his head coach exactly what he was looking for.

 Towards the end of the near two-hour session, Williams and the offense began the final move-the-ball period backed up at their own 1-yard line. Like majority of practice, this exercise was completely off-script, with the objective for Williams' unit to convert two first downs to win the drill.

 One play after Dillon Thieneman blitzed off the edge and nearly ran Williams out of the back of the end zone, the quarterback slipped through a gap as he felt pressure to his right and fired off pass to Rome Odunze , who scampered 58 yards down field on a catch-and-run.

 Moments later, Willams briefly lost Scotty Miller -- "that's what happens when you're on the shorter end," Williams quipped -- before he caught a glimpse of the veteran wide receiver streaking open on a crossing route and ripped the ball for another big gain to win the drill.

 It was an exclamation point on the type of practice Williams said the Bears needed; one that helps build callouses for an offense looking to continue its late-game dominance from a year ago when it became the first team in NFL history to pull off a total of seven fourth-quarter comebacks.

 "He's taken complete control of what we're trying to do, and so we're on the right track," Johnson said. Williams' search for consistency through the Bears' first 11 practices has been a focal point of camp. The quarterback who had to curtail the urge to text his head coach throughout the offseason as he eagerly awaited the start of their second year together was red hot during the opening stretch of camp.

 His operation from the huddle to the snap was crisp. His connections with Odunze, Colston Loveland , Luther Burden III and Kalif Raymond showed what this offense is capable of at full strength. Just about every practice featured a "wow!" moment from Williams, who showed up to camp down 10-15 pounds and with sky-high confidence.

 Then came the lull, to which Johnson shouldered some responsibility. It wasn't as if the issues that routinely plagued Williams last training camp were resurfacing. Unlike a year ago, the quarterback hardly felt like he was drowning. Having his head above water meant surviving an intense installation period designed to see how much the quarterback can handle.

 

 "Those first four practices I thought were really, really good, and then as the volume has continued to go up -- and it's my fault as much as anything, just because I think I've put in more this year on offense than I did a year ago by design," Johnson said. "I want it to feel like a lot right now -- that there's been a level of plateau up to this point. Now that things will slow down from an installation point, I think we're going to see him continue to go on the upswing."

 By every account, Tuesday's practice snapped that lull. Even in the areas where Williams still seeks improvement, like with his accuracy, the quarterback's growth is tangible in different areas. While the Bears built themselves into the kings of the fourth quarter, the offense's ability to score before halftime was an issue in 2025. Most practices end with the team repping crunch-time moments with situations that force the offense into hurry-up mode and the two-minute drill.

 On Aug. 8, Williams delivered one of those wow moments during an end-of-half situation. With the offense facing a third-and-10 with 12 seconds until halftime, Williams bought time when dropping back before throwing a 17-yard laser to Odunze, who high-pointed the ball between two defenders in the back of the end zone for a touchdown.

 Mastering moments like these allows Williams to fulfill Johnson's objective of throwing as much as he can at the quarterback in film and walkthrough sessions to see what he can retain and execute at full speed on the practice field.

 "One, it takes reps," Williams said. "That's always important. I think, two, it takes a bit of failure, it takes a bit of maybe plateauing and going up and down. Taking one step up, one step down and kind of being at the same level trying to figure things out so that when you get to the season, now you're rolling. When you get to the season, the confidence is there.

 "When you get to the season, it's everything is coming together and like I said, that's the point of this moment, this time, being able to go out there and fail. Go out there and come back to the film room and correct it and go out there the next day in walkthrough or whatever it is and get out there and correct it and get it right so that Coach has the proper confidence in myself but also the team to be able to go out there on game days."

 But nothing carries a bigger endorsement for where Williams is at this point of training camp than how Johnson sees an extension of himself on the field. Rather than coaches leading the charge in afternoon walk-throughs from practice hours before, players, particularly Williams, are now focusing on where corrections need to be made.

 "He certainly is leading that charge," Johnson said. "He knows when it's not good enough; he's huddling us back up and let's get it right.

 "I felt that in practice [the other day] too. You guys might've noticed it; we broke the huddle and things weren't quite right and he's regrouping us. So, I think that's a huge step in the right direction. I know those guys really value what he has to say. They're getting extra reps when the horn is done for the day and continuing to working on hooking up in the passing game with all the pass catchers, and that's only going to pay dividends down the road."

title: 2026 Dallas Cowboys training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Cowboys training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Cowboys reporter Todd Archer has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at the Cowboys' camp. Will Dallas turn around the NFL's worst defense from 2025? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Cowboys' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Cowboys camp 
 
 Sources: Cowboys, Quinnen Williams reach 3-year, $105.9M deal 
 Cowboys' Dak Prescott not shying away from setting lofty goals 
 Jones optimistic about Cowboys, likes 'what we put together' 
 Source: Ex-Cowboys QB Will Grier returns as offensive assistant 
 Quieter offseason has Cowboys focused on the right things 
 

 

 Who is the Cowboys' top performer so far at camp? 

 George Pickens . He has essentially made a big play in every practice as he gets set to play on the $27.3 million franchise tag. Whatever disenchantment some might have expected from Pickens without a long-term deal has not materialized. Coaches have noted his attention in the meeting rooms since the start of training camp.

 He and Dak Prescott have picked up where they left off in 2025 when the receiver had career highs in catches, yards and touchdowns. Does that mean he will surpass those figures again in 2026? Not necessarily, but his performance so far has shown a focused player as the season inches closer.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 Because the Cowboys aren't going to play their starters in the preseason, it's impossible to completely answer anything about the defense. There have been encouraging signs there, but let's look to the offense for what can be answered in the preseason games: Who will back up Prescott?

 Joe Milton III and Sam Howell have alternated as Prescott's backup in practice and both have had good moments and not-so-good ones. The Cowboys believe they have line play and skill players to give both QBs a fair shot to perform in the preseason and not have them running for their lives. Read more below:

 

 Friday, Aug. 14 

 Most of the regulars will not play in Saturday's preseason opener against the Seattle Seahawks , but there is one important position that could start to take shape: backup quarterback.

 Throughout training camp, Joe Milton III and Sam Howell have alternated days as Dak Prescott 's backup as they compete to be the No. 2.

 "It's been a very highly competitive contest," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "I think Joe's talent and ability to throw the football and athleticism jumps off the practice field when you see it. I think Sam's doing a great job of moving the team. But at the end of the day, the preseason games, they're going to play really the entire preseason, and that's where the bulk of the evaluation will be."

 Schottenheimer said there has been a back and forth between the quarterbacks. Milton served as Prescott's backup last year, appearing in four games and completing 15 of 24 passes for 183 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions. Howell signed a one-year deal worth $2.5 million guaranteed in free agency.

 He has started 18 games in his career, including all 18 for the Washington Commanders in 2023.

 Milton said having a full year in the offense has "definitely made a huge difference. Shoot, coming in here last year at this time I probably knew 85% of the playbook, 75% of the playbook. Now it's pretty much everything and picking up all of the small stuff, the new stuff, so it's been great."

 Howell has liked what he has done in training camp.

 "We've both been doing a good job trying to make each other better," he said. "I think that's the main thing, coming out each and every day, trying to get better, trying to make the quarterback room better, trying to push each other."

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 

 Over the years in training camp in Oxnard, the Cowboys have been accustomed to welcoming stars of all kinds to training camp. Magic Johnson stopped by. Denzel Washington, Jamie Foxx and Kevin Costner watched a couple of practices too.

 On Thursday, it was Dustin Hoffman's turn. Owner and general manager Jerry Jones referenced "The Graduate" when asked what his favorite Hoffman movie is. That and Marathon Man, "when they pulled his teeth."

 "He's a great guy. He's really a great guy. And why wouldn't he be?" Jones said. "But we sure enjoyed his interest on us out here."

 Hoffman admitted he did not know anything about football but liked what he saw.

 

 Other observations: 

 
 Dak Prescott struggled some Thursday, completing 11 of 24 passes in team drills. He was intercepted once when Markquese Bell took away a deep ball to the post. He had passes knocked down by Dee Winters , Cobie Durant , Caleb Downs and Shavon Revel Jr . There was even a botched snap on the exchange with Cooper Beebe . 
 Winters has come on lately with noticeable work in the past three practices. He was strong against the run in the joint practice versus the Rams on Tuesday and was able to stay within distance of CeeDee Lamb on an over route to take away Prescott's path for the throw. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 It was not a perfect performance for the Cowboys defense against the Los Angeles Rams Tuesday, but it was a lot better than the work against the Rams in last year's joint practices.

 "It's just showing what we've been building on from the spring up until now," linebacker DeMarvion Overshown said. "It was good to hit a different color jersey. I feel like we've been going at it with our offense. They're one of the best in the league so getting to see what we got against another top offense, it puts stuff in perspective. Just another block that we're building on."

 On the first series of team drills,  Shavon Revel Jr . was able to close on a deep ball from Matthew Stafford to  Puka Nacua  and break up the play. Later, DaRon Bland was able to bat away a fade to Davante Adams .

 The Rams' run game was able to get a couple of good runs, but nothing out of the ordinary.

 "We just looked at it as another opportunity to get better. We know [Stafford] is one of the best in the business, then their receiver corps, the running backs and O-line, so we know it wasn't going to be no just easy come in, handle our work and get back on the bus and not break a sweat," Overshown said. "We got some good work in, but I feel like it was good for them to see what we got on our side of the ball as well. I know it's completely different than when they came to Oxnard last year and damn near had a field day."

 More observations: 

 
 The player of the day without question was linebacker Justin Barron . He intercepted three passes, including one on the final play of the two-minute drive off of  Stetson Bennett IV . Barron also had a few stops in the run game. 
 Fresh off agreeing to a three-year, $105.9 million extension, Quinnen Williams was stout in the middle of the defense. On the first set of team drills against the Rams, Williams stopped the running back cold and flexed his right biceps in celebration. He had a couple of tackles for loss. 
 After a slow start, the Cowboys run game was better in the second portion of drills. Tyler Smith had a block to open up a Javonte Williams run. After a fumble, Jaydon Blue was able to get a positive gain on a wide run. 
 Rams OLB Byron Young gave the Cowboys' pass protection some fits early on, getting to the edge on right tackle Terence Steele , which would have negated a completion to George Pickens . 
 The Rams' biggest completion for the first teamers may have been to tight end Terrance…

title: 2026 Green Bay Packers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Packers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Packers reporter Rob Demovsky has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Packers camp. Will the revamped WR corps help QB Jordan Love and the offense take another step? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Packers' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news out of Packers camp 
 
 Aaron Rodgers wishes game at Lambeau, discusses retirement return 
 Packers QB Love expected to play in first preseason game 
 Micah Parsons: Playing vs. Cowboys in Week 6 'realistic' 
 Packers RT changes last name to Bako-Bewele to honor heritage 
 Packers star TE Tucker Kraft activated off PUP after ACL recovery 
 Packers CEO: Team needs financial bump to stay competitive 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 14 

 Friday's media sessions with the defensive coaches left one thing clear: Keisean Nixon is not guaranteed a starting job.

 
It's an unusual position for a player coming off a Pro Bowl appearance, but based on what was said -- and what wasn't said -- Nixon has not done enough to lock up the starting outside cornerback job he held all of last season.

 
This after Nixon (along with safety Kitan Oladapo ) whiffed on a tackle that turned a short gain into a 25-yard catch-and-run by Germie Bernard and gave up another completion during a 19-play stint in Thursday's preseason opener against the Steelers. Officially, Nixon was credited with one tackle.

 
"We have a corner competition," secondary coach Bobby Babich said when asked what's going on with Nixon.

 
Babich added that every position has competition, but compared with how the coaches talked about Nixon, the praise for rookie Brandon Cisse and veteran free agent addition  Benjamin St-Juste was effusive.

 
Said Babich of second-rounder Cisse, who started at the other cornerback spot opposite Nixon on Thursday: "Habit-wise he's ahead of the game as far as when it comes to rookies. Guy's a film junkie. Wants to be really good."

 
Cisse played 19 snaps, the same number as Nixon, and had three tackles (including one on special teams).

 
St-Juste played 24 snaps with the backups and recorded two tackles.

 
"He showed yesterday that he will really put his body on some guys," cornerbacks coach Daniel Bullocks said of St-Juste. "Been really impressed."

 
The best anyone offered about Nixon was how he has handled the competition.

 
"He's handled it great," Babich said. "He's locked in. Every player is going to have plays they want back."

 Other observations: 

 
 Speaking of competitions, there appears to be a new one brewing on the offensive line. It had been assumed by most that when Aaron Banks (knee) returned to 11-on-11 drills, the left guard job would be his, like it was last year. But while the veteran has been given rest days and limited to individual drills, rookie Jager Burton has played better and better. "I think he's going to make it extremely difficult," coach Matt LaFleur said of the decision at left guard. "I think Jager has done a really good job. I think not only him but [Jacob] Monk ." 
 Lukas Van Ness played only three snaps but had what defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon called two "wins" -- one against the run and one for a sack. "Lukas has been having an excellent camp," Gannon said. "He's a very versatile player, and he can win in a lot of different areas." How well Van Ness and the other edge rushers play until Micah Parsons comes back from his torn left ACL might determine how the Packers fare early in the season. Fellow edge rusher Brenton Cox Jr . also had a sack early in the game. 
 LaFleur said running back Josh Jacobs (groin) could "potentially" return to practice this coming week but added "it wouldn't be until later in the week." 
 The Packers don't practice Saturday but resume open training camp practices Sunday. 
 

 

 Who is the Packers' top performer so far at camp? 

 Not that Xavier McKinney didn't play well last season -- he was second-team All-Pro after all -- but so far this looks more like the version of McKinney from 2024, when he was first-team All-Pro and had a career-best eight interceptions. McKinney looks like the perfect fit in new coordinator Jonathan Gannon's system, moving all over the field and finding himself in the middle of more action. Between McKinney, Evan Williams and Javon Bullard , the Packers could have one of the best safety trios in the league.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 When will the offensive line jell? One underrated thing that ruined last season was inconsistent offensive line play. Given that the starters won't play much in the preseason games, it's worth wondering when that group will finally come together.

 While there has been some shifting of personnel, most notably new left tackle Jordan Morgan , the preferred group of five has yet to get any 11-on-11 snaps together. Left guard Aaron Banks (knee) has been limited to individual drills in practice, and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele has slowly integrated back into practice. There's also competition at guard with Jacob Monk , Anthony Belton and rookie Jager Burton . Monk may have usurped Belton for the right guard spot, while Jager has looked solid at left guard in place of Banks.

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 Three weeks and 11 practices into training camp, and something's missing: fighting.

 
There hasn't even been so much as a scuffle or shoving match.

 
This is training camp No. 7 for veteran safety Xavier McKinney and when asked if this is the deepest into training camp he has ever gone without seeing a fight, McKinney didn't hesitate.

 
"Hell yeah," he said. "For sure."

 
But McKinney doesn't think that's a bad thing. Nor is it a sign that the players are not competitive enough.

 
"I think we're past that, to be honest," McKinney said. "I think we have a bigger goal, and that bigger goal is to get over this hump that we've been kind of dealing with these last couple years. We're not focused on fighting. Nobody's trying to get kicked out of practice. Nobody's trying to have practice stop early. We're just trying to focus on our technique. We're trying to find ways where we can improve as individuals. We want to be the best group that we can possibly be. We want to be better than what we were last year."

 
The Packers also haven't had a joint practice yet. So even McKinney said all bets are off when the Cardinals come to town for a practice Aug. 26.

 
"That always happens," McKinney said.

 Other observations: 

 
 Just when it looked like the injury list would keep getting longer, a few key players returned to practice. Receivers Matthew Golden (toe) and Jayden Reed (ankle) were back after missing two practices. So was tight end Josh Whyle (neck). All took part in team (11-on-11) periods. Cornerback Carrington Valentine , who dropped out of practice Aug. 2 because of a hamstring injury, returned for individual drills only. The only new addition to the DNP list was rookie edge Dani Dennis-Sutton , but it was because of an illness. 
 The Packers had a pair of new defensive backs on the field after signing Trey Dean III and Travion Fluellen . They both worked with the safeties during individual drills. Safety Javon Bullard (foot) remained out. 
 After taking reps with both the second- and third-string defenses Monday, Keisean Nixon was back at his regular left cornerback spot with the No. 1 defense. In fact, he worked exclusively with that group and appeared to be on the field for every snap that the starters took. Brandon Cisse…

title: Rookie Benson earns shot to start at RT for Chiefs
summary: The former starter for national champion Indiana has garnered a lot of praise in camp for his attitude and strength.
full_text:
ST. JOSEPH, Mo. -- If you listen to  Kahlil Benson 's new teammates, especially the  Kansas City Chiefs ' veterans, you can tell just how enthusiastic they are about him -- and his potential for this season.

 "Kahlil has been hungry since day one, eager to learn," right guard Trey Smith said last week. "He works extremely hard and he's a strong man. I think he has a real aspiration, a real want to be great."

 No, Benson is not one of the Chiefs' top draft picks. In fact, Benson wasn't even one of the Chiefs' priority free agents in late April after the NFL draft ended. Instead, Benson joined the team a few days later, earning a contract after participating in the rookie minicamp that consisted of 104 players.

 "You can tell [football] is important to him," center Creed Humphrey said of Benson at the start of training camp. "He shows up every meeting, walk-through, lift with the right mindset."

 A mere three months later, Benson is expected to be a starter Saturday afternoon when the Chiefs play the Los Angeles Rams in their preseason opener. Throughout training camp, the Chiefs have given Benson most of the first-team reps.

 If Benson continues to overachieve in the preseason -- which he has done for the past 105 days -- he has a chance to win the starting right tackle job, supplanting five-year veteran Jaylon Moore , and play a pivotal role in front of quarterback Patrick Mahomes and running back Kenneth Walker III .

 "He's done great," Walker said last week of Benson. "We've got pads on now, and you get to see how well he's doing out there. He's going to have a great impact on this team."

 Benson, 23, has experience playing on a championship team. Last season in college, he was the right tackle for the University of Indiana, protecting quarterback Fernando Mendoza , who led the Hoosiers to an undefeated season and a national championship. Listed at 6-foot-6 and 319 pounds, Benson is the prototypical size -- with arms that are almost 35 inches long -- that often interests NFL scouts.

 But Benson's production last season was mixed. Too often, he struggled against quality speed from edge rushers. His blocking techniques were inconsistent, too. Although he wasn't selected in the draft, Benson was confident he would be able to compete for a roster spot.

 "Honestly, I kept my head down and knew my time was going to come," Benson said after Wednesday's practice. "I really just stayed humbled, stayed faithful and just kept praying to God that I was ready to be on call when it was that time.

 "Whatever position you get put in, you've got to take it on the chin. You just keep going and make sure there's nothing left on the table to be eaten."

 In early May, Benson impressed the Chiefs immediately, both in the classroom and on the field during the rookie minicamp, often having reps across from defensive end R Mason Thomas , the team's second-round pick. Benson made his first jump up the depth chart the next month. He began sharing first-team reps with Moore during mandatory minicamp.

 In wanting to give Benson a proper evaluation, the Chiefs traded Wanya Morris , a three-year veteran, to the Atlanta Falcons .

 "He's done a great job just competing," Mahomes said last week of Benson. "I remember watching [rookie minicamp] film and seeing that guy and seeing him kind of do stuff the right way. And he's just gotten better and better all the way to this point. We still have a long way to go, but I'm happy with the progress so far."

 Earlier this month, Benson showed improvement from one padded practice to the next. He has been most impactful as a run blocker. One example was when, in an 11-on-11 period, Benson executed a double-team block with Smith to move defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga back. The rep finished with Benson also blocking linebacker Nick Bolton , which created more space on the right side of the field for Walker. A few minutes later, Benson blocked defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah in pass protection for Mahomes to connect with receiver Tyquan Thornton for a completion for more than 30 yards.

 Of course, Benson has had his rookie moments. A few practices later, Anudike-Uzomah used a combination of quickness and power to win several one-on-one battles against him.

 "He's done a nice job," coach Andy Reid said last week of Benson. "He's learning. Very strong and powerful, good feet, good athletic ability. He's working at the consistency part, scheme-wise. Physically, he's got all the tools. He'll just keep working at it and we'll see where it goes, but he's got a lot of talent."

 The Chiefs have a history in the past few years of starting rookies on the offensive line in front of Mahomes. In 2021, Humphrey and Smith started as rookies, helping to rebuild Mahomes' pass protection. Left tackle Josh Simmons started last year as a rookie, too, demonstrating he could properly protect Mahomes' blind side.

 Over the past week, Benson has shown that he could at least be the Chiefs' top backup lineman if he loses the battle to Moore. Benson has taken all his reps at right guard since Smith has been out with a hip injury. Those reps have featured Benson trying his best to be an effective blocker against Chris Jones , the Chiefs' best pass rusher, the same veteran who helped prepare Smith ahead of his rookie season. 

 "It's really helpful," Benson said. "Everything's been going good. I see everything as beneficial when it comes to the teammates. They're lifting us up, especially as rookies. You want to do the best that you can, especially just trying to keep the coaches how they're supposed to be. [You] really [take] those coaching points moving forward."

 Against the Rams on Saturday, Benson is expected to play two positions in the first half: right guard with backup quarterback Justin Fields and right tackle with rookie quarterback Garrett Nussmeier . Reid acknowledged this week that Benson having quality snaps at both positions to show his versatility could be a factor in whether he wins the right tackle role over Moore, who is the safer option.

 All that is left for Benson is to showcase against opponents that his sudden rise with the Chiefs is quite legitimate, a rookie ready to continue surprising his teammates.

 "I don't really feel like it's a challenge," Benson said of switching positions. "You've got to be able to adjust when it's time and your number is being called. You just never know what could happen."

 Who is the Rams' top performer so far at camp? 
 CB  Trent McDuffie . The Rams ended last season with a clear weakness in the cornerback room. McDuffie has been a standout during training camp on a roster not lacking star talent.  "Trent's out there doing something every single play," Adams said. "... He's always got the right technique. He's got a great way of reading you out. He understands his position on any given play, whether it's his leverage or situationally a smart player and great technique.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 How does rookie quarterback Ty Simpson look?

 The No. 13 pick hasn't gotten as many reps during training camp as starting quarterback Matthew Stafford or 2023 fourth-round pick  Stetson Bennett IV , but he should get ample snaps during the preseason. Heading into the first preseason game, it appears that Bennett will be the team's backup quarterback going into the season, and Simpson will serve as the third-string quarterback. But if Simpson plays significant snaps -- and it seems he will -- the Rams will get their first extended look at their rookie quarterback to see how he operates coach Sean McVay's offense.

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 

 After the Rams' final practice before the preseason opener against the Kansas City Chiefs on Saturday, coach Sean McVay said 2023 fourth-round pick Stetson Bennett IV will start the game.

 McVay said rookie quarterback Ty Simpson will also play.

 Bennett, who played in the Rams' first two preseason games a year ago, said he feels a difference in his confidence playing in this offense compared to then.

 "Yeah, for sure, Bennett said. "And I think that just comes with being better at your job and having more ownership, knowing the offense more, being closer with the guys."

 Bennett took the majority of the second-team reps on days Matthew Stafford was practicing and the first-team reps when Stafford was not.

 "I did see that," McVay said. "... [Cowboys quarterback] Dak Prescott  does a good job being able to move in the pocket and I think there's some excellent players on the perimeter that we were able to get some really good looks at, but it did feel like those guys were able to make their presence felt."

 McVay said he's not concerned about Garrett missing time, saying the pass rusher told him he feels "about 85 percent" healthy.

 "When he's been out there, he has certainly made his impact felt, but we want to make sure that when he returns to play, he's able to return to full performance and feel like himself," McVay said.

Because head coach Sean McVay does not play his starters or key backups during the preseason, he especially values the chance to get his starters in these competitive, but more controlled environments.

 The Rams don't gameplan for the practice, but McVay said he's looking forward to "the competition" of going against a different team than his players see practicing against each other.

 Monday's practice was a rest day for quarterback Matthew Stafford . He is scheduled to practice against the Cowboys on Tuesday.

"The plays that happened today, there was a handful of turnovers, but I thought it was a really great reflection of excellent execution defensively, some outstanding individual plays. And sometimes that's the price of doing business."

title: Rookie Caleb Douglas atop Dolphins WR depth chart for preseason opener
summary: Miami's thin wide receiver room created an opportunity for Caleb Douglas to make an early impact, which he has done so far.
full_text:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- The first name on the Miami Dolphins ' first depth chart of the year has been one of the most consistent players at the team's training camp this summer -- even though he's yet to log his first NFL snap.

 Rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas was named a starter as the team prepares for its preseason opener Friday against the Washington Commanders . The depth chart is considered unofficial at this point of the season, but is a sign that the third-round pick has exceeded expectations so far.

 

 "It's been (his) consistency over time -- he's been really consistent," Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Wednesday. "He's made some flash plays and then he's made some plays where he needs to catch the ball, but he's probably been one of our most consistent guys. He showed up every day. So that's where he deserves to be at this point."

 The Dolphins took Douglas with the 75th overall pick in this year's draft, making him the 11th receiver taken -- just ahead of fellow training camp standouts Zachariah Branch and  Ja'Kobi Lane . At the time, it was considered a reach considering his college production (2,031 yards, 16 touchdowns in four seasons), struggles with drops and inconsistencies winning contested catches.

 Hafley said the latter was the "number one thing" he wanted to see from Douglas once practices began, but that the rookie has impressed him with his ability to do so.

 Douglas has used his 6-foot-4 frame to create separation from defensive backs and is starting to learn how to make defenders pay for assuming how he'll use his speed (4.39-second 40-yard dash).

 "Really just always knowing that I'm a bigger guy, they're going to always think I'm going vertical," Douglas said. "So me being able to sell my vertical so well and being able to snap it down, I have a lot of ways of going inside, outside, back down the stem."

 

 Over the past two weeks, Douglas has separated himself as quarterback Malik Willis ' most reliable target. Veterans Jalen Tolbert and Malik Washington have more experience, but the rookie's upside is undeniable.

 Despite the occasional drop due to a lack of focus, Willis said Douglas has been efficient with his opportunities so far.

 "I think he's a great player. I wouldn't even say (he's) even a safety valve yet. I'm still trying to figure everybody out," Willis said. "Everybody's trying to figure me out. We're trying to figure this out together ... He's been making nice grabs in the times where he's the option, where he's the read. So I'm excited for him. I think he's doing a great job getting open. I think he's attacking the mental side of it. It's been great."

 Douglas' production carried over into Wednesday's joint practice with the Commanders, for which he drew praise as the brightest spot of an otherwise underwhelming Dolphins offense.

 

 Miami's thin wide receiver room created an opportunity for Douglas to make an early impact and offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik believes he's done so thanks to tireless work on his fundamentals since his arrival -- although there are still a few habits from college that he'll need to clean up before the season begins.

 "He's an immensely talented dude. He's got long arms. He's fast. He's got really good feet," Slowik said. "He's tall. We just need him to continue to grow in his technique and his fundamentals of what receiver play entails at the Miami Dolphins, and he's doing that. Like it flashes. It shows when he does it. And then there's still little things that you can get away with in college for all our young guys that in the NFL you no longer can do.

 "You know, the catch tuck how important that is, how fast that is. In college, you can probably catch, wait on your tuck for a good two seconds with no issues. The way our defense is going at the ball right now, if it's not instantaneous, it might come out. If our footwork isn't clean on our transitions, we're probably getting tackled. If we have clean footwork on our transitions, now we've got a chance to run through some stuff. So it's just little things like that for all our young guys, we got to continue to grow."

 Douglas' starting job is not cemented; he'll have to continue to produce in practice and in the team's three preseason games in order to keep it. But on a Dolphins offense that lacks options in the passing game, Douglas' opportunity is there for the taking.

 Saints defensive end Chase Young estimated he had six sacks in Thursday's joint practice against the Jacksonville Jaguars ' first team. The actual number likely wasn't far off.

The red zone offense is one of the areas in which the Saints could use improvement, as they've often settled for field goals instead of touchdowns after driving down the field during practices this summer.

 

 Friday, Aug. 14 

 The Saints held a walkthrough in the Superdome on Friday afternoon, going through everything from where they'll line up to stretch to a brief run through of what Saturday's game against the Jaguars might look like. The Saints won't be playing most of their starters against Jacksonville, preferring to use Thursday's lengthy practice session instead.

 Coach Kellen Moore didn't say if that would also be the case next week when they hold joint practices against the Cowboys and Rams in California. It was really even more than the full game as far as the intensity [and time spent practicing]."

 QB  Spencer Rattler will start against the Jaguars, and the team will go to Zach Wilson "at some point." Moore also expects to get Hunter Dekkers , who has not gotten a practice rep this summer, into the game.

 Moore said it's to be determined whether WR  Jordyn Tyson , who injured his hamstring, travels with the team to California on Monday. 
 Both kickers will kick in Saturday's game and will rotate back and forth. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 
 The Saints came away from their joint practice against the Jaguars with positivity on both sides of the ball. The offense had one of their best days of camp. Some highlights include a deep touchdown by QB  Tyler Shough , who completed a deep pass to Bryce Lance working against Travis Hunter with pressure in his face. Hunter would have attempted to tackle Lance if it were game situation, but there was no live tackling to the ground in practice.

 Other highlights included a QB  Zach Wilson to Bub Means touchdown; a Shough to Chris Olave touchdown, where Olave kept his toes in bounds for a score; and a Spencer Rattler to Trey Palmer deep touchdown. Shough said he felt his personal highlight occurred during the two-minute drill where he had six straight completions to set Charlie Smyth up for a 53-yard field goal as time ran out. Defensively, Julian Blackmon kicked things off with an interception of Jags' QB  Trevor Lawrence while the defensive line was active and in position for multiple sacks. At the end of the day, Young estimated he was involved in six sacks.

 More observations:  

 
 Jonas Sanker and Hunter Dekkers both got new numbers, with Sanker switching to No. 7 and Dekkers now wearing No. 13. 
 Sanker finished the day on the sideline with what appeared to be a cut above his eye. 
 Jordyn Tyson came down hard after a reception, jogged off and did not return to practice. 
 Charlie Smyth went 5-for-5 and Tanner Brown went 4-for-5 in a kicking session, where Brown's 51-yard attempt clanked off the uprights. Both made long field goals at the end of the two-minute drill 
 Spencer Rattler will start the preseason game against the Jaguars. 
 The final period for the first-team defense against the Jags first-team offense in the two minute situation had two pressures and two sacks. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 The Saints took a step back in anticipation of Thursday's joint practice session against the Jacksonville Jaguars . The Saints will practice against three different teams over the course of camp, and tomorrow's practice will essentially function as their preseason game. The starters won't play in Saturday's game, but they will get extensive time against the Jaguars' first-team tomorrow. The Saints had a short, non-padded inside practice to get ready for that.

 They still ran some 11-on-11 drills with a few highlights -- Isaac Yiadom broke up a Spencer Rattler pass to Bryce Lance , continuing to work through the play until the ball came out. Some teammates rushed over to celebrate the play. In the next team session, Lance caught a touchdown from Rattler in the end zone, making the catch over Jordan Howden and Elliott Davison before spiking the ball in celebration. They'll be back in pads tomorrow against Jacksonville.

 There were multiple bad snaps among all their units, including a high snap from Erik McCoy to Tyler Shough . That comes a day after the offense had several penalties. Moore said the team is a work in progress. "We need to play more consistent football. We have to get there and that's what this time of the year is about," Moore said. 
 The Saints ended practice with red zone work, scoring a touchdown off a handoff to  Travis Etienne Jr . up the middle. Shough's two passes in the four-play session were incomplete, including an attempt to Juwan Johnson on the run with pressure from Chase Young .

title: A Harbaugh team meeting during training camp -- an inside look
summary: What does an everyday Harbaugh team meeting look like? It's filled with personal messages and quirky terms.
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- John Harbaugh was admittedly nervous. He couldn't wait to address the New York Giants for the first time.

 The date was April 7. It had been 77 days since he was hired as their coach. And this was the first time he was allowed by rules to address the entire team.

 "I'm standing up here in front of the New York Giants. The New York Giants ," Harbaugh said while pacing the front of the meeting room at the Quest Diagnostics Training Center. "This is the New York Giants sitting in this room! The New York Giants! Wow! This is an honor."

 It was his first team meeting as coach of the Giants after 18 seasons with the Baltimore Ravens . Harbaugh was genuinely excited to be leading one of the NFL's marquee franchises considering the steep history and legacy. That was a massive part of his decision to take the job over several other options .

 When the team released a snippet of this speech last month to promote the impending "Giants Life: The Offseason" video series, some fans viewed it as old-school and real. They were pumped that this was the new Giants coach and liked the attitude he brought with him from Baltimore. But it was also met with some ridicule and chuckles for its hokeyness.

 Former NFL quarterback Cam Newton was among those especially critical of the speech. Speaking on his "4th&1" podcast, Newton questioned, "How could that be what inspires a group of grown men?" He said the silence was awkward, the message was off. Newton thought Harbaugh should be sharing his vision for the Giants, explaining his core values and mission.

 In reality, he did. Perhaps that just wasn't the ideal one-minute promo to showcase his oratory skills and ability to captivate the room. 

 "It was the opening sentence of a whole meeting," Harbaugh told ESPN last week at training camp in West Virginia. "That was about a 30-minute meeting to kind of just kick things off and get to know each other and just kind of talk about stuff that presents a vision for where we were going. So that was just the opening line. After that, then the message came."

 

 Giants fullback Patrick Ricard , who previously played for Baltimore, defended Harbaugh's speech on Instagram. Tight end Isaiah Likely also thought the public reaction wasn't in line with the room in which it was spoken.

 "I think it was taken way differently," Likely said.

 That specific meeting was flush with introductions. First with the coaches and then the players, who each shared their identity and purpose. Harbaugh believed creating vulnerability would help team-building.

 On a bigger scale, the clip wasn't exactly an accurate depiction of what an everyday Harbaugh team meeting looks like. He specified that there are also different meetings for different times of the year. That was a first meeting ever with a team.

 A Harbaugh team meeting during training camp begins with something he calls "wise words." This is where individual players get up and share a daily message. It's inspiration or advice, and the order for who speaks is selected based on seniority.

 Harbaugh used "wise words" throughout his Ravens tenure. Just not always to start meetings. Often, it was after practices. He also employed something called "spotlight" in Baltimore during which a guy would tell his backstory to the team. 

 Veteran wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr . used "wise words" last Tuesday to say: "Yesterday's touchdown doesn't win you today's game." His point being you can't rest on the laurels of a good practice. You have to bring it again the following day. Beckham had his second straight strong practice that afternoon.

 Likely went with: "Win your 1/11th and be where your feet are," which means take care of your own business first. Don't try to do too much.  

 After the players offer their initial contributions at the team meetings, Harbaugh takes over.

 

 "Then I might have something for the day or I might not, based on whatever's kind of going on," he said. "A lot of times it's a story, like something happens or sometimes it's just whatever. It's whatever I'm kind of feeling. And then right now, this time of year, we go through practice. So I've got about 30-35 plays from the practice that I want to make coaching points on."

 If the previous day's practice was poor, such as last week when the Giants committed 14 penalties in one session, that's when you might get a "hard Harbaugh," according to Likely. Though it's rare to hear Harbaugh yelling over the music or other coaches during practice, he regularly coaches his players hard because he expects greatness every day and doesn't want to see the same mistake again.

 Then Harbaugh will outline the plan for that day's practice.

 "We'll go through situations, whatever the situations are. We try to detail those out," he said. "We teach every situation. We always have some sort of teach-the-game type of a deal, whether it's situations or it's field position or it's turnovers or it's ball security or it's how to get the ball north efficiently. There's always these fundamentals that we'll have something all through training camp."

 The Giants even ended a practice last week by practicing long drives. This is what Harbaugh calls the "opportunity of fatigue." He wants to see who can execute when they're tired and hot, when things are hard. The new coach isn't looking for his players to be perfect in this situation, just better than the guy lined up across from them.

 Harbaugh's messages at the team meetings vary by the day. They can be historical, famous quotes or even something that was texted to him that morning, maybe even by his mom or dad. There will also be a message for that specific practice.

 And Harbaugh has quite the catalog to choose from having been a coach for 40-plus years.

 "I've been doing it for a long time. Even as a special teams coach, I had that stuff," he said. "So I have a lot of messages that I've had and I rewrite them every year."

 Harbaugh has a computer file filled with messages and stories. He updates them to make them current and relevant. He hopes they're better now than they were 10 years ago, knowing it's important to evolve with the times.

 "Sometimes he'll quote family, family history. Or somebody texts him in the morning," Likely said. "He'll probably, if it goes with the message of his speech, he'll put it in a team meeting, let him know, read it out loud, stuff like that."

 Veteran defensive tackle DJ Reader said one day last week that Harbaugh used a message as simple as, "It takes what it takes." Reader liked that. He didn't view it as anything profound but enjoyed that it was simple and to the point. Just get it done was his takeaway.

 

 Harbaugh uses a lot of personal stories. He likes to come clean with his feelings. He believes guys like that best because it's authentic and shows the true, sometimes vulnerable, version of himself.

 "And you can tell he's wired a little bit different. Just in a quirky obsession type of way," Reader said. "He's obsessed with ball and doing things the right way. And you can tell it's him though. He can't shut it off. He's not up there faking it. And that's fun to see."

 Harbaugh seems to be a lot more like his brother, Jim, head coach of the Los Angeles Chargers , than most realize. Jim is known for his khaki pants and other quirks. John seems to suppress them more. 

 In the meetings, the Giants get the real John Harbaugh. An offbeat unifier who has proved his approach can lead to winning games with his previous team. If it works, why change it?

 "He's all about having everyone on the same page, building a vision of what he sees the football team and how we all should be thinking," Ricard said of his years with Harbaugh. "So every day he'll give us a message and he'll give it to us either by quotes, stories, maybe even historical, and he'll try to relate it back to football and back to us as a team. And he just tries to have a vision. And then as the season goes…
