full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Seattle Seahawks ' camp is taking place in Renton, Washington, and Seahawks reporter Brady Henderson has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Seahawks camp. What is new with the defending Super Bowl champions? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Thursday.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Seahawks camp 
 
 WR Tory Horton healthy after cracking tibia last season 
 Seattle Pro Bowl DL Williams confirms deal talks 
 Seattle's Nick Emmanwori has ankle surgery, expected to play W1 
 Who are the Khoslas? Meet the family set to buy the Seahawks 
 
 

 Who has been the Seahawks' top performer so far at camp? 
 The offense in general has been impressive considering the transition to new coordinator Brian Fleury and the fact that it faces the league's best scoring defense from 2025 every day in practice. In terms of individuals, we'll give the nod to Jaxon Smith-Njigba . The league's leading receiver from last season and the reigning AP Offensive Player of the Year has remained an almost-unstoppable force. Rashid Shaheed is the deep threat in Seattle's offense, but QB  Sam Darnold has connected with JSN on several down-field shots this summer.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Who will win the third cornerback job? After letting Riq Woolen leave in free agency, the Seahawks have Noah Igbinoghene and Nehemiah Pritchett competing to replace him. Coach Mike Macdonald demands physicality from his corners, so preseason games (and Seattle's joint practice next week against the Titans) could be the differentiator in this battle. Regardless of who emerges, the position looks like a question mark, which is why Seattle is looking into free agent corner Terrion Arnold , who was released by the Lions in June after being was arrested on felony charges of armed robbery and kidnapping.

 
 

 Friday, Aug. 14 
 After 15 practices and three walk-throughs over the first three weeks of training camp, the Seahawks are set to open the preseason Saturday night against the Dallas Cowboys at Lumen Field.

 "Our players have earned the right ... to go let it rip and trust your training and go have fun," coach Mike Macdonald said Friday. "Go play football [like] they know how and our brand of ball, and hopefully it comes to life, and hopefully we have some cost-of-doing-business celebration penalties."

 Macdonald said many of the team's established starters will not play. That includes Sam Darnold , whose only preseason action last summer was 10 snaps in the second game. Drew Lock will start against Dallas and Jalen Milroe will play next, and in a change from a year ago, Macdonald said the plan is for the quarterbacks to continue to rotate "to some degree."

 Rookie running back Jadarian Price will not play as the team's first-round pick continues to work his way back from what Macdonald has described as "lower-body soreness" that should not keep him out for long. Price has taken part in both walk-throughs this week but missed the past five actual practices. Macdonald said Friday that Price is "on the mend."

 George Holani , who has shared first-team reps with Price, "should see some action" against the Cowboys. He's one of only four healthy tailbacks the Seahawks have available with Price, Emanuel Wilson and Jacardia Wright banged up and Zach Charbonnet still on the physically unable to perform list.

 Macdonald said Wilson is working through an undisclosed injury and "should be back at some point." He used similar wording on outside linebacker Derick Hall , saying he shouldn't be out long term.

 The Seahawks put fullback Robbie Ouzts on injured reserve earlier this week because of a neck injury that will end his season. It does not sound career-ending, based on how Macdonald described it.

 "It's an unfortunate situation," Macdonald said. "It's just someone you're really rooting for. But to our knowledge, there is a recovery process, and this should help his career long term. This is why we're doing it."

 

 
 Thursday, Aug. 13 
 Seahawks quarterback Jalen Milroe has had a hand in the team's expected addition of Terrion Arnold , having vouched for his college teammate and close friend while Seattle was vetting the free agent cornerback amid his ongoing legal case.

 Milroe is also hoping to help the Seahawks on the field in Year 2 after an underwhelming rookie season. Seattle drafted him in the third round with the plan to utilize his athleticism in specialty packages, but it was shelved after a rough, fumble-filled start.

 Given the difficulty of making three quarterbacks active on game days, Milroe might again have a hard time getting snaps in 2026 as Seattle's QB3. He doesn't appear ready to overtake Drew Lock for the No. 2 job behind Sam Darnold  but has nonetheless looked much more functional than he did a year ago.

 "He's looked really good," said tight end AJ Barner , who had a long reception on an over-the-middle Milroe throw Thursday. "He's throwing the ball very confident, and I think that's the biggest thing. Ask any player out here. You want to make confident decisions and then go let it rip, and I think J-Mil has really taken a stride this camp."

 As Barner noted, Milroe has a quick release and throws with plenty of zip. His accuracy appears to have improved on shorter and intermediate throws. Still, plays tend to die with him holding onto the ball in the pocket more often than with Seattle's other quarterbacks. He doesn't take off and run as much as he could, as if he's being coached to not rely too much on his legs.

 But they still pose a clear threat.

 "I can just feel him get more comfortable in the pocket," Barner said. "He's standing in there, he's making decisions. When he wants to use his athleticism, he's going to go ahead and do that."

 If the number of reps Milroe got Thursday were any indication, it looks as if he's in line to play extensively Saturday when the Seahawks open the preseason against the Dallas Cowboys .

 "Another guy on Saturday that I'm stoked for him to just go out there and show what he's got," Barner said.

 Other observations: 

 
 RB Jadarian Price was out again Thursday. The Seahawks' top pick took part in Wednesday's walk-through but has missed the past five actual practices. Coach Mike Macdonald has described it as a minor issue -- calling it lower body soreness -- and has said Price should be back soon. 
 S Nick Emmanwori still is not practicing after being activated off the physically unable to perform list earlier this week. 
 Also not practicing Thursday were OLB Derick Hall and CB Julian Neal . 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 There was nothing noteworthy to come from the Seahawks' 16th practice of training camp, with players wearing shorts and T-shirts during a 55-minute walk-through. But there was a development with  Terrion Arnold . 
 
After working out for the Seahawks on Sunday, then visiting the New Orleans Saints on Tuesday, the third-year cornerback continued his free agent tour by meeting with the New York Giants  on Wednesday. If the Seahawks are going to truly pursue Arnold, who is facing eight felony charges in Florida in connection with a kidnapping and robbery in early February, then it sounds like they'll have competition. 
 
Coach Mike Macdonald's comments on Arnold earlier this week made it clear that Seattle's interest is much more than simply the team's usual due diligence. That was reinforced on the second episode…

title: HC Mike Macdonald: 'Overwhelmingly positive' reviews helped with Terrion Arnold decision
summary: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said one factor in the team's decision to offer Terrion Arnold a contract despite the felony charges he's facing was the "overwhelmingly positive" reviews they heard while vetting the free agent cornerback.
